scope: Indonesia-first with Phase 2 ASEAN job discovery

jobs.title: Hub Lead
jobs.description:
hub lead bertanggung jawab memantau dan memastikan pengiriman barang berjalan tepat waktu dari penjemputan hingga penerimaan oleh pelanggan di area kab. sleman, di yogyakarta. posisi ini mengoordinasikan aktivitas dengan tim gudang, line haul, dan pihak 3pl, memitigasi risiko kehilangan atau kerusakan paket, mengontrol seluruh transaksi di hub, mengawasi alur inbound dan outbound, serta melatih dan meningkatkan performa staf operasional hub.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk, diploma, atau sarjana (s1) dari segala jurusan. memiliki pengalaman kerja minimal 3 tahun sebagai supervisor atau koordinator di bidang logistik, rantai pasok (supply chain), atau sektor terkait. memiliki rekam jejak kerja di operasional last mile atau first mile. menguasai alur perencanaan, pengiriman, dan manajemen pergudangan secara menyeluruh. terampil mengoperasikan microsoft excel.

jobs.title: Hub Lead
jobs.description:
posisi hub lead di spx express bertanggung jawab untuk memantau dan memastikan pengiriman barang tepat waktu mulai dari pengambilan hingga pengantaran ke pelanggan. tugas utama mencakup koordinasi dengan tim gudang, line haul, dan 3pl terkait pengiriman barang, menjaga keamanan pengiriman untuk menekan risiko paket hilang atau rusak, memantau seluruh aktivitas transaksi di hub, mengawasi proses inbound dan outbound, serta melakukan pelatihan dan pengembangan kinerja staf di lokasi hub penempatan kab. trenggalek, jawa timur.

kandidat memiliki ijazah sma/smk, diploma (d3), atau gelar sarjana (s1) dari semua jurusan. memiliki pengalaman minimal 3 tahun sebagai supervisor atau koordinator di bidang logistik, supply chain, atau sejenisnya. memiliki pengalaman kerja di area last mile atau first mile, menguasai seluruh proses perencanaan pengiriman dan pergudangan, serta mahir menggunakan microsoft excel.

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
kami mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk bergabung dengan tim kami. bertanggung jawab untuk meningkatkan penjualan dan mencapai target penjualan. melakukan analisis pasar dan kompetitor, serta membangun hubungan dengan merchant.

laki-laki/wanita usia maks 35 tahun, minimum pendidikan sma sederajat, memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, memiliki komunikasi skill yang baik, memiliki kendaraan roda dua, memiliki sim c aktif, pengalaman menjual mesin edc & akuisisi

jobs.title: Therapist
jobs.description:
ozen reflexology sedang membuka lowongan untuk posisi therapist. posisi ini bertanggung jawab memberikan layanan refleksi kepada pelanggan dengan standar pelayanan yang baik. kandidat diharapkan memiliki orientasi pada kepuasan pelanggan, mampu bekerja dalam sistem shift malam, serta bersedia mengikuti pelatihan yang disediakan perusahaan.

kandidat harus pria atau wanita dengan penampilan menarik dan usia maksimal 40 tahun. pendidikan minimal sma/smk. terbuka bagi yang berpengalaman maupun non-pengalaman. wajib memiliki kemampuan komunikasi yang baik, berorientasi pada pelanggan dan hasil, serta bersedia bekerja shift malam dan mengikuti pelatihan.

jobs.title: Staff Penagihan Lapangan
jobs.description:
nusantara sakti group membuka lowongan untuk posisi staff penagihan lapangan. tanggung jawab utama meliputi melakukan kunjungan dan penagihan kepada konsumen sesuai dengan prosedur (sop) perusahaan, menjalin komunikasi yang baik dan persuasif untuk menyelesaikan keterlambatan pembayaran, serta membuat laporan kunjungan harian dan berkoordinasi terkait kendala di lapangan.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk. memiliki sepeda motor pribadi dan sim c yang masih aktif. mampu berkomunikasi dengan baik, memiliki kemampuan negosiasi, dan siap bekerja di lapangan.

jobs.title: Merchant Succes Executive (Sales)
jobs.description:
bukuwarung sedang mencari merchant succes executive (sales) untuk melakukan akuisisi merchant dan penjualan mesin edc di berbagai wilayah di jawa tengah dan diy. posisi ini bertanggung jawab untuk memperluas jaringan merchant dengan dukungan gaji pokok, tunjangan pulsa dan transportasi, serta jaminan bpjs.

pria atau wanita dengan usia maksimal 35 tahun dan pendidikan minimal sma sederajat. kandidat wajib memiliki pengalaman sebagai sales fmcg, kemampuan komunikasi yang baik, serta memiliki kendaraan roda dua dan sim c aktif. pengalaman dalam menjual mesin edc dan akuisisi sangat diutamakan.

jobs.title: HUB LEAD
jobs.description:
posisi hub lead di spx express bertanggung jawab untuk memantau dan memastikan kelancaran pengiriman barang dari pengambilan hingga sampai ke tangan pelanggan. anda akan berkoordinasi dengan tim gudang, line haul, dan pihak ketiga, mengawasi aktivitas inbound dan outbound, menjaga keamanan paket dari risiko kerusakan atau kehilangan, serta melatih dan mengembangkan kinerja staf di hub.

## Terms of Reference (ToR)

### Final Evaluation of the Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP) Project

**Funded by the European Union**

### 1. Background

#### About People in Need

People in Need (PIN) is an international non-governmental organisation founded in the Czech Republic in 1992. It has implemented hundreds of humanitarian and development projects across Europe, Asia, Africa and Central America. PIN began its operations in the Philippines in 2013 in response to Super Typhoon Yolanda, and its programmes have since grown to cover market systems development, sustainable livelihoods, disaster resilience, renewable energy, peace and social cohesion, including in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

PIN seeks the services of a qualified external evaluator or evaluation team, referred to in this ToR as the Evaluator, to conduct the final evaluation of the LEAP project. The assignment will be carried out in close cooperation with the PIN project and MEAL teams and the consortium partners.

#### About the LEAP Project

The Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP) project develops the coffee and seaweed value chains in the island provinces of Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi (BaSulTa) in BARMM. It is implemented by People in Need as lead applicant, together with the co-applicants MARADECA and UNyPHIL-Women, under the European Union’s Bangsamoro Agri-Enterprise Programme (BAEP). The project runs from 1 July 2023 to 31 December 2026.

**Overall objective:** To contribute to a peaceful, cohesive, secure and inclusive development of agri- and aqua-culture value chains in Bangsamoro.

**Specific objective:** Coffee and seaweed production improved in quality, diversity, consolidation and its response to the needs of the market.

#### Outputs

- **Output 1:** Coffee and seaweed value chains in the island provinces are mapped, analysed and better coordinated.
- **Output 2:** Individual farmers and farmer or fisher folk groups are equipped for diversified, quality production through access to crop and sea inputs and extension services.
- **Output 3:** Farmer and fisher folk small social enterprises within the coffee and seaweed value chains are established and strengthened.
- **Output 4:** Enhanced post-harvest and processing facilities are in place.

#### Target Groups

The main target group is coffee and seaweed farmers, small farmer groups and cooperatives in Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi, a minimum of 2,000 farmers, with particular focus on women, youth and indigenous people.

Other target groups are traders and input suppliers in the three provinces; local, regional and provincial authorities, including MAFAR, MTIT and OPAG and the provincial agricultural offices; and academia, in particular MSU Tawi-Tawi.

The final beneficiaries are farmers, cooperatives and traders across BARMM and the general population of the island provinces.

### 2. Purpose and Objectives of the Evaluation

The final evaluation will assess the extent to which LEAP achieved its objectives and results, and how the intended and unintended changes came about. In line with the project design, the evaluation is conducted by an external evaluator with strong expertise and experience in markets development in the Philippines. It will provide lessons and recommendations that assist PIN, the consortium partners and other stakeholders to enhance the impact of future interventions in BARMM.

The specific objectives of the evaluation are to:

- Assess the project's performance against its overall objective, specific objective and the four outputs, measured against the logframe baseline and targets.
- Identify what worked, what did not, and why, across the coffee and seaweed value chains and the three island provinces.
- Generate practical lessons learned and actionable recommendations for future value-chain programming in BARMM.
- From a market systems perspective, the evaluation should assess not only what LEAP delivered, but the extent to which the project contributed to changes in how the coffee and seaweed market systems function. This should include changes in relationships, incentives, behaviours, capacities and roles among farmers, cooperatives, private-sector actors, service providers and public institutions, and the likelihood that these changes will continue, adapt or expand beyond direct project support.

### 3. Scope of the Evaluation

**Type of evaluation.** This is a performance evaluation against the standard OECD-DAC evaluation criteria. Impact is assessed as the project's plausible contribution to change measured against baseline values, and not through a counterfactual design. A separate impact evaluation of the programme will be conducted by the European Union, so this evaluation focuses on performance and does not attempt to measure the macro-level impact indicators.

**Period under review.** The whole project duration, from 1 July 2023 to the time of the evaluation.

**Geographic scope.** The three island provinces of Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi, with in-person data collection in each province.

**Coverage.** The evaluation covers the whole project, both the coffee and the seaweed value chains, the specific objective and all four outputs, assessed against the logframe baselines and targets.

### 4. Evaluation Criteria and Questions

The evaluation applies the standard OECD-DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, together with EU added value, inclusivity and gender equality and social inclusion, and cross-cutting themes. The questions below are the key areas to be answered. The Evaluator is expected to refine them and develop the corresponding judgement criteria, indicators and data sources in an evaluation matrix as part of the inception report.

#### Relevance

- To what extent did the project respond to the real needs and priorities of coffee and seaweed farmers in the island provinces, including women, youth and indigenous people?
- To what extent were interventions informed by identified market demand, commercial opportunities and underlying constraints within the coffee and seaweed market systems, as opposed to primarily responding to the immediate needs of producers?
- Was the project design and its modalities of support appropriate and conflict-sensitive given the security context of the island provinces?

#### Coherence

- How well did the project align with BARMM priorities and relevant sector roadmaps, and complement the work of MAFAR, MTIT, OPAG, the provincial agricultural offices and other actors in the coffee and seaweed sectors?
- How coherent were the interventions internally, across the four outputs and the two value chains?

#### Effectiveness

- To what extent were the specific objective and the four output targets achieved, measured against the baseline?
- How did results differ between the coffee and seaweed value chains, and what explains the differences?
- How well did the distinctive components perform, in particular the coordination platforms, the private nurseries, the post-harvest and processing facilities, savings groups, and the solar technologies and climate services?
- What were the major factors influencing the achievement or non-achievement of results?

#### Market Systems Effectiveness

- What market-system constraints did LEAP successfully address, and which constraints remain binding for the growth and inclusivity of the coffee and seaweed sectors?
- What changes occurred in the behaviour, practices, relationships and incentives of key market actors as a result of LEAP?
- To what extent have market actors taken ownership of functions initially supported or facilitated by the project?
- Is there evidence that practices, services, business models or relationships introduced or strengthened through LEAP have been adopted by actors beyond those directly supported by the project?
- Where systemic change has not occurred, what prevented it (weak commercial incentives, capacity constraints, institutional barriers, limited demand, conflict dynamics, project design or another factor?)

#### Efficiency

- Were the financial and human resources used economically to deliver the outputs across two value chains and three provinces?
- Did the consortium model of PIN, MARADECA and UNyPHIL-Women deliver in an efficient and well-coordinated manner?
- Was implementation timely, including the use of the 6-months extended implementation period to December 2026?

#### Impact (Contribution)

- What significant changes occurred in production, quality, diversification, market access, sales and household income, and to what extent did LEAP plausibly contribute to these changes? What other actors or contextual factors contributed to the observed results?
- Were there different effects for women, youth and indigenous people, and any unintended effects, positive or negative?

#### EU Added Value

- What did EU funding of this project add beyond what regional or national actors could have delivered on their own?

#### Sustainability

- Are the coordination platforms and the emerging industry bodies, such as the Sulu Coffee Industry Development Board and the Basilan Coffee Industry Cluster Council, likely to continue functioning after the project ends?
- How durable is the institutional anchoring of the seaweed value chain, which is weaker than that of coffee?
- Are the post-harvest and processing facilities likely to be maintained and continue to operate independently?
- Are the social enterprises and savings groups viable beyond the life of the project?
- For key functions supported by LEAP, which actors now have both the capacity and commercial or institutional incentive to continue performing these functions without project support?
- If LEAP support ended completely, which changes would continue, which would weaken, and which would stop, and why?
- Is there evidence of replication, imitation, crowding-in or spontaneous adoption by farmers, businesses, service providers, government institutions or other actors that were not directly supported by LEAP? What factors enabled or constrained such scale?

#### Inclusivity and Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)

- To what extent did the project reach and benefit women, youth and indigenous people as intended, and was their participation meaningful rather than only numerical?

#### Cross-Cutting Themes

- How well did the project apply conflict sensitivity and a do-no-harm approach in practice?
- Were the Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM) and safeguarding measures functioning and accessible to target groups?
- How were environmental sustainability considerations addressed?

#### Lessons and Learning

- What are the main lessons from LEAP that PIN and partners should carry into future value-chain programming in BARMM?

### 5. Methodology

The Evaluator is responsible for developing the evaluation design and detailed methodology to meet the objectives above. A mixed-methods approach is expected, combining qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis. Findings must be measured against the logframe baseline values wherever the indicators allow. The proposed approach, the sampling strategy and the data collection tools are to be presented in the inception report and agreed with PIN.

#### Desk Review

The Evaluator will review the project's logframe and description of the action including amendments, the baseline study, narrative and progress reports, monitoring data, the coffee and seaweed value chain studies and other studies conducted under the project, and summaries of feedback received through the CFRM.

#### Field Data Collection

- Key informant interviews with project and MEAL teams, consortium partners, government and private stakeholders.
- Focus group discussions with farmers and other value chain actors, held in person in all three provinces.
- Direct observation of nurseries, post-harvest and processing facilities and donated equipment, to verify that they are in place and functional.

Given the cultural context of the island provinces, the evaluation team should be gender-balanced so that women farmers can be interviewed by women enumerators where appropriate. The team must also cover the local languages in use in the target areas, including Tausug, Sama and Yakan, either within the team or through qualified interpreters.

The qualitative methodology should include purposive interviews with market actors positioned both within and beyond LEAP's direct intervention portfolio, including buyers, traders, processors, input suppliers, financial/service providers and relevant public institutions. This will enable the evaluation to test whether observed changes extend beyond direct beneficiaries and project-supported structures.

Evaluator should use contribution analysis and/or outcome harvesting to reconstruct the change pathway, assess LEAP's contribution alongside other influencing factors, and identify evidence of behavioural change, ownership, replication and sustainability.

#### Note on the Inception Report

Once approved by PIN, the inception report becomes the reference document for the assignment, and the final evaluation report will follow it. Approval of the inception report is internal to PIN.

### 6. Key Deliverables

Deliverable

Description

Inception report

Methodology, evaluation matrix, sampling strategy, data collection tools and workplan, developed in consultation with the PIN project and MEAL teams. Once approved, it becomes the reference document for the assignment.

Draft evaluation report

Main findings presented for review by PIN and the consortium partners.

Final evaluation report

Feedback incorporated. The executive summary should not exceed 3 pages. The report should be concise and evidence-led.

Validation presentation

Key findings and recommendations presented to the project team and relevant stakeholders.

Findings-sharing event

A one-day findings-sharing event in Zamboanga City/Cotabato for about 30 external stakeholders, organised and fully funded by the Evaluator, including venue, participant transport, meals and logistics. PIN will support coordination with the stakeholders and agrees the participant list.

Datasets, tools and transcripts

Cleaned and anonymized datasets, the data collection tools, transcripts, and the analysis files or calculations used in the evaluation.

Thematic learning briefs

One or two short briefs on specific components or approaches, for example the market systems development approach, designed for reuse in future programming. E.g. Market Systems Learning Brief: What did LEAP teach us about facilitating inclusive market-system change in fragile and conflict-affected island economies?

Inputs to the PIN evaluation brief

A short summary of the key findings and recommendations for the PIN evaluation brief.

#### Structure of the Final Report

The final report should include an executive summary, an introduction describing the project and the purpose and questions of the evaluation, the methodology and its limitations, the findings organised by evaluation question, conclusions against each criterion, lessons learned, actionable recommendations, and annexes including this ToR, the evaluation tools and the logframe.

The final report should include a dedicated synthesis of market-system change, distinguishing between:

1. Direct beneficiary-level results.
2. Changes in market actor behaviour and relationships.
3. Changes in supporting functions, rules or institutions.
4. Evidence of sustainability, replication, crowding-in or scale.

### 7. Indicative Timeline

The timeline below is indicative and will be confirmed at contracting. The Evaluator should propose a detailed workplan in the inception report.

### 8. Qualification Requirements

#### Mandatory

- Proven experience in conducting final evaluations of EU-funded projects, or final evaluations for international non-governmental organisations.
- Demonstrated experience evaluating market systems development (MSD) and/or systemic value-chain development programmes, including assessment of market actor behaviour change, sustainability, facilitation, crowding-in and systemic change.
- Experience applying contribution analysis, outcome harvesting or other theory-based approaches to assessing systemic change.
- Strong quantitative and qualitative research skills, including survey design, key informant interviews, focus group discussions and data analysis.
- Experience working in conflict-affected or conflict-sensitive areas, and with marginalized communities.

#### Desirable

- Knowledge of the BARMM and BaSulTa context.
- Experience with the coffee or seaweed value chains and with agriculture, fisheries or aquaculture programmes.
- Experience in inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches. The proposed team should be gender-balanced.
- Coverage of the local languages in use in the target areas, including Tausug, Sama and Yakan, within the team or through qualified interpreters.
- Excellent analytical, report-writing and presentation skills in English.

### 9. Selection Criteria

Applications will be assessed against the following criteria, for a maximum total score of 100 points. Only proposals meeting all mandatory qualifications will be scored. The budget is published and fixed, so the financial offer carries a low weight in order to focus selection on quality.

jobs.title: Technical Officer – Ocean Observations
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Geoscience Energy and Maritime (GEM) Division** provides advice, technical assistance, research and training support to Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs). There are four (4) areas of scientific programming within this division:

1. **Oceans and Maritime Programme (OMP)** – assists member countries with services that provide applied ocean science and knowledge for evidence-based policy-making and technical solutions for improved ocean and maritime governance, management and capacity development.
2. **Georesources and Energy Programme (GEP)** – assists member countries by applying technical knowledge in the areas of geoscience and sustainable energy use.
3. **Disaster and Water Resilience Programme (DWRP)** – assists member countries to demonstrate strengthened resilience through integrated action on disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, natural resource management and increased access to water and sanitation.
4. **Earth and Ocean Observation Services** – Promoting spatial data and systems analysis and capacity to improve decision-making to improve resilience and sustainable resource management.

The role – **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** will provide technical hands-on support for SPC’s regional ocean observation and monitoring activities, with a primary focus on wave monitoring systems. The role operates within SPC’s technical workshop capability, supporting the deployment, maintenance, and operational sustainability of wave buoys, while contributing to other in situ ocean observing systems (e.g. ADCPs, water-quality sensors, and multi-sensor platforms) across SPC member countries, including applications relevant to fisheries, maritime, and ocean and climate services.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Wave and Ocean Monitoring System – Deployment and Field Operations**

- Plan, coordinate, and participate in deployment, recovery, and redeployment of wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing instruments, in collaboration with SPC teams and national counterparts, including participation in diving operations where required.
- Undertake or contribute to site assessments, mooring design and deployment planning ensuring alignment with local environmental conditions and operational requirements.
- Lead or support offshore and coastal field operations, ensuring compliance with SPC safety and operational procedures, and alignment with mission objectives.
- Prepare mission plans, risk assessments, and field operation reports, documenting technical outcomes, issues encountered, and lessons learned.

**Maintenance, Troubleshooting and Technical Support**

- Provide technical maintenance and troubleshooting support for wave buoys and other in‑situ ocean observing systems, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and moorings, in collaboration with national counterparts, SPC teams and service providers.
- Plan and coordinate preventative and corrective maintenance activities, to ensure operational availability and longevity of observing systems.
- Diagnose technical faults, recommend corrective actions, and support their implementation by relevant SPC teams, service providers, or national partners.
- Maintain accurate maintenance logs, calibration records, and technical documentation to support asset tracking, audits, and knowledge transfer.

**Data Quality Assurance, Data Management Procedures & SOP Development**

- Support the application of agreed data management and data quality assurance procedures for wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing systems, in line with SPC and country arrangements.
- Support the timely and reliable ingestion of observation data from SPC‑supported systems into SPC and agreed national data management platforms.
- Work with national counterparts to support the sharing and integration of country‑owned observation data in accordance with agreed processes and data governance arrangements.
- Contribute to the development, maintenance, and application of standard operating procedures (SOPs) covering deployment, maintenance, data handling, and incident response.

**Procurement and Asset Management**

- Provide technical input to procurement processes for ocean observing equipment and services, including preparation of technical specifications, participation in evaluations, and engagement with suppliers, in line with SPC policies and procedures.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of ocean observing assets, including inventories, warranties, servicing requirements, and lifecycle status, to support effective planning, maintenance, and sustainability of observing systems.
- Coordinate logistics for ocean observing equipment, including shipping, customs clearance, insurance, and freight documentation, in collaboration with SPC logistics, procurement, and finance teams.
- Ensure asset and logistics documentation is complete, current, and accessible to support audits, reporting, and effective handover between staff and teams.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Degree in electronics, electrical engineering, marine science or technology, ocean instrumentation, or a closely related technical discipline or an equivalent body of knowledge and experience.
- Open Water Diving certification or equivalent occupational diving certification, and fitness to undertake work‑related diving activities.

**Technical expertise**

- Minimum 4-5 years’ progressive technical experience in marine, oceanographic, environmental monitoring, or related operational fieldwork.
- Demonstrated experience in the deployment, recovery, commissioning, testing, and validation of in situ observation systems, such as wave buoys, moorings, current meters (e.g. ADCPs), or multi‑sensor platforms.
- Practical experience maintaining and troubleshooting marine instrumentation, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and associated electronics.
- Experience supporting or applying preventative and corrective maintenance practices, including record‑keeping and technical documentation.
- Understanding of marine field operations, including site selection, environmental conditions, operational risks, and safety requirements.
- Experience delivering hands‑on technical training or mentoring to adult learners or technical counterparts.
- Proven ability to work effectively with government agencies, technical services, and regional partners.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **Until 30 June 2028** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** is a band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,146‒2,683 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 6,632–8,290 (USD 2,876–3,595; EUR 2,595–3,244). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Chief of Party, Food for Peace (FFP)
jobs.description:
**Program: Food for Peace (FFP) Non-Emergency Multi-Year Programming**

**Location: To be determined based on final USDA Notice of Funding Opportunity**

**Reports to: Global Communities Country Director**

**Please Note: This position(s) is contingent upon award and USDA approval with an anticipated start date of early 2027.**

**Overview:**

*Global Communities champions innovative solutions to complex challenges at the intersection of humanitarian assistance, sustainable development, and financial inclusion. We ensure our approaches are as dynamic and diverse as the communities we serve. We bring together local ingenuity and global insights to save lives and secure strong futures.*

Global Communities is seeking a Chief of Party (COP) for an anticipated multi-year, USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency project. Authorized under Title II of the Food for Peace Act, USDA’s multi-year Food for Peace Non-Emergency Programming will target people and places that experience recurrent food crises with a Graduation through Agriculture-led Development Approach and by utilizing U.S. agricultural commodities. This approach combines the Graduation model with targeted Market Systems Strengthening focused on agricultural value chains to build resilience, improve food security, and reduce dependence on emergency food assistance.

The COP will lead and oversee the overall implementation of the program, including setting vision and programmatic strategy and providing financial and operational leadership to attain targeted project deliverables and outcomes. The COP will manage a team of senior staff to ensure the quality, timeliness, and efficiency of all products and activities generated under the project. The COP will be responsible for communications with USDA, for publicly representing the project, and for liaising with Government entities and other institutions/stakeholders.

**Responsibilities:**

- Provide program leadership, direction, and supervision, including oversight of staff, consultants, and partners, monitoring and evaluation, and program implementation.
- Ensure implementation of technical interventions, resulting in concrete and on-time and on-target outcomes.
- Serve as primary point of contact for the project with USDA, government counterparts, and other critical in-country stakeholders.
- Lead regular work plan, budget, and implementation reviews to facilitate the cost-effective and timely achievement of deliverables.
- Manage team members, including highly specialized technical staff, to deliver against the annual workplan.
- Ensure project activities maximize impact and are completed in compliance with Global Communities policies, USDA rules and regulations, and local laws, and agreement requirements.
- Lead in adaptive management, achieving peak performance and innovation.
- Oversee timely and high-quality reporting to USDA, effectively and accurately communicating project progress, achievements, challenges, and utilization of funds.
- Ensure establishment and maintenance of systems for project operations.
- Build and maintain strong working relations with key internal and external stakeholders, beneficiaries, suppliers, and partners. Provide effective and timely responses to inquiries and concerns.
- Foster good working relationships with other agencies working on similar or complimentary projects, maximizing visibility and learning.
- Ensure that lessons learned are disseminated and applied.
- Liaise with Global Communities colleagues to coordinate the inputs of gender and inclusion, monitoring and evaluation and other advisory inputs to provide cross-cutting support.
- Collaborate with Global Communities colleagues and projects in-country to ensure effective coordination of Global Communities country operations.
- Undertake all other duties and projects as may be assigned from time to time.
- Frequent travel to project locations required

**Qualifications:**

- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a discipline related to agriculture, agri-business, economics, international development or other relevant field with a minimum of 10 years of professional experience, including managing multi-sectoral projects with increasing responsibilities and duties; or,
- Bachelor’s degree in a discipline related to agriculture, agri-business, economics, international development, or other relevant field with a minimum of 12 years of professional experience, including managing multi-sectoral projects with increasing responsibilities and duties.
- At least 5 years’ experience as Chief of Party, senior management position, or equivalent, leading implementation of large international donor programs.
- Technical expertise in food security, nutrition, market systems development, value chain development, and/or graduation models.
- Experience working in emerging markets with experience in [USDA’s priority countries](https://www.fas.usda.gov/newsroom/stakeholder-notice-advancing-alignment-america-first-food-assistance-priority-countries) (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo DRC, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Kenya, and Mozambique) preferred.
- High level of interpersonal, technical, and analytical skills, including a demonstrated ability to interact effectively and collaborate with a broad range of public and private sector counterparts and other key stakeholders.
- Demonstrated knowledge and application of non-emergency Food for Peace, agriculture-led development, resilience or similar programs preferred.
- Ability to develop effective working relationships with government officials, civil society organizations, private sector actors, implementing partners, international donors, and other stakeholders.
- Proven ability to communicate a common vision among diverse partners and the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams is desired.
- Evidence of effective communication skills, both oral and written, to fulfill the diverse technical and managerial requirements of the agreement is desired.
- Languages: Full Professional Proficiency in spoken and written English and Spanish is required. Must be able to use both languages fluently and accurately and be able to read all styles and forms on all levels pertinent to professional needs.
- A passion for the mission and values of Global Communities.
- Local candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

*Global Communities positively welcomes and seeks applications from all sections of society. We are committed to a work environment that respects the dignity and worth of everyone and offers equal opportunity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.*

*Global Communities holds strict safeguarding principles and has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment. In the process of recruitment, selection, and appointment, Global Communities will conduct robust reference and background screening checks, including international vetting as a signature of the Global Misconduct Disclosure Scheme to ensure children and vulnerable adults are safeguarded, and abuse is prevented. The incumbent is required to carry out their duties in accordance with Global Communities Safeguarding policy and the Standards of Conduct.*

jobs.title: Administrative coordinator (F/M) - Ukraine
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Ukraine**

MdM International Network has been operating in Ukraine since 2014, improving access to health care, especially providing comprehensive Primary Health Care (PHC), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) and Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.

Since February 2022, MdM Spain is leading the country response for the network, while MdM-France is in charge of the operations in Southern Ukraine. The global strategy aims at ensuring the access to quality comprehensive healthcare services for the conflict-affected population in Ukraine.

In Southern Ukraine, MdM-France has set up its country office and a base office in Mykolaiv. An office in Odesa is still running for specific activities monitoring in Odesa. The program consists in supporting various local-based organizations in the delivery of health services for people facing severe constraints to healthcare in Mykolaev and Kherson Oblasts.

The main strategic objectives for the Adminisrative department are, to consolidate the operational process at mission level to strengthen the quality of support services, to transfer competencies to national staff as well as working closer with national partners to build capacities.

Living conditions in Mykolaiv are pleasant (access to restaurants, presence of other organizations, places to relax...).

Expats share modern, well-equiped guesthouse. However, there are strict security rules (curfew imposed by the authorities) and a volatile environment (regular activation of air alerts).

**About the role**

As Administrative Coordinator, you ensure completeness, correctness, timeliness and integrity in your role. As a strategic partner to the operations, you will contribute to the definition and implementation of the mission’s objectives, participate in the sizing of the HR and financial needs and provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and Financial management of the mission.

**What you’ll do**

More specifically, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Nationalize the administrative coordinator position
- Review & implement a new HR set up of Finance & HR department post nationalization
- Supervise the implementation of the mission’s HR set-up
- Define, adapt, plan, and supervise the implementation of the mission’s human resources frameworks, procedures and policies while respecting the local context, local legislation and MdM policies and values (compensations and benefits, recruitment good practices, performance reviews, staff safe guarding, talent management, staff disciplines, career development and learning or team building)
- Plan, centralize, coordinate, and supervise the financial management and administration of the mission (accounting, budget construction and follow-up, internal and external reporting, donor compliance, audits, administrative legal obligations, etc.)
- Follow up the evolution of the legal environment and ensure MdM remains in line with official guidelines and policies in the framework of its principled approach
- Recruit, train, and manage an administrative department team
- Provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and financial management of the mission
- In terms of coordination and representation, you will ensure, when needed and by delegation of the General Coordinator, the representation of MdM in front of donors and liaise with INGOs heads of Admin Departments in-country
- You will provide strong oversight to MDM local Partner activities, including compliance with donor regulations

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the General Coordinator (F/M), you will manage the HR and Finance team in the coordination office and functionally support the HR and Finance team in the operational base(s). You will closely interact with the HR and Finance Advisors based in the HQ and the other departments at mission level (logistics, programs etc.)

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- hold a 3 years’ higher education management qualification
- have at least 4 years of experience in administration (HR and Finance) in a humanitarian context (including at least two years’ experience in an international NGO at coordination level)
- have an experience in a conflict setting or challenging environment. like in Ukraine (strong asset)
- have previous experience with MdM (preferred)
- proved your ability to negotiate and build / consolidate a network with authorities in a complex and volatile legal environment
- have a previous successful experience in team management (preferred)
- have a significant experience in PSEA management (an advantage)
- have a solid experience in budget management backed by institutional donors, payroll and accounting in a humanitarian context (prerequisite)
- you proved you are able to understand and interpret the legal administrative framework for staff and the MdM rules
- you have excellent Microsoft Office skills (especially Excel) and knowledge of accountancy software (like Saga or any relevant ERP)
- are fluent in English (mandatory, C1 level minimum), and have some knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian (would be an asset

**This role may not suit you if:**

- you are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach
- you are not able to defend the Administrative point of you in front of other actors/leaders
- you are not diplomatic and assertive

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3'392 €
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting in beginning of December
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Mykolaiv
- Regular field visits

**Benefits**:

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse managed by the mission
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials**:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
if you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Integrante de Equipo de Acción Contra Minas
jobs.description:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Barranquilla y Bogotá, actualmente también incorpora actividades en Nariño y en Norte de Santander.

**Objetivo del cargo:**

Ejecutar de manera segura, eficiente y conforme a los Procedimientos Operativos Normales (PON), las Normas Nacionales de Acción Contra Minas y los estándares internacionales aplicables, las actividades operacionales, técnicas y comunitarias requeridas para la implementación de los procesos de liberación de tierras. Bajo la supervisión directa de los responsables operacionales, contribuir al cumplimiento de los objetivos del programa mediante la ejecución de tareas de despeje, estudios no técnicos y enlace comunitario.

Como **Desminador**, realizar operaciones de despeje de forma sistemática, controlada y segura en Áreas Peligrosas Sospechosas (APS) y Áreas Peligrosas Confirmadas (APC), aplicando los procedimientos establecidos para la detección, localización, excavación, recuperación, señalización y apoyo en la destrucción de minas antipersonal, municiones sin explosionar (MUSE) y otros artefactos explosivos, con el fin de garantizar la liberación segura de tierras de acuerdo con los criterios técnicos definidos.

Como **Auxiliar de Estudio No Técnico (ENT)**, apoyar la planificación y ejecución de las actividades de recolección, verificación, análisis y registro de información relacionada con la contaminación por artefactos explosivos, incluyendo la elaboración de actas, diligenciamiento de formatos, levantamiento de información geográfica, georreferenciación, mapeo de áreas peligrosas, gestión documental y mantenimiento de las comunicaciones operacionales, contribuyendo a la toma de decisiones y a la delimitación adecuada de las áreas de intervención.

Como **Enlace Comunitario**, facilitar la comunicación y coordinación entre la organización y las comunidades beneficiarias durante todas las fases del proceso de liberación de tierras, promoviendo la participación comunitaria, la construcción de confianza y el intercambio de información relevante. Asimismo, desarrollar actividades de Educación en el Riesgo de Minas (ERM), orientadas a fomentar comportamientos seguros frente a la amenaza de minas antipersonal, municiones sin explosionar y otros artefactos explosivos, garantizando en todo momento el respeto de los principios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

**Responsabilidades Desminador:**

- Hacer el mantenimiento, calibración y manejo del detector asignado según el manual del fabricante.
- Garantizar que todas las señales de material metálico han sido investigadas y eliminadas, descartando o confirmando una amenaza, en el carril que le haya sido asignado, señalando el límite de área Reducida/Despejada de acuerdo con el sistema de marcación.
- Seguir las instrucciones del jefe de Equipo para iniciar el Despeje/Reducción del carril.
- Reducir/Despejar el carril asignado siguiendo estrictamente los POA de DRC-ACM y loa EN-AICMA.
- Ante la localización de cualquier objeto sospechoso o componente de MAP/AEI/MSE, debe detenerse, avisar al jefe de Equipo y desde una distancia segura indicarle el indicio a este. En caso de ser confirmado, debe marcar y cerrar el carril.
- Informará al jefe de Equipo el avance de un carril y retornar hasta la Línea Base, retomando la labor en una nueva senda según se le indique.
- Mantener y conservar en buen estado y limpio el equipo asignado.
- Solicitar al jefe de Equipo los elementos que sean necesarios para su labor.
- Cumplir en todo momento las órdenes que indique el jefe de Equipo en el desarrollo de trabajos de ET/D y/o el mantenimiento de las áreas administrativas o alojamiento.
- Responsable de su propia seguridad y autocuidado.

**Responsabilidades Auxiliar de ENT:**

- Estudio y análisis de la información disponible (Expediente Municipal, eventos IMSMA, etc).
- Asistir al jefe de Equipo en la planeación de las tareas de recolección de información en campo.
- Recolectar la información disponible mediante un análisis detallado de la evidencia existente con todas las fuentes de información útil, que refiera de la sospecha o presencia de Artefactos Explosivos, en las zonas asignadas.
- Asistir al jefe de Equipo en el análisis y diagnóstico de las áreas/sectores estudiados, que permita concluir el estado de contaminación o sin contaminación.
- Asistir al jefe de equipo en la marcación de las Áreas Peligrosas o Áreas Peligrosas Confirmadas por medio de la recolección, análisis de información y evidencias.
- Asistir al jefe de equipo en un primer reconocimiento visual de los Artefactos Explosivos localizados en las zonas de investigación.
- Recolectar información relevante para el diligenciamiento de documentos normativos de interés para la organización y sus diferentes programas.
- Asistir al jefe de equipo en la definición de los niveles de priorización de intervención.
- Facilitar el desarrollo de las actividades de DRC-ACM, mediante el correspondiente Enlace Comunitario.
- Seguir los procedimientos operacionales desarrollados por la organización y aprobados por la Autoridad Nacional.
- Apoyar según requerimiento por la gerencia de DRC-ACM, a otros componentes del proceso de liberación de tierras.
- Estar dispuesto a ser traslado de lugar de trabajo conforme a la necesidad de la organización.

**Responsabilidades Enlace Comunitario:**

- Presentar formalmente DRC -ACM, ante las autoridades locales y comunitarias.
- Presentar los objetivos de la presencia de DRC-ACM en las áreas de intervención.
- Incentivar la participación de las autoridades locales y comunitarias en el proceso de ejecución de las tareas de ET/D.
- Obtener información relevante acerca de la comunidad (por ejemplo, el tamaño de la población y sus movimientos, principal medio de subsistencia o fuentes de ingreso principal y cuestiones socioeconómicas).
- Obtener la información sobre el problema de los Artefactos Explosivos en una comunidad específica (historia y dinámica del conflicto / Tipo de Bloqueo / Proyectos de Desarrollo / Priorización, etc.).
- Identificar los grupos de riesgo específicos en la comunidad y entender la toma de riesgos, alcance y los motivos subyacentes para la contaminación por MAP/AEI/MSE.
- Proporcionar información sobre la ubicación y el tipo de Artefacto Explosivo requeridos para el ET/D y la marcación.
- Proporcionar información a la comunidad afectada sobre el ET/D.
- Asegurarse de que los representantes de la comunidad y/o usuarios de la tierra sean consultados y participen en el proceso desde su planeación hasta su finalización.
- Apoyar el desarrollo de la comunidad basado en la participación que implique el fortalecimiento del capital social.
- Informar sobre el sistema de marcación y señalización de las AP/APC, coordinando con la comunidad la existencia de alguna señal que se requiera añadir o quitar por un motivo justificado, buscando la aceptación de las señales oficiales dispuestas AICMA.
- Informar a la comunidad la importancia de la marcación de un área, enfatizando que no se debe quitar ninguna marca o ingresar al área, mientras el trabajo esté en curso y hasta que haya sido entregado por las autoridades.

**Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo**

- Procurar el cuidado integral de su salud.
- Participar activamente en la conformación del COPASST – Comité de Convivencia Laboral –Brigadas de emergencia, así como las actividades que los mismos realicen.
- Cumplir con las normas reglamentos e instrucciones del SG SST.
- Informar oportunamente de los peligros y riesgos latentes con su sitio de trabajo.
- Asistir a las capacitaciones en SST definidas por el programa de capacitación del SG-SST.
- Velar por el mantenimiento del orden y aseo de su puesto y área de trabajo.
- Suministrar información clara, veraz y completa sobre su estado de salud.
- Reportar inmediatamente al área de SST y su jefe inmediato los accidentes de trabajo que se presenten, incidentes (casi Accidentes) y enfermedades diagnosticadas como laborales.
- Reportar al jefe inmediato la necesidad de tomar acciones correctivas o preventivas, que correspondan ante no conformidades reales o potenciales del proceso al cual pertenece.
- Participar en las actividades de capacitación, simulacros y las que sean programadas desde seguridad y salud en el trabajo
- Participar y contribuir con el cumplimiento de la política y los objetivos del SG-SST.

**Soporte médico, Mando y Control:**

- Mantener actualizados las competencias de primeros auxilios y MEDEVAC que la organización le instruya.
- Conocer al detalle los Planes MEDEVAC en su sitio de trabajo, base, campamentos y/o en ruta.
- Asistir al jefe de Equipo o cualquier que sea responsable en cada momento en la ejecución del MEDEVAC en caso de accidente.

**Logística y recursos:**

- Asegurarse que los equipos y medios puestos a su disposición son empleados de manera correcta, manteniéndolos en perfecto estado
- de operatividad (limpieza y cuidado).
- Reportar inmediatamente al jefe de Equipo todos los daños y/o pérdida de materiales/equipos.
- En caso de tener un vehículo asignado, deberá cumplir con las leyes del tránsito, cuidado y mantenimiento del vehículo y cualquier otra norma que vele por el cuidado del vehículo.
- Apoyar en las actividades diarias de mantenimiento de las áreas habitadas por DRC, campamento, áreas de desminado y otras relacionadas con la organización.

**Responsabilidades transversales:**

- Asistir a capacitaciones especiales según se le requiera.
- Aplicar los principios humanitarios y de DRC en el ejercicio de sus funciones.
- Estar dispuesto a realizar otras labores, en que DRC-ACM lo capacite, para el mejor cumplimiento de los objetivos e indicadores del programa, por ejemplo, de conductor de Vehículo.
- Dar cumplimiento al código de conducta de la organización.
- Cumplir con el reglamento interno de trabajo, las normas locales de seguridad y toda disposición de personal y material.

**Se espera que todo el personal de DRC asuma las siguientes tareas generales:**

- Trabajar en el marco de los valores y estándares fundamentales de DRC.
- Estar familiarizado y adherirse a todas las políticas y procedimientos de DRC.

**Experiencias y competencias técnicas:**

- Haber trabajado por turnos extensos en campamentos y conocimiento del medio rural
- Habilidades en herramientas de uso en el campo
- Buen estado físico para trabajo de alta exigencia.
- Capacidad para manejar información sensible y confidencial.

**Educación** (Incluir certificados, licencias)

- Bachiller completo o Técnico o Tecnólogo en alguna área del conocimiento.

**Deseable:**

- Bachiller completo o Técnico o Tecnólogo en alguna área del conocimiento.
- Tener habilidades básicas en uso de herramientas tecnológicas
- Un (1) año de experiencia en trabajo con las comunidades
- Habilidad demostrable en comunicación y socialización de contenidos, para lograr interactuar con la comunidad y autoridades nacionales y locales.
- Manejo de computadores y adquisición de datos.

**Idiomas:**

- Dominio básico de Ingles. (deseable).

**Todas las funciones de DRC requieren que el titular domine las competencias básicas de DRC:**

• Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes

• Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación

• Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación

• Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad

• Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

- Salario: iniciando en $ 1.979.000 según experiencia y competencias del candidato
- Tipo de contrato: Obra Labor
- Horario: Ciclos operativos de seis semanas de trabajo de lunes a sábados de 8:00 a 4:00 p.m., al final del ciclo operativo se disfruta de 2 semanas de descanso (esta información se ampliará en el proceso de entrevistas).
- Fecha de inicio: noviembre 2026
- Medicina Prepagada: al 100% para el trabajador.
- Alimentación: Servicio de alimentación en base.
- Alojamiento: Alojamiento compartido en base
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina principal Nariño donde inician y finalizan los ciclos operacionales, con disponibilidad de traslado por necesidad programática a los municipios del triángulo del telembi.

**Proceso de solicitud**

Todos los solicitantes deben subir únicamente una carta de presentación (1 página) y una hoja de vida

actualizada (que no supere las 3 páginas) no se reciben más soportes por este medio.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes:** 01 de noviembre de 2026 a las 11:59 am Hora Local.

***Nota: Esta vacante está sujeta a subordinación de fondos por parte del donante.***

**Nota 1:** El postulante que aplique a esta convocatoria autoriza a DRC a validar la información personal suministrada en la hoja de vida. Su identificación será comprobada en las bases de datos públicas y privadas con el uso exclusivo de convalidar la información, de acuerdo con nuestras políticas antifraude, lavado de activos y financiación del terrorismo.

**Nota 2:** El/la postulante que de forma libre y voluntaria deseen hacer parte del proceso de selección para ocupar la posición de la presente convocatoria, deberán observar un estricto apego a las normas que apliquen para la materia (idoneidad en los títulos presentados, ejecución de pruebas de forma personal e individual y veracidad en la información) adhiriéndose a los manuales y Políticas anti fraude de DRC, so pena de declarar descalificado el postulante que incurra en cualquier irregularidad a juicio de la organización, aún por la mera sospecha, e incluso en posibles conductas de tipo penal conforme la legislación colombiana.

**Nota 3:**

¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!

En DRC creemos que la diversidad nos fortalece y que cada persona aporta talentos, experiencias y perspectivas valiosas. Promovemos un entorno de trabajo inclusivo donde todas las personas sean bienvenidas y valoradas por su talento, experiencia y potencial.

Invitamos a postularse a todas las personas que cumplan con el perfil del cargo, sin distinción de género, identidad o expresión de género, orientación sexual, edad, origen étnico o nacional, creencias, condición socioeconómica o cualquier otra característica que contribuya a la diversidad de nuestro equipo.

jobs.title: Responsable Relation Bailleurs - H/F - Tchad
jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

L’ESPRIT ALIMA : La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées sur la proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :

1. Le patient d’abord
2. Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
3. Responsabilité et liberté
4. Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
5. Faire confiance
6. L’intelligence collective
7. Responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent ou à l’adresse prévue à cet effet

**SOIGNER - INNOVER – ENSEMBLE** :

Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté.

L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires.

Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte

Contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA : Plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS** : Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Soudan, Soudan du sud , Mauritanie, Ethiopie, Haïti.

NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET : Malnutrition, Santé Maternelle, Santé Primaire, Pédiatrie, Paludisme, Épidémies (Ebola, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue), Hospitalisation, Urgences, Violences Basées sur le Genre, Protection transversale, santé mentale …

**CONTEXTE DE LA MISSION** : Les programmes ALIMA AU TCHAD

Le Tchad connaît une crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle sévère, accentuée par des afflux de population importants mais aussi par sa vulnérabilité aux catastrophes naturelles et aux épidémies.

ALIMA a débuté ses activités au Tchad en 2012 en partenariat avec l'ONG médicale tchadienne Alerte Santé.

En 2012, le projet implanté dans le district sanitaire de Ngouri, dans la province sanitaire du Lac, a été mis en œuvre grâce au soutien d'ECHO, de OFDA, de l'UNICEF et du PAM. Dans le cadre de ce projet, l'accent a été mis sur l'amélioration de la qualité de la prise en charge, un défi majeur au Tchad étant données les difficultés à mobiliser des compétences médicales qualifiées. Depuis 2021, Alerte Santé & ALIMA mène dans le DS de Ngouri, Dibinitchi et Isserom, le projet d’étude OptiMA grâce au soutien financier de Givewell ainsi que le projet d’hôpital résilient CRESH grâce au soutien de plusieurs fondations.

A partir d’avril 2013, ALIMA & Alerte Santé appuient également la prise en charge de la MAS à N’Djamena. Avant la mise en œuvre de ce projet d'ALIMA & AS, seul le dispensaire de Notre Dame des Apôtres dans le district Sud, proposait une prise en charge gratuite de la malnutrition dans la capitale. Fort de deux années d’activités, le projet a permis de montrer l’ampleur de la problématique de la malnutrition en milieu urbain (à N’Djamena où le taux de MAS atteint 2.8%).

Depuis 2021, un projet d’étude OptiMA est en cours au sein de l’UNT de l’HATC à N’Djamena.

ALIMA mène également un projet communautaire dans le 9eme arrondissement de N’Djamena depuis 2022 en partenariat avec l’Agence Française de Développement pour le traitement et la prévention de la malnutrition.

Dans le bassin du Lac Tchad, la situation humanitaire s’est dégradée consécutivement à la recrudescence des attaques des GANEs et aux effets du changement climatique.

Depuis 2019, ALIMA/AS offre des soins médico-nutritionnels gratuits et de qualité aux enfants de moins de 5 ans et des soins de santé préventifs et curatifs gratuits aux populations déplacées et hôtes du DS de Liwa affectées par la crise du Lac. L'approche d'ALIMA/AS permet d’offrir des soins médicaux et nutritionnels dans des zones éloignées des centres de santé et ainsi permettre l’accès aux soins de santé pour les populations déplacées.

En réponse à la crise soudanaise et l’afflux de réfugiés soudanais au Tchad, ALIMA est intervenu dès 2023 pour mener des activités en santé et nutrition en faveur des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes présentes dans l’Est du pays. ALIMA intervient actuellement dans la province du SILA, appuyant la prise en charge médicale des patients dans les sites de réfugiés ainsi que dans un centre de santé.

De par son importante couverture et la qualité reconnue de son intervention, ALIMA s’inscrit au Tchad comme un acteur majeur de la santé.

Entre janvier et septembre 2024, ALIMA a pris en charge plus de 35000 cas de malnutrition aigue chez les enfants de moins de 6 ans, soit près de 9% du total des prises en charge du pays.

Sur la même période, 140669 consultations ambulatoires, 1146 hospitalisations et 13000 prises en charge à domicile ont été réalisées par nos équipes sur l’ensemble de nos zones d’opérations.

LIEU DU POSTE : N’Djamena, TCHAD

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

Niveau 3 : Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES**

- Responsable Hiérarchique : Chef.fe de Mission (basé à N’Djamena)
- Responsable Fonctionnel : Référent Bailleurs ‐ Desk 1 (basé à Dakar)

**MISSION PRINCIPALE**

Sous la supervision du.de la Chef.ffe de Mission, le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de financement en lien avec le plan d’actions pays d’ALIMA.

Plus spécifiquement, il.elle est responsable de mobiliser des financements qui permettront la mise en œuvre des projets. Il·Elle entretient des relations régulières avec les bailleurs de fonds, et mène une recherche active de financements. Il.Elle est le garant ou la garante de la rédaction des propositions de projet et rapports aux bailleurs. Il·Elle appuie le suivi des indicateurs contractuels bailleurs, en collaboration avec les Coordinateurs.trices de projet et le.la Coordinateur.trice Médical.e.

**ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

- Définition et suivi de la stratégie de financement pays

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs effectue une analyse de la stratégie des bailleurs et la disponibilité de financements pour le pays concerné, afin de maintenir un niveau élevé d’information et de compréhension des enjeux. Il.Elle identifie les besoins de financements sur la mission en collaboration avec l'équipe de coordination et propose une stratégie de financement pertinente pour la mission. Il.Elle évalue les enjeux et propose l'adaptation de la stratégie selon le plan d’action opérationnel du pays. Au cours de la mission, le.la responsable Relations Bailleurs effectue le suivi de la stratégie de financement et l’adapte selon l'évolution des besoins. En lien avec le Chef de Mission et le.la Référent.e Bailleurs au siège, il.elle appuie la conception et la mise en œuvre d'une stratégie d'acquisition de subventions et de mobilisation de ressources

- Entretien de la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds

En lien avec le Chef.fe de Mission, il·elle assure la représentation auprès des bailleurs de fonds et négocie des financements pour les projets d’ALIMA. Il.Elle entretient les relations avec les bailleurs de fonds qui financent les projets pour assurer une communication régulière de qualité. Il.Elle coordonne la visite des bailleurs de fonds sur les projets quand la situation sécuritaire le permet, avec l’appui du.de la Chef.ffe de Mission.

- Recherche de financements

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs, en appui au Chef de Mission, mène une recherche active de financements et identifie les nouveaux bailleurs de fonds à approcher dans le but d’assurer la bonne connaissance d’ALIMA et des projets mis en œuvre par ses acteurs. Il mène une veille active sur les priorités thématiques des donateurs et des mécanismes de financement dans le pays. Il.Elle effectue la cartographie des donateurs et la collecte de renseignements, et informe régulièrement la coordination pays ce sujet. Il.Elle développe des fiches projets et plaquettes pour assurer la communication institutionnelle tout au long de l’année

- Appui à la planification opérationnelle en lien avec les priorités des bailleurs de fonds

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs appuie les Coordinateurs.trices Projet et l'équipe de coordination dans la conception d’interventions en lien avec la stratégie des bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle s’assure que les interventions sont alignées avec les priorités thématiques et opérationnelles des bailleurs de fonds, et que les soumissions respectent les formats requis par ces derniers.

- ## Production de concepts notes et de propositions de projet

Afin d’obtenir des financements, le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de la soumission des concepts notes et propositions de projets dans les délais imposés par les bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle assure l’écriture des documents de projet pour répondre aux opportunités auprès des bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle est garant de la qualité et conformité des documents produits.

- ## Diffuse les informations clés sur les procédures bailleurs, les contrats de financement et appui les Coordinateurs.trices de Projet dans le suivi des exigences contractuelles

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de la mise à jour de l’équipe de coordination sur les guidelines des bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle informe continuellement les équipes de l’évolution des procédures et exigences des bailleurs de fonds. En plus, le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs appuie les Coordinateur·rice·s de Projet dans le suivi des exigences contractuelles des bailleurs de fonds. Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs suit les évolutions opérationnelles, y compris budgétaire, afin de proposer des modifications contractuelles si nécessaires.

- Suivi des données pour répondre aux exigences du reporting

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs développe et incorpore des éléments solides de monitoring et de suivi dans les rapports dans les outils de suivi des projets et il.elle participe donc, avec le.la Data Manager et le.la Coordinateur.trice Médical.e, au contrôle et à la compilation des données opérationnelles. Il.Elle s’assure de la mise à jour des outils de suivi de données en lien avec les contrats de financement, et anticipe les échéances des rapports afin d’assurer la complétude des données et une analyse de qualité.

- Assurer la production de rapports narratifs précis et analytiques dans les délais définis

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de l’élaboration des rapports intermédiaires et finaux pour les bailleurs de fonds, selon les formats et règles de reporting imposés. Il est directement chargé de la rédaction des documents, sur la base des informations précises, quantitatives et qualitatives et capitalisées au cours de l’année. Il·Elle établit une liaison régulière avec les Coordinateur·trice·s et responsables de projet et, pour l’élaboration des rapports, fait le lien entre les engagements auprès du bailleur et la réalité des projets et des terrains. Il.Elle s’assure du respect des deadlines et est responsable de la qualité des rapports.

- ## Assurer la gestion contractuelle des contrats de financement

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est garant du suivi des contrats de financement avec les bailleurs de fonds. Il·Elle est en contact direct avec les représentants nationaux du bailleur pour les questions de gestion contractuelle. Il·Elle s’assure de connaître et respecter les procédures du bailleur et que celles‐ci soient connues du reste de l’équipe. Il·Elle dispose pour cela d’un outil commun de suivi de contrat qu’il·elle contribue à mettre à jour.

- ## Assurer l’application des standards en prévention contre les abus

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs doit participer aux formations et aux séances de sensibilisation. Il·Elle applique les standards relatifs à la prévention contre les abus dans toutes les tâches qu’il·elle entreprend (ex: ajout de la thématique dans les rapports, les propositions de projet, clause sur la prévention des abus, etc). Il·Elle contribue à créer et maintenir un environnement épanouissant et protecteur.

**EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES**

- Diplôme d’études supérieur (niveau Master ou équivalent) en lien avec le poste (études du développement, santé publique, relations internationales, gestion de projet…)
- Excellent niveau d’anglais et de Français, à l’oral et à l'écrit
- Bonne maîtrise des outils de gestion de projet (cycle de projet, cadre logique, proposition de projets, reporting, etc…)

**Type de contrat** : CDD de droit Français avec possibilité de renouvellement

**Durée du contrat** : 6 mois renouvelable

**Lieu du poste** : N’Djamena, TCHAD

**Salaire :** Selon grille salariale ALIMA (niveau 11BIS) + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem

ALIMA prend en charge :

Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission

Les frais d’hébergement

La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droit

L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droit.

Date de prise de poste : **ASAP**

- Une expérience professionnelle en reporting, conception et/ou gestion de projet d’au moins un an, ainsi que d’une expérience de terrain.
- Excellentes capacités d’analyse, de synthèse et rédactionnelles
- Autonomie, capacité d’initiative, facilité à travailler en équipe et à communiquer
