jobs.title: Oficial de Cadena de Suministro - Maracaibo
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Cadena de Suministro** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

El Oficial de Cadena de Suministro es responsable de todas las adquisiciones de bienes y servicios, almacenamiento, transporte de bienes y personas, gestión de flotas de vehículos y apoyo logístico general al programa general en Zulia de conformidad con el marco interno de Danish Refugee Council – DRC y las regulaciones impuestas por los donantes.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Compras**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de compra requeridos para el adecuado funcionamiento de las operaciones de DRC en Maracaibo.
- Colaboración directa con los equipos de programa para la planificación local de las necesidades de compra y logísticas de los programas de DRC en Zulia.
- Generar seguimiento y trazabilidad de las solicitudes de compra.
- Validar la integridad documental de los procesos según los requerimientos de los donantes.
- Contacto con proveedores para cotizaciones y evaluaciones de compras locales.
- Comunicación directa con proveedores relacionados con la entrega de insumos en los programas de DRC.
- Seguimiento a devoluciones o reclamaciones con proveedores.
- Preparación de solicitudes de pago para el trámite de los equipos de Finanzas de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**Logística**

- Asegurar la entrega oportuna de los materiales solicitados, teniendo en cuenta los procesos y tiempos establecidos por DRC.
- Control, registro y seguimiento de los activos fijos gestionados en la oficina local.
- Realizar inventarios y llevar el control detallado del inventario general de DRC.
- Garantizar la gestión de los servicios generales para los equipos de trabajo (alojamiento, personal, visitantes, oficinas, lugares de almacenamiento y seguridad).
- Implementar procesos de registro, control, seguimiento y verificación de elementos del programa asignados al personal y a los logísticos de la oficina.
- En colaboración con el Líder de equipo de Cadena de Suministro apoyar en la inducción al personal de la oficina sobre los procesos de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**Gestión de Almacén**

- Comprobar que todos los activos antiguos y nuevos estén correctamente registrados y etiquetados.
- Gestionar el inventario de suministros de oficina y consumibles.
- Monitorear y administrar las existencias según los procedimientos de almacenamiento de DRC.
- Preparar y revisar todos los informes mensuales de movimiento de inventario antes de enviarlos al Oficial de Cadena de Suministro para su validación.
- Recogida o entrega de mercancías.
- Asegurar que todos los artículos en el almacén estén correctamente almacenados, apilados y contabilizados con precisión en todo momento.

**Gestión de Flota**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de gestión de flota de DRC en Maracaibo, Venezuela.
- Garantizar la disponibilidad de los vehículos para las operaciones de programa.
- Controlar el uso y consumo del servicio de transporte en la oficina local.

**Administración**

- Participar y ayudar en la implementación del ERP (DRC Dynamics).
- Colaboración con la unidad de finanzas para el correcto registro de la cadena de abastecimiento.
- Coordinación con la unidad de finanzas para la oportuna ejecución de los pagos.
- Redacción de contratos y acuerdos marco para la operación local.

**Competencias esenciales:**

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia en logística humanitaria, adquisiciones, transporte y distribución, almacenamiento y gestión de stocks.
- Vocación de servicio.
- Enfoque al detalle.
- Capacidad de auto-organización.
- Motivación por el trabajo en el sector humanitario.
- Orientación de servicio a los programas.
- Conocimiento de sistemas de ERP para compras.
- Manejo Avanzado de OneDrive, MS Word, Excel y Adobe PDF.
- Capacidades analíticas.
- Orientación a la resolución de problemas.
- Capacidad de trabajo bajo incertidumbre.

*Deseable:*

- Maestría o especialización en Ingeniería de Salud Pública, Ingeniería Hidráulica, Ingeniería Ambiental, Ingeniería Civil, Ingeniería Mecánica, Arquitectura o campo directamente relacionado;
- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Con conocimientos de aspectos de protección;
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad de crear buen ambiente de equipo y trabajo con socios locales implementadores;
- Manejo del inglés;
- Conocimiento de marco legal venezolano y derecho internacional.

**Educación (Incluir certificados, licencias)**

**Idiomas:**

**Ofrecemos:**

- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

jobs.title: Líder de Equipo WASH Shelter & Infrastructure (Caracas - Personal Nacional) - Republicado
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Líder de Equipo WASH Shelter & Infrastructure altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a el Líder de Equipo de Agua, Saneamiento, Higiene, Alojamientos e Infraestructura (WASI) de Emergencia será responsable de liderar operativamente la respuesta de emergencia y la recuperación temprana en los sectores de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Alojamientos de Emergencia (Shelter) e Infraestructura.

**Objetivo general del puesto**

Bajo la supervisión del Coordinador de Emergencias y/o Gerente de Base y la orientación técnica del Especialista Nacional WASI, el Líder de Equipo de Agua, Saneamiento, Higiene, Alojamientos e Infraestructura (WASI) de Emergencia será responsable de liderar operativamente la respuesta de emergencia y la recuperación temprana en los sectores de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Alojamientos de Emergencia (Shelter) e Infraestructura, asegurando la rápida evaluación de daños y necesidades, la priorización de intervenciones, la movilización eficiente de recursos y la supervisión técnica de las actividades implementadas por el equipo WASI para restablecer servicios esenciales y apoyar a la población afectada por el desastre. Además, garantizará el cumplimiento de los estándares humanitarios aplicables, la integración de los enfoques de protección, AAP y PSEA, la adecuada coordinación con autoridades, comunidades y otros actores humanitarios, y la gestión eficiente del equipo y los recursos asignados para el logro de los objetivos programáticos de DRC en contextos de emergencia.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Gestión**

- Dirigir y gestionar al equipo WASI de terreno, planificando sus actividades.
- Garantizar una adecuada planificación operativa y una ejecución de calidad de las actividades de respuesta WASI en terreno.
- Supervisar y acompañar técnicamente a los Oficiales WASI y demás personal vinculado a la implementación de actividades sectoriales.
- Asegurar el seguimiento diario de las intervenciones WASI, identificando oportunamente riesgos, limitaciones y oportunidades de mejora.
- Promover la integración transversal de los enfoques de protección, género, inclusión, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP) y protección contra la explotación y el abuso sexual (PSEA) en todas las actividades.
- Garantizar que el personal conozca, comprenda y cumpla las políticas, procedimientos y reglamentos de DRC.
- Reportar incidentes, faltas o incumplimientos del personal y participar en los procesos disciplinarios correspondientes cuando sea requerido.

**Programas y operaciones**

- Liderar la planificación operativa y la priorización de las acciones de respuesta rápida durante las primeras horas, días y semanas posteriores al desastre, asegurando una movilización eficiente de recursos humanos, materiales y financieros.
- Garantizar una ejecución eficiente y eficaz de los proyectos WASI en emergencias, en cumplimiento de los objetivos, cronogramas, presupuestos y estándares de calidad establecidos.
- Coordinar la realización de evaluaciones rápidas de necesidades en contextos de emergencia para orientar la planificación de la respuesta.
- Consolidar y analizar información proveniente de evaluaciones, monitoreo y reportes de terreno para apoyar la toma de decisiones estratégicas y la priorización de la respuesta.
- Identificar y escalar oportunamente necesidades críticas, brechas de asistencia, riesgos emergentes y limitaciones operativas que requieran decisiones o recursos adicionales.
- Supervisar la planificación e implementación de actividades de comunicación de riesgos y sensibilización comunitaria en higiene, distribución de kits WASH, kits de alojamiento y artículos no alimentarios (NFI).
- Coordinar con el equipo de Soporte la adquisición acelerada de materiales, equipos, servicios y obras necesarios para la respuesta.
- Participar en la elaboración de informes internos, reportes para donantes, propuestas técnicas y contribuciones programáticas relacionadas con el sector.
- Dirigir al equipo en la implementación de actividades de monitoreo y seguimiento de proyectos, incluyendo verificaciones en terreno, monitoreo post distribución y acciones de rendición de cuentas.
- Liderar la transición de las actividades de respuesta inmediata hacia intervenciones de recuperación temprana orientadas al restablecimiento progresivo y resiliente de servicios e infraestructura básica.

**Obras WASH, Shelter e Infraestructura**

- Supervisar la evaluación rápida de daños y condiciones de funcionalidad de infraestructuras afectadas para orientar la priorización de intervenciones de emergencia y recuperación temprana.
- Garantizar la priorización y supervisión de intervenciones destinadas al restablecimiento oportuno de servicios esenciales de agua, saneamiento e infraestructura en comunidades, centros de salud, escuelas, refugios colectivos y otras instalaciones críticas afectadas.
- Liderar la planificación y supervisión de intervenciones de sistemas WASH, alojamiento de emergencia, refugios colectivos y soluciones temporales de alojamiento conforme a estándares humanitarios.
- Priorizar junto con el Especialista WASI y el Coordinador de Emergencia las intervenciones de rehabilitación y recuperación temprana de infraestructuras esenciales.
- Supervisar la adecuación y gestión técnica de refugios colectivos y espacios temporales de alojamiento, garantizando condiciones mínimas de seguridad, dignidad, accesibilidad y protección para la población afectada.
- Supervisar la preparación de especificaciones técnicas, alcances de obra, presupuestos referenciales y requerimientos de contratación para intervenciones de emergencia y recuperación temprana.

jobs.title: Consultancy - Mid-Term External Assessment. Project: Strengthening Legal Accountability and Inclusive Justice in South-East Asia
jobs.description:
**Background**

The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) is seeking qualified applicants to conduct a mid-term assessment for its project on strengthening legal Accountability and inclusive justice in South-East Asia.

The project focuses on four interconnected result areas:

1. Strengthening legal aid provision.
2. Enhancing justice systems in project locations
3. Supporting gender-inclusive transitional justice and peacebuilding processes.
4. Strengthening international advocacy and accountability efforts.

As outlined in the project MEL Strategy, an independent assessment will be conducted at the project's midpoint to review progress against the approved logframe, assess implementation effectiveness, generate learning, and provide recommendations for the remaining implementation period.

- **Overview of the ICJ**

Composed of 60 eminent judges and lawyers from all regions of the world, the ICJ promotes and protects human rights through the rule of law, by using its unique legal expertise to develop and strengthen national and international justice systems. Established in 1952 and active on the five continents, the ICJ aims to ensure the progressive development and effective implementation of international human rights and international humanitarian law; secure the realization of civil, cultural, economic, political and social rights; safeguard the separation of powers; and guarantee the independence of the judiciary and legal profession.

- **Purpose of the Assessment**

The purpose of the mid-term assessment is to:

- Assess progress towards achieving project outputs and intended outcomes
- Review the effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, and adaptability of project implementation
- Assess the extent to which project activities are contributing to improved justice and accountability efforts
- Review safeguarding, security, gender, and inclusion measures taken by project interventions
- Identify lessons learned, good practices, and implementation challenges
- Generate practical recommendations for strengthening implementation during Year 2 and Year 3
- **Scope of Work**

The assessment shall cover all project activities implemented during the first 15–18 months, including:

The assessment will cover project implementation during approximately the first 15–18 months, examining progress towards expected results, key achievements, implementation challenges and outstanding activities. It will consider the effectiveness and quality of activities aimed at strengthening the capacity of legal and justice actors, supporting access to justice and human rights protection, building knowledge and skills on relevant legal and policy issues, and contributing to research, analysis, advocacy and engagement with relevant stakeholders. The assessment will also review the quality, relevance and progress of key project outputs and deliverables, including capacity-building activities, technical resources, legal and policy analysis, and other project-supported initiatives.

- **Key Assessment Questions**

Relevance

- Is the project responding to the priority of justice needs identified by legal practitioners, survivors, and justice actors?
- Do project interventions remain relevant in the relevant country’s evolving political and security context?
- Are the selected implementation approaches appropriate for project operating environments?

Effectiveness

- To what extent have planned outputs been achieved?
- Have legal practitioners increased their capacity in documentation, fair-trial standards, and accountability mechanisms?
- Are trained practitioners applying acquired knowledge in legal aid, documentation, or advocacy work?

Sustainability

- Which project approaches and capacities are likely to remain after project completion?
- Are local actors developing sufficient ownership of project processes and outcomes?
- **Methodology**

The consultant should use a mixed-methods approach consistent with the project's security-sensitive MEL framework. The ICJ’s Regional Director for Asia and Pacific Programme (Project Lead) and MEL Officer will review the methodology proposed by the evaluator. Ideally, it will include (i) a desk review of pertinent project documents and records (including the project proposal, logical framework, amended project documents, quarterly reports, intermediate evaluation, and various records containing monitoring data); (ii) primary data collection (remote and in-person). The primary data should involve mixed quantitative and qualitative research methods – including but not limited to interviews with project staffs, project partners, targeted CSO, event participants, lawyers and other target groups, quantitative survey with project beneficiaries.

- **Evaluation Implementation**

The evaluation should take place in November – December 2026 with the final deliverables due and contract concluding by **23 December 2026.**

The ICJ staff will provide logistical and technical support as appropriate throughout the evaluation process (compilation of project documents, assisting with scheduling meetings / interviews if desired, etc.).

A total of up to 22 working days (depending on national holidays in the incumbent’s country) will be available for:

- *Evaluation preparation* (including finalizing the evaluation methodology, performing the initial desk review of project materials, creating and testing data collection tools, compiling a brief inception note);
- Remote and in-person data collection;
- *Data analysis and synthesis*(including transcription, data aggregation, writing a draft report, presenting findings to the ICJ, and incorporating feedback from the ICJ into a final report).
- **Deliverables**

**Deliverable 1:** Inception Report

The Inception Report will set out the overall approach and methodology for the mid-term assessment and will include:

- Detailed assessment methodology;
- Assessment matrix;
- Data collection tools; and
- Detailed workplan and timeline.

**Deliverable 2:** Preliminary Findings Presentation

A virtual presentation of the preliminary findings to ICJ management and the project team, providing an opportunity to discuss emerging findings and obtain initial feedback.

**Deliverable 3:** Draft Mid-Term Assessment Report

A Draft Mid-Term Assessment Report presenting the findings, conclusions and recommendations of the assessment. The report should be maximum of 30–40 pages excluding annexes.

**Deliverable 4:** Final Mid-Term Assessment Report

A Final Mid-Term Assessment Report incorporating and responding to comments and feedback provided by the ICJ on the draft report.

jobs.title: Awards & Sub-Awards Officer
jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

The Awards & Sub-Awards Officer supports the effective management of CARE’s donor-funded portfolio across Syria operations, covering both the award (budgeting, financial monitoring, and reporting) and sub-award (partner due diligence, contracting, monitoring, and close-out) management cycles. Under the direct supervision of the Awards & Sub-Awards Coordinator, the position assists in pre- and post-award processes, including proposal budget preparation, financial monitoring and reporting, and sub-recipient due diligence, contracting, and monitoring, ensuring compliance with donor and CARE policies throughout. The Officer works closely with program, finance, partnership, and operations teams to ensure budgets are accurate, expenditures are aligned with donor requirements, financial reports are complete and timely, and sub-recipients comply with donor regulations, CARE policies, and project requirements.

The employee is also required to;

1\. Remain aware of and comply with safety and security regulations/procedures and bear responsibility for personal safety and security while under contract.

2\. Comply with the organization’s Policies which includes but not limited to Safeguarding Policy, Code of Conduct and other organizational and HR policies.

3\. The organization has a zero-tolerance approach towards sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse towards any person including our staff, representatives, partners, programme participants and members of the community where we work. We expect all staff, partners and related personnel to share this commitment by understanding, abiding by and working within the organization International Safeguarding Policy and related framework at all times whilst representing the organnization.

4\. Ensure that all direct team members are aware of their responsibilities with the CI Safeguarding Policy commitments, including signing of the Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct, and completing induction and refresher trainings;

5\. Depending on specific role and responsibilities, may be requested to comply with the terms of additional policies, guidelines and related regulations, as and when necessary.

**Key Responsibilities**

1. **Budgeting and Proposal Development:**

- Support the preparation of proposal budgets and budget amendments in line with donor rules and CARE policies.
- Assist in consolidating cost estimates from program, HR, and operations teams.
- Ensure proposed budgets include accurate shared costs and align with internal templates.
- Help maintain the Country Office Master Budget and update it upon new awards or revisions.
- Support in developing budget tools, templates, and guidance for internal use.

1. **Award Setup, Monitoring, and Reporting:**

- Support grant setup in CARE’s financial systems and ensure fund codes and chart fields are correctly established.
- Prepare monthly BVAs and pipeline updates for review by the Coordinator.
- Assist in analyzing budget variances and expenditure trends; flag potential overspending or underspending to relevant budget holders.
- Support the preparation of donor financial reports, ensuring completeness and compliance before submission.
- Contribute to grant close-out by verifying expenditures, ensuring reconciliations, and archiving supporting documents.

1. **Partner Assessment and Due Diligence:**

- Support the pre-award due diligence (DDA) process for potential partners by collecting and reviewing documentation.
- Assist in assessing partners’ financial systems, risk levels, and compliance readiness.
- Maintain partner DDA tracker and ensure all required documents are properly archived.
- Support preparation of partner risk ratings and mitigation plans.

1. **Sub-Award Management and Monitoring:**

- Assist in drafting and reviewing sub-award agreements and amendments to ensure financial and compliance accuracy.
- Track sub-award deliverables, reporting timelines, and payments.
- Review partners’ financial reports for accuracy, completeness, and eligibility of costs.
- Ensure timely submission of required documents, reconciliations, and cash advance settlements.
- Support desk reviews, site visits, and partner monitoring exercises in coordination with the Coordinator.

1. **Capacity Building and Partner Support:**

- Support in organizing and documenting partner capacity-building activities.
- Provide day-to-day guidance to partners on financial reporting templates, documentation standards, and compliance requirements.
- Track progress of partners’ corrective actions and follow-up on outstanding issues.

1. **Compliance, Documentation, and Coordination:**

- Ensure all budgets, sub-award agreements, and reports comply with donor and CARE standards.
- Assist in reviewing IPIAs and award modifications under the guidance of the Coordinator.
- Maintain complete and proper documentation for each award and sub-award, including agreements, reports, correspondence, and financial documentation.
- Prepare summaries and trackers for outstanding advances, payment reconciliations, and partner status updates.
- Support the preparation of award and sub-award sections in donor or audit reports.
- Ensure award and partner information is properly recorded in CARE systems.
- Support communication between Finance, Program, Partnership, and RMU teams to ensure accuracy and timeliness in financial management.

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
- Minimum 3 to 4 years of experience in budgeting, financial reporting, grants management, or donor-funded NGO projects.
- Strong analytical and numerical skills.
- Advanced Excel skills and financial analysis capabilities.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
- Excellent communication and coordination skills.
- Fluency in English (spoken and written

**Safeguarding Commitments**

The organization has a zero-tolerance approach toward sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse. We will carefully examine allegations and investigate, and take appropriate disciplinary action where this is needed, taking into consideration the rights and interests of the survivor, consistent with the organization’s survivor-centred approach. We make very clear that sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse in any form, perpetrated by our staff, partners or other related personnel, towards anyone, will not be tolerated.

We provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, handicap, disability, or marital status.

jobs.title: IT Officer - Horn of Africa (Somali nationals)
jobs.description:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO Horn of Africa (HOA)**

HOA was launched in 2019 as a regional entity and is based in Hargeisa, Somaliland, coordinating and supporting INSO’s activities in Kenya, Somalia, and Somaliland.

We are now hiring an IT Officer, Horn of Africa. This position is based in Hargeisa, Somaliland with travel to Kenya and Somalia

**Job Summary**

Reporting to the Operations Manager, Horn of Africa, you will be responsible for providing high-level IT and application support to INSO Kenya and Somalia offices. You will coordinate with Headquarters’ IT department to administer IT services such as INSO’s Office 365 and Exchange Online accounts, Adobe, ArcGIS Licensing, and internet maintenance and troubleshooting.

You will assist the Operations Manager in delivering a first-class support service to INSO staff and offices, acting primarily in a first-line support capacity, resolving issues in person, over the phone, or via remote connectivity.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Install and configure computer operating systems, printers, networks, and applications per INSO policy and guidelines.
- Monitor and maintain INSO’s network performance.
- Troubleshoot hardware and software issues in person, remotely, and via phone.
- Ensure all INSO users have access to all relevant licensed software, including Adobe, MS Office, and GIS software via the HQ IT Team.
- Update and manage INSO SharePoint’s folders and permission structure.
- Ensure procurement of IT equipment meets INSO’s global standards.
- Ensure IT equipment is updated in the asset database and stock in cooperation with the logistics officer.
- Work closely with colleagues to understand and respond to their IT needs.
- Provide IT training for newly hired staff.
- Coordinate with the Headquarters IT team to roll out and assist in maintaining new applications and technologies.
- Develop tutorials for local staff in relation to INSO applications and software.
- Assist the Operations Manager in preparing IT budgets.
- Assess the security threat to INSO’s IT systems and ensure it is appropriately mitigated.
- Monitor usage, renewal, and billing aspects of all third-party applications and report to the Operations Manager in case of required renewals.
- Perform other duties as required.

**Mandatory Requirements**

- Minimum 3 years of experience supporting IT services in a medium to large internationally focused organisation
- Extensive experience with Windows operating systems and other Microsoft technologies such as Office 365 applications, Exchange Online, Microsoft Intune, and SharePoint Online.
- Knowledge of local network management.
- Familiarity with ArcGIS and Adobe (licensing and installation).
- Fluent in written and spoken English and Somali.
- Degree or equivalent in Information Technology, Computer Science, or relevant field.

*Nice to Have:*

- Master’s in IT or similar
- Microsoft certificates
- Somali language
- NGO experience
- Experience in Remote support

**Core Competencies**

- Problem-Solving – Identifies issues, analyzes root causes, and contributes to effective and practical solutions.
- Communication – Conveys information clearly and professionally while maintaining strong organizational coordination.
- Interpersonal – Builds productive relationships through active listening, effective questioning, and confident stakeholder engagement.
- Diligence – Demonstrates understanding and application of humanitarian principles, values, and operational practices.
- Accountability – Works independently, meets deadlines, takes ownership of responsibilities, and maintains strict confidentiality of information.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

The Operations Manager (OM) is responsible for the direct or indirect oversight and coordination of all operational functions in the Bay Area (San Jose and Oakland) grouping, resulting in a well-functioning, compliant operational environment. The Operations Manager serves as the primary liaison for HQ Regional Functional Leads including Supply Chain Advisor (SCA), Regional Safety & Security Director (RSSD), Regional IT Director (RITD) and Global Facilities Director (GFD). This position reports to the Executive Director and oversees the Operations staff in both offices. This position is based in either San Jose or Oakland, with regular weekly onsite presence within both offices.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Security—S&S:**

- Oversee regional S&S matters.
- Responsible for the implementation and maintenance of all office S&S documentation.
- Organize all-staff S&S meetings at office or program site.
- Ensure that a minimum of one emergency evacuation is exercised at office or program site level per year and other appropriate trainings informed by Security Risk Assessment findings.
- Cascade HQ and/or office security warnings and advisories to staff, interns, and volunteers as needed.
- Report all S&S incidents involving covered persons in accordance with established protocols.
- Coordinate immediate incident management including filing police reports.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with other S&S actors or stakeholders, including but not limited to community organizations and partners, authorities, security and rescue services, and property owners.
- Assist in the development of office-specific S&S onboarding materials, ensuring the provision of S&S briefings to new staff and covered persons.

**Supply Chain—SC:**

- Serve as the region’s primary focal point for procurement, asset and inventory management, in-kind donations tracking and reporting, vehicle fleet management and transportation, and warehousing in accordance with established organizational and donor requirements.
- Lead the bidding process, including request for quotation process, request for proposal process, tender evaluation, and facilitating procurement committee functioning.
- Manage relationships with suppliers and vendors.
- Maintain up-to-date supplier and service provider records. Maintain asset register and inventory lists of purchased and donated items. Establish and manage inventory control for office supplies, stationery, and other consumables. In collaboration with the Finance Manager, ensure inventories reconcile with financial reports.
- Support program teams in meeting their match goals.
- Ensure policy compliance for the fleet of IRC-owned vehicles and oversee their maintenance and usage.
- Working with HQ Supply Chain to maintain IRC policy at all the times.
- Control and maintain the IRC policy through the PO system in Integra.

**Facilities Management:**

- Manage the region’s office and equipment leases, coordinate repairs and improvements with property managers, and lead the procurement of office equipment.
- Coordinate the allocation of workspaces and support related employee lifecycle needs such as building access.
- Support smooth functioning of office infrastructure including communications equipment and services.
- Assist with planning and coordinating office events and meetings.
- Responsible for coordinating on- and off-site storage needs.
- Maintain NorCal’s status with all counties related to annual property’s tax along with exemption status.

**Information Technology—IT:**

- Oversee grouping IT and communications infrastructure, hardware and software matters.
- Educate staff about IT support resources, including appropriate channels for incident reporting.
- Work with regional and HQ IT team to address any internet or telecommunications service disruptions, liaising with local internet and telecommunications service providers.
- Escalate any unresolved incidents or larger-scale IT projects (such as office moves or expansion) as needed.
- Ensure compliance with IT protocols, policies, and procedures including information security policy, IT procurement and asset management policy, acceptable use of IT resources policy, and new software procurement protocols.

**Other Duties**

- Provide mentorship and supervision to Operations staff, including leading team meetings, individual supervision and coaching, and conducting goal setting, and performance reviews.
- Approve Integra vendor creations and invoice journals.
- Coordinate with the Finance Director to manage administrative expenses and reports.

jobs.company: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
jobs.description:
*Note: Please note that this vacancy has been republished. Applicants who have already submitted an application do not need to reapply.* ​

Within ICMPD’s Mediterranean operations, the Modernisation Officer - AI and Automation contributes to the integration of AI enabled and automation solutions across regional portfolios and projects, including those delivered through field offices in Jordan, Lebanon, Libya and Tunisia. ​

The position focuses on supporting the implementation of fit-for-purpose automation, analytics, and digital workflows across projects, contributing to quality, timeliness, compliance, and resource efficiency within defined project scopes and operational priorities.

## **Functional Overview**

Within ICMPD's Mediterranean operations, the Modernisation Officer - AI and Automation contributes to the integration of AI enabled and automation solutions across regional portfolios and projects, including those delivered through field offices in Jordan, Lebanon, Libya and Tunisia. Working under the overall supervision of the Regional Portfolio Manager, and in close coordination with Portfolio Managers, Project Managers, and relevant HQ counterparts, the position supports the application of regional modernisation priorities within project delivery, ensuring alignment with organisational standards, policies, and operational requirements.​

The role focuses on supporting the identification, assessment, design, and implementation of fit for purpose AI enabled and automation solutions across projects in the region, contributing to quality, timeliness, compliance, and resource efficiency within defined project scopes and operational priorities. The position contributes to the development and implementation of project level solutions and outputs related to automation, knowledge retrieval approaches, delivery checklists, basic analytics and dashboards, results evidence pipelines, document workflows, and translation or proofreading support. This includes gathering and analysing requirements, facilitating stakeholder inputs, assessing solution options, including third party tools where relevant, and coordinating implementation with delivery teams, with a focus on practical and scalable outputs.

The incumbent contributes to the responsible and secure application of AI and automation in line with institutional data protection and information security requirements and with relevant principles of responsible AI, including human oversight, transparency, risk awareness, and inclusion, applying existing organisational frameworks and guidance. Where relevant and within approved project objectives, the position also provides technical support to project activities involving partner country institutions in the area of digitalisation and innovation, helping to ensure that solutions are context appropriate, practical, and sustainable.

## **Key Results**

**Coordinated Project Level AI and Automation Support:** Project teams across the Mediterranean region are supported in identifying, assessing, and advancing AI enabled and automation solutions that respond to operational needs and project delivery requirements. Project level initiatives are coordinated in line with regional priorities and organisational standards, contributing to coherence, reduced duplication, and more efficient implementation. Solutions and practices with potential for wider use are documented and shared for possible adaptation across projects where appropriate.

**Fit for Purpose Digital Solutions for Project Delivery:** Technical support is provided for the development, adaptation, and rollout of digital tools, dashboards, workflow solutions, and related delivery support mechanisms within approved project scopes. Requirements, use cases, and implementation considerations are analysed and translated into practical proposals and solution options. The operation of systems, processes, and project activities is strengthened through solutions that are feasible, user oriented, and aligned with delivery needs.​

**Responsible AI and Risk Aware Implementation:** AI and automation related initiatives are supported with appropriate consideration for privacy, information security, human oversight, transparency, and operational risk. Risks related to data sensitivity, misuse, bias, and vendor or platform dependency are identified, flagged, and addressed through practical mitigation measures within existing organisational frameworks. Project teams are supported in applying available guidance and controls to strengthen compliant and responsible adoption.

**Capacity Development and Knowledge Sharing:** Guidance notes, SOPs, templates, toolkits, and user aids are developed and maintained to support consistent implementation of modernised delivery practices across the region. Good practices and lessons learned from project implementation are captured and shared through established channels to support replication and organisational learning. Relevant project teams and stakeholders are supported through targeted training, practical guidance, and on the job assistance to strengthen adoption and effective use of AI and automation solutions.

## **Required Expertise**

- Strong analytical and conceptual skills, with the ability to support the application of AI enabled and automation approaches in project delivery and operational processes.
- Demonstrated expertise in AI, automation, digitalisation, or related methodologies, including awareness of associated operational, reputational, and governance risks.
- Proven ability to analyse delivery processes, identify improvement or automation opportunities, and contribute to practical and reusable solutions within programme and project contexts.
- Experience in gathering requirements, assessing user needs, and supporting the design and implementation of digital tools, workflows, or system improvements.
- Ability to assess and compare digital and AI related solutions, including third party tools where relevant, and to contribute to defining requirements, use cases, acceptance criteria, and implementation safeguards.
- Sound understanding of data governance, information management, and responsible AI principles, with the ability to translate them into practical guidance for project teams.
- Strong coordination skills and the ability to manage assigned initiatives and collaborate effectively across portfolios, projects, countries, and functions in an international context.
- Ability to translate technical concepts into clear, practical, user-oriented guidance and support materials for non-technical audiences.
- Proven capability to support capacity development and adoption of modernised delivery practices through training, coaching, documentation, and user support.

## **Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills**

- Master's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field. A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the Master's degree.
- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in digital transformation, automation, or AI-enabled solutions, preferably in international programme environments.
- Strong analytical, drafting, communication, and presentation skills.
- Proficiency in (verbal/written) English is required, knowledge of Arabic and/or French is an asset.
- Advanced proficiency in digital, IT, and collaboration tools.
- Relevant certifications (e.g. ITIL) are an asset.
