jobs.title: Mission France - Mediateur.rice interculturel.le F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Mediateur.rice interculturel.le pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

**Votre rôle :**

Au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel de passerelle entre les personnes accompagnées et les équipes médicales, psychosociales et sociales. Grâce à vos compétences linguistiques et interculturelles, vous faciliterez la compréhension mutuelle, contribuerez à lever les obstacles à l’accès.

**Principales responsabilités :**

Favoriser une communication claire et respectueuse entre les personnes accompagnées et les équipes MSF, en atténuant les barrières linguistiques, les incompréhensions culturelles et les discriminations, afin de contribuer à un accès équitable à des soins et à un accompagnement adaptés.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

## **Faciliter la communication et la médiation interculturelle**

- Assurer une interprétation fidèle et adaptée à la culture des personnes, dans la langue dans laquelle elles souhaitent s’exprimer.
- Aider les équipes et les personnes accompagnées à comprendre les différences socioculturelles susceptibles d’influencer les échanges, les soins ou l’accompagnement.
- Partager avec les professionnels les éléments de contexte culturel utiles à la prise en charge, et signaler les obstacles à l’égalité d’accès aux services.
- Contribuer à un environnement respectueux, sans racisme ni discrimination, en accord avec les principes de MSF.

## **Accueillir, informer et orienter les personnes**

- Accueillir les personnes dans les lieux de répit et de consultation de MSF, créer un lien de confiance et, si nécessaire, recueillir les premières informations de base.
- Faciliter l’orientation et le suivi des personnes vers d’autres structures de santé ou services sociaux lorsque cela est nécessaire.
- Informer les personnes, en lien avec les professionnels concernés, sur le fonctionnement du système de santé et les services disponibles : hébergement, alimentation, transport, accompagnement social ou assistance juridique.
- Participer aux activités collectives proposées, contribuer à l’organisation du lieu d’accueil et veiller à ce qu’il reste adapté et sûr, notamment pour les jeunes enfants accompagnants.

## **Contribuer au suivi des situations et à la compréhension des besoins**

- Participer aux réunions de gestion de cas et aux échanges interdisciplinaires lorsque cela est nécessaire.
- Contribuer aux évaluations, enquêtes et collectes de données sur les enjeux médicaux et humanitaires, avec une attention particulière aux situations de vulnérabilité.
- Assurer une collecte et une saisie fiables des données et transmettre aux équipes les informations pertinentes exprimées par les personnes et les communautés, dans le strict respect de la confidentialité.
- Fournir une interprétation linguistique et interculturelle lors du recueil de témoignages destinés aux actions de communication ou de plaidoyer.
- Contribuer, le cas échéant, aux revues médiatiques et à la création de contenus de communication.

## **Veiller à un accueil sûr et respectueux**

- Surveiller les conditions d’accueil et signaler au responsable tout problème de sécurité concernant les lieux d’activité.
- Veiller à la bonne application des mesures de safeguarding et contribuer à la protection des personnes accompagnées.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes MSF et les partenaires concernés, dans le respect des procédures et des règles de confidentialité.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Niveau d’enseignement secondaire indispensable ; un diplôme en sciences sociales, communication sociale ou enseignement est souhaitable.
- Une formation en médiation interculturelle ou en interprétariat constitue un atout.
- Une expérience en traduction et/ou médiation culturelle est souhaitée.
- Une expérience auprès de publics en situation de précarité, d’adolescents ou de jeunes majeurs, ainsi qu’au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, est appréciée.
- Une connaissance de la protection sociale, de la protection de l’enfance, des dispositifs d’accueil des mineurs non accompagnés et des dynamiques migratoires est souhaitable.

**Qualités :**

- Sens du service, écoute et capacité à créer une relation de confiance.
- Respect des personnes, de leur parcours et de leurs différences culturelles.
- Goût du travail en équipe et de la coopération.
- Capacité d’adaptation et aptitude à travailler dans un environnement exigeant, y compris de nuit.
- Adhésion aux principes et aux valeurs de MSF.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable ; l’anglais est souhaité.
- Maîtrise obligatoire d’au moins une des langues suivantes : tigrinya, amazigh, farsi, somali ou kurde-sorani.
- La connaissance de l’arabe est un atout.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants, notamment Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **2 767,75 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an·
- Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir :** Dès que possible.

*En raison de contraintes administratives liées à la durée du contrat, les candidats doivent déjà disposer d'une autorisation de travail en France (citoyen de l'Union européenne) ou d’un titre de séjour leur permettant de travailler sur le sol français.*

jobs.title: Chief of Communication, P-5, FT, #00089802, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo - WCAR
jobs.description:
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit [our website](https://www.unicef.org/) to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

**For every child,** ***the right to a Future***

The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) stands at a crossroads between immense natural wealth and extraordinary human potential. With an estimated 113 million inhabitants, including 61 million young people under 18 years of age, the DRC boasts one of Africa’s youngest populations - a generation of energy, creativity, and promise capable of shaping a future of peace, innovation, and prosperity. Spanning 2.3 million km², an area comparable to Western Europe, the DRC is Africa’s second-largest country and shares borders with nine nations, making it a natural hub for regional trade, integration, and cooperation. Beneath its soil lie some of the world’s richest mineral and environmental reserves: the Congo Basin rainforest, a vital carbon sink for the planet, and abundant deposits of cobalt, copper, gold, and uranium, which are essential to the global green transition and digital economy. This powerful combination of natural and human capital positions the DRC as a strategic engine for Africa’s sustainable development. However, decades of conflict and instability-particularly in the east-have left deep scars. As of 2024, 25.4 million people, including 14.9 million children, were living amidst violence, disease, and extreme poverty, while 7 million were internally displaced. Ongoing governance challenges and structural constraints continue to hinder progress, and the DRC ranks among the lowest on global development indices. The country hosts the second largest displaced population in the world, with children exposed to heightened risks of violence, abuse, and deprivation, and many lacking access to basic services such as clean water, healthcare, and education. Compounding these challenges, the DRC faces recurrent epidemics including Ebola, cholera, measles, and polio. Despite these adversities, the resilience of Congolese communities remains unwavering. Across the country, youth, women, and local innovators are driving positive change-from peacebuilding and education initiatives to renewable energy solutions and digital-skills programs. If nurtured through sustained investment in education, employment, governance, and innovation, the DRC’s demographic dividend could become the foundation for a new era of stability and shared growth.

In this complex environment, UNICEF continues to play a pivotal not only as a humanitarian actor but as a key development partner and catalyst for systems strengthening and inclusive growth. Through integrated, multi-sectoral programming and strong collaboration with government and partners, UNICEF bridges emergency response with long-term development and resilience-building efforts, ensuring that investments in children translate into sustainable, system-wide results. The DRC’s challenges are undeniable-but so too is its extraordinary potential. With its unparalleled natural endowment and a generation of 61 million young Congolese-motors of hope, peace, and prosperity- the Democratic Republic of the Congo holds the key to a more sustainable, inclusive, and equitable future for Africa and the world. UNICEF DRC is one of the largest and most dynamic country offices globally, with an annual budget of USD 300 million, a team of 366 staff, and six field offices in addition to the national office in Kinshasa. Operating in a context of both significant humanitarian needs and growing development opportunities, the office has recently undergone restructuring to enhance efficiency and deepen engagement with communities and government partners.

**How can you make a difference?**

The Communication and Advocacy Section, comprising six fixed-term staff and led by a P-5 Chief of Communication, plays a pivotal role in shaping UNICEF’s visibility, partnerships, and public engagement. Its work covers media engagement, supporting programmes teams, organizing World Children’s Day events, and younth engagement on environmental and climate change.

**Key accountabilities and duties & tasks:**

1. **Communication strategy:** Ensure that the Country Office has a clear communication strategy and associated work plan to support the country programme objectives and get children’s issues into the public domain, strengthen political will in support of UNICEF's mission and objectives, and enhance the organization’s credibility and brand.
2. **Media relations:** Ensure that the Country Office has a well-managed country communication team that maintains and continually develops a contact list of journalists and media outlets covering all media – print, TV, radio, web etc. – and a successful process of communicating and maintaining regular contact and close collaboration with the media to communicate the story of UNICEF's cooperation to a wider audience. New ways are identified to increase positive exposure and leverage that prominence for new opportunities for UNICEF.
3. **Communication, networking and partnerships:** Manage a country communication team to ensure that the Country Office has a well maintained and continually developed contact list of individuals, groups, organizations and fora (including business), whose support is essential to/can assist in achieving the advocacy and communication objectives of the communication strategy. Network is developed, strengthened and maintained with the UN Country Team, UN communication counterparts and high-level counterparts in key partner organizations.
4. **Celebrities and special events:** Ensure that the Country Office has a well-managed national celebrity relations programme with a well maintained and continually developed contact list of appropriate, nationally-known personalities who have been identified, engaged and support UNICEF’s efforts and who actively participate in special events and activities that support country programme goals. Among these high-profile individuals a handful are identified whose recognition level extends beyond national borders and co-ordinate closely with DOC and the regional office in extending their impact and use beyond national borders.
5. **Global priorities and campaigns:** In addition to local/national campaigns, ensure that the Country Office has an effective process in place for integrating and taking action on UNICEF’s global communications priorities and campaigns, both disseminating these elements in a locally-appropriate way, as well as providing/enabling coverage of the work in the country for global use.
6. **Resource mobilization support:** Ensure that global and country level fund-raising are supported by effective advocacy and communication strategy and activities.
7. **Management:** Ensure that the human resources (the communication team) and financial resources (budget planning, management and monitoring) for the communication section of the Country Office are both effectively managed and optimally used.
8. **Monitoring and evaluation:** Ensure that communication baselines are established against which the objectives of the communication strategy are regularly evaluated; analysis is undertaken to continuously improve the effectiveness of communication strategy, approach and activities; results and reports are prepared and shared on a timely basis.
9. **Capacity building and support:** Ensure that the Representative and the country programme team are provided with professional expertise and advice on all aspects of communication as required; opportunities for development among the country communication team and other colleagues are identified and addressed; opportunities to build communication capacity among media and other relevant partners are identified and addressed.
10. **Advisory support and communication for strategic results:** Implementation of UNICEF programme (regional) plans, ensuring communication on gender and equity issues are mainstreamed across all programmes.

If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: [JD\_Chief\_of\_Communication\_P5.pdf](https://secure.dc7.pageuppeople.com/apply/TransferRichTextFile.ashx?sData=UFUtVjMt6jdqY1Or_bNHUh8zq6eggtcaQWvdrR9e3rc3qmiQwEGUW0ineUUy-9TQYA3n63cwI85G6kQ1mDl7Idd5KufyGUMp2Nx2IhrP2U395RcReD22qyqqDRO1m_QLcOuU8MWo3xyeeYLGd3HmpRLf6btcxQ%7e%7e)

**To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…**

***Minimum requirements:***

- **Education**: Advanced university degree in Communication, Journalism, Public Relations or other related fields of disciplines.
- **Work Experience**: Ten (10) years of progressively responsible and relevant professional work experience. International and national work experience in both developed and developing countries. Professional experience in communication, print, broadcast, new media. Background/familiarity with Emergency situations.
- **Skills**: Candidates should demonstrate experience in global advocacy engagement, partnership engagement and maintenance, global and local media relations, monitoring and evaluation, and B2B engagement.
- **Language Requirements**: Fluency in French and English are required.

***Desirables:***

- Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language is an asset.
- Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts.

**For every Child, you demonstrate...**

UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: [UNICEF Values](https://www.unicef.org/careers/get-prepared#Values)

jobs.title: Consortium Manager South Sudan Juba
jobs.description:
**Background:**

NRC works to protect the rights of displaced and vulnerable people during crisis and meet immediate humanitarian needs, prevent further displacement, and contribute to durable solutions. Through our mobile emergency response capacity, we provide lifesaving multisectoral assistance to crisis affected populations in hard-to-reach areas across South Sudan. In areas throughout the country where we have established operations, we ensure that displacement affected people are safe, can exercise their rights, access quality services and protection and secure durable solutions. To that end, we contribute to safe and stable environment needed to allow for return and reintegration or integration of displaced communities. We do this through advocacy, coordination, and collaboration, as well as integrated and multi-sectoral long-term interventions.

In South Sudan, NRC established in 2004 and provides humanitarian assistance and supports durable solutions with integrated and multi-sectoral long-term interventions in six core competencies: Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Protection from Violence, Education, WASH and Shelter. In line with NRC global direction, our WASH and Shelter programmes are transitioning from mainly humanitarian response to support communities with more sustainable water systems and sanitation facilities in response to securing lasting solutions. Also, NRC has the ambition to grow its urban programming to facilitate durable solutions for the swelling urban population in South Sudan.

**What you will do:**

NRC South Sudan leads an EU-funded Education Agri-TVET Consortium in partnership with a wide network of both national and international partners. The Agri-skills for Resilient, Inclusive, and Sustainable Economies (ARISE) Consortium aims to bridge the critical skills gap in South Sudan’s agricultural sector by delivering competency-based Agri Value Chain TVET skills aligned to profitable value chain commodities being developed by Green Resilience Economy partners across targeted states in South Sudan. ARISE will strengthen South Sudan’s Agri–value chain TVET system so youth, especially girls/young women and displacement-affected learners, gain market-relevant, green and transferable skills that lead to decent work and viable self-employment. The action is designed to complement the EU’s Green and Resilient Economy (GRE) investments by building a reliable skills-to-jobs pipeline into existing value chain and MSME ecosystems, rather than duplicating market systems or production programming.

The Consortium Manager will oversee the Consortium and be responsible for their overall management. This position is responsible for strategic advice on the management and direction of the consortium programme(s), the operational management and implementation of the project(s), including project implementation in terms of coordinating delivery and the inputs from consortium members. The Consortium Manager will facilitate the strategic development of consortium programmes, responsible for forging strong relationships with and between consortium members, donor(s) and other relevant stakeholders, as well as ensuring compliance with donor contractual requirements, and NRC and/or Consortium internal procedures.

General Responsibilities:

1. Compliance and adherence to NRC policies, CC tools, handbooks and guidelines.
2. Provide overall direction and leadership of the Consortium to ensure seamless operations, leveraging complementarity among partners
3. Provide systematic training and build capacity of technical staff where relevant.

Specific responsibilities:

- Coordinate with consortium members to ensure high-quality implementation of activities, compliance with donor and consortium rules, and accountability to beneficiaries.
- Oversee day-to-day management of the project, including planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation and budget spending, ensuring project is always on scope and schedule
- Represent the Consortium towards relevant stakeholders, including national authorities, donors and counterparts, promoting the best interests of Consortium partners
- Line Manage and supervise the work of the Consortium Management Unit; carry out any needed recruitments, including for consultants
- Lead the consultations, design and preparation of the next phase of the Consortium based on evidenced needs, donor expectations and drawing from partners’ diverse expertise

Please refer to the full [Job Description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBQiZTWSdoeR7iyfO4fnOG0Acj-7BedNwjsRTUIkAUvUos?e=gLQcoH) as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum BA in relevant areas preferably
- Minimum 5 years of humanitarian experience across multiple context with at least 2 years’ experience of youth programmes
- At least 3 years project management experience of managing multi-million (EURO) projects;
- Experience in consortium management or extensive involvement in a consortium, with a multi-year duration
- Experience developing training tools, manuals, information management systems for humanitarian action and accountability to affected people.
- Self-motivated and confident communicator, with experience in giving briefings and presentations.
- Strong inter-personal skills, working well both in teams and independently
- Able to work under pressure and good at timely decision making
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal.
- Preferred experience or knowledge of Sudan context.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Juba, South Sudan
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **international contract.**
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
- **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
- **Your updated Cover Letter.**
- **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
- **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for all international candidates.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Distribution Coordinator
jobs.description:
Northern Lights Aid (NLA) is a small grassroots NGO in Kavala, Northern Greece, that focuses on improving the quality of life of people living in the nearby Perigiali Refugee Camp, as well as other vulnerable communities in the local area. We provide material support through a free store, and operate a Community Centre where we offer informal education and recreational activities.

We are looking for a Distribution Coordinator to join us in Kavala on the **7th of January 2027** for a minimum of 4 months.

The role of the Distribution Coordinator is to ensure the smooth execution of all distribution efforts, including the daily operations in our free store as well as the weekly distribution of baby items. The Distribution Coordinator acts as the central point of oversight for all distribution activities and is involved in stock management, documentation, and the guidance of volunteers. They are dedicated to creating a welcoming and dignified atmosphere for all ages, genders and backgrounds across all distribution operations.

## Responsibilities:

### Coordination of daily distribution efforts

- Facilitate a dignified and efficient experience for all community members according to the organization’s project guidelines, policies and values
- Ensure all community members receive items in a fair and consistent manner
- Respond to daily challenges such as complaints or special requests from community members
- Track daily project attendance
- Ensure information regarding store opening hours and distribution activities is available, accessible to people of all backgrounds, and shared with community members through appropriate channels
- Collaborate with the Community Centre Coordinator to align efforts and respond to community needs comprehensively

### **Management of stock levels and spaces**

- Sort and organize incoming donations
- Monitor stock levels
- Assist in developing procurement approaches and in exploring potential collaborations
- Optimize storage layout and maintain a clear and organized system in the warehouse
- Ensure the cleanliness and tidiness of the store and storage area

### **Support of volunteer management**

- Communicate daily tasks with volunteers and ensure tasks are completed
- Welcome new volunteers, conduct project inductions, and follow up to ensure clear understanding of the space, their role, and their responsibilities
- Lead daily volunteer debriefs to gather input, address concerns, and encourage suggestions
- Pass on needed information regarding volunteer management including wellbeing concerns and potential conflicts/tensions within the team to the Field Manager

### **Report to Field Manager**

- Engage in weekly meetings with the Field Manager to keep them informed about project developments
- Communicate shortages and inventory stock needs
- Draft quarterly reports in collaboration with the Field Manager
- Keep track of and share feedback from community members
- Alert the Field Manager about behaviour from volunteers or community members that violates guidelines, and report safeguarding concerns appropriately
- Participate in project development by collaborating with the Field Manager and Director of Operations to evaluate NLA’s capacity to make changes to the project

## Requirements:

### **Required Skills**

- Highly organized and proactive approach to work
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to respond calmly in challenging situations
- Politically and culturally sensitive with the ability to act with patience, tact, and diplomacy
- Ability to work well both independently and cooperatively within a team
- Ability to demonstrate clear professional boundaries with community members
- Good management abilities and capacity to take on responsibilities
- Strong commitment to the values of NLA and dedication to supporting displaced people
- Fluency in English (knowledge of Arabic, Farsi, Turkish, or Kurmanji is an asset)

### **Relevant Experiences**

- Previous experience working with displaced people
- Volunteer or professional experience in project coordination
- Strong interest in, or educational background/professional experience related to logistics, distributions, retail, or stock management

### **Other**

- Minimum time commitment: 4 months
- Minimum age: 23 years old
- Ability to reside legally in the EU for the full duration of the commitment
- Starting date: 7th of January (handover period mid-December, preferably in person)

**This is a volunteering position. NLA will provide free accommodation in a shared flat and a small monthly stipend.**

jobs.title: GRANTS EXPERT - YEMEN
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Under the supervision of the Under the supervision of the Head of Department - Grants and Partnerships, your mission will be to provide dedicated support to the Grants and Partnerships Department.
More specifically, your responsibilities will be as follows:
Grants ManagementSupport the planning, coordination, and submission of donor reports in line with contractual deadlines (ECHO DRR, ECHO Consortium, GAC).
Maintain updated grants tracking tools (GFU) and reporting schedules.
Support the contractual follow-up of projects and ensure compliance with donor and ACF requirements.
Provide ad hoc support for partnership follow-up within the framework of ongoing projects.
Proposal DevelopmentContribute to the development of concept notes, proposals, budgets, and supporting annexes for the ECHO, GAC, FCDO and Sida proposals.
Follow up on proposal development processes with identified partners, when applicable.
Support donor mapping and fundraising intelligence for the Yemen Country Strategy.

Profile :

You hold a degree in international development or a related field, you have at least 3 years of experience in in Grants management, proposal development, donor reporting and a previous experience with ACF (field and/or HQ).
You have worked with major institutional donors (ECHO, BMZ, CDCS, FIFSAN, Sida, FCDO), with a successful track record of drafting writing and submitting funded proposals. You also have experience leading new business development efforts, including program design, proposal writing, partner relationship development.
You have knowledge of Project Management cycle, tools and are familiar with budget development.
Well-organized, attentive to detail, and able to manage multiple tasks concurrently, you have also good written and oral communications skills and demonstrated ability to write and edit reports under deadline pressure.
You master English (written and spoken).
Additional language skills in Arabic and previous experience in Yemen are considered an asset.

Conditions d'emploi

Fixed term contract under French legislation: 3 months
Monthly gross salary from 2597 to 2968euros upon experience, including 13th month
Reimbursement of the pension insurance for non-French citizens: 16% of the gross monthly salary
Annual salary increase: 6% increase after and each 12 months of continuous contract
Monthly per diem and living allowance: 730 USD net, field paid
Monthly country allowance: 450euros
Child allowance: 1500euros per year per child present in the country of origin (maximum 6000euros/year)
Transportation and accommodation: Coverage of transportation costs and guest house
Medical coverage: ACF covers 100% of the health and repatriation insurance agreement fees, for your medical expenses (as well as your dependents if you have a family post), and up to 1 month after the end of your contract.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to the International President
jobs.description:
**Location:** Geneva

**Contract:** Permanent, full-time contract

**Starting date:** As soon as possible

**Deadline to apply:** 13th of November 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**MSF INTERNATIONAL**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and other branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**JOB PURPOSE**

The IP Executive Assistant (EA) provides high-level strategic, organisational and administrative support to the International President, enabling effective leadership, governance, decision-making and execution of the IP’s responsibilities.

The EA supports far beyond administrative coordination - they act as a strategic partner, anticipating needs, streamlining decision making, and ensuring the IP’s time is focused on the highest impact priorities.

The postholder will pre-emptively maintain and refine internal processes while coordinating internal and external resources to expedite workflows, and to plan and orchestrate work to ensure priorities are met, organisational goals are achieved, and best practices are upheld.

**CONTEXT**

The Executive Assistant accompanies the IP at the heart of the organisation, providing a pivotal role in creating the conditions that allow the IP to perform at their highest level within the complex globally interdependent MSF network.

This means clear organisation of priorities, managing multiple schedules, preparing briefing materials, coordinating cross functional communication, and acting as a trusted point of contact for internal and external stakeholders.

It involves anticipating needs before they arise, filtering information intelligently, and ensuring priorities stay aligned with organisational goals.

The postholder becomes an extension of the IP’s leadership presence, helping maintain momentum, clarity, and efficiency across the wider team. As such there is a business requirement for the post holder to be a visible presence and point of contact for the IP and to be physically based in the Geneva office.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**1. Provides executive support**

- Serve as a trusted advisor and thought partner to the IP, helping to prioritise initiatives, manage competing demands, and maintain organisational alignment.
- Anticipate needs and proactively address issues before they escalate.
- Exercise sound judgment in all interactions, decisions, and requests for support.
- Conduct research and synthesise information to inform decision-making.
- Track key initiatives, decisions, commitments, and follow-up actions arising from the IP’s engagement with stakeholders and maintain visibility on progress.
- Support the proactive planning of IP business in close partnership with the Office of the IB and ISG.

**2. Organises and streamlines administrative processes and planning to ensure focus on deadlines and deliverables**
- Manage the IP’s diary proactively and coordinate travel arrangements in collaboration with the IB Assistant.
- Act as a gatekeeper, protecting the IP’s time and ensuring focus on priority areas.
- Coordinate meetings and executive-level events.
- Lead or support cross-functional projects, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.
- Identify and refine core processes to strengthen efficiency and coordination.

**3. Ensures relevant, timely and quality communication and documentation is created for, on behalf of and available to the IP**
- Prepare speeches, briefing materials, agendas, and follow-up actions for internal and external meetings.
- Draft, edit, and proofread high-level correspondence, presentations, and reports.
- Coordinate internal communications on behalf of the IP, escalating important issues and facilitating timely communication of senior decisions.
- Maintain records effectively to ensure they are available on demand at short notice when required.

**4. Manages internal and external relationships**
- Build strong relationships across the organisation and with external stakeholders.
- Act with professionalism, discretion, and emotional intelligence.
- Handle sensitive information with the highest level of confidentiality.

**SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it to protect others.

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Experience and Knowledge**

- Extensive experience working as an Executive Assistant to Director / CEO level.
- Demonstrable experience of managing complex, dynamic calendars with an emphasis on strategic time allocation.
- Excellent English, other languages asset (for example French, Arabic)
- Experience in governance, international organisations, NGOs or complex multi-entity organisations an added advantage.
- Comfortable coordinating cross-functional teams and liaising with stakeholders at all levels, including external partners and senior executives.
- Experience preparing briefings, reports, presentations, and meeting materials with a high level of accuracy.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, able to draft clear, concise, and professional correspondence.
- Experience in the practical use of personal IT equipment and Microsoft Office 365 suite. The ability to effectively collaborate and communicate within a hybrid working environment utilising Teams, SharePoint, One Drive and Viva Engage. An aptitude for quickly learning new software and systems.

**Professional skills**

- Organisation and autonomy
- Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to anticipate needs and plan.
- Strong time-management skills and an ability to coordinate multiple concurrent projects.
- Skilled at filtering information, prioritising tasks, and maintaining momentum across multiple workstreams.
- Ability to work in a disciplined and organised fashion, under pressure, with conflicting priorities and across time zones.
- Confident decision-making and the ability to act autonomously when required.

**Personal skills**

- Proactive mindset with a natural inclination to take ownership and improve processes.
- Flexible team player, willing to adapt to changes, and confident tackling unfamiliar challenges across multiple domains of knowledge/experience.
- High level of discretion, judgement, and emotional intelligence.
- Calm, composed, and solutions focused under pressure.
- Relationship builder who can represent the IP with professionalism and warmth.
- Adaptable, resilient, and comfortable navigating ambiguity.
- High integrity and a strong sense of responsibility.
- Thrives in a role that blends strategic support with hands on execution.
- Enjoys being a trusted partner who enables leadership effectiveness.
- Values confidentiality, reliability, and excellence in delivery.
- An enquiring, curious mind with a demonstrable ability to search for answers, make connections and navigate new situations and people.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

jobs.title: Mission France - Responsable des activités de travail social F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de travail social pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la personne responsable de la protection de l’unité migrations, vous concevrez, superviserez et suivrez les activités de travail social du projet. Vous encadrerez les travailleur·ses sociaux·les, contribuerez à la stratégie de protection et veillerez à la qualité des accompagnements proposés.

Ce poste associe pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe et intervention directe sur le terrain : vous consacrerez notamment 30 % de votre temps aux activités de travail social, aux maraudes et à l’« aller-vers ».

**Principales responsabilités :**

Piloter Définir et piloter la stratégie de travail social et de protection

- Co-définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de travail social du projet, en cohérence avec les orientations opérationnelles et le cadre de travail social de MSF.
- Développer les activités autour de la gestion de cas, du soutien social aux patient·es, du lien social de première ligne et des interventions communautaires.
- Analyser le contexte et les déterminants sociaux de la santé afin d’identifier les vulnérabilités récurrentes, les situations de violence, les phénomènes de déplacement et d’exclusion, ainsi que les besoins critiques d’assistance et de protection.
- Contribuer à la définition des objectifs et des interventions de protection, notamment en matière de signalement et de prévention des risques.
- Documenter les restrictions d’accès aux services et analyser les obstacles rencontrés afin de proposer des pistes d’action et de plaidoyer en lien avec la référente médicale en migration et la mission MSF France.

**Garantir un accompagnement social de qualité et gérer les situations complexes**

- Superviser les parcours d’accompagnement social : accueil, évaluation des besoins, élaboration et mise en œuvre du plan d’intervention, orientation sécurisée, suivi et clôture des situations.
- Veiller à la prise en charge des besoins sociaux critiques, dans le périmètre du projet, par un accompagnement direct ou une orientation vers des services adaptés.
- Accompagner les équipes dans la gestion des situations complexes et intervenir directement dans les cas sensibles, notamment lorsqu’il existe des risques élevés de violence ou qu’un mineur non accompagné est concerné.
- Organiser des temps réguliers de concertation autour des situations suivies, afin de partager les difficultés et de construire des réponses adaptées avec les autres disciplines.
- Favoriser le pouvoir d’agir des personnes accompagnées en leur donnant une information claire sur leurs droits, les services disponibles, les critères d’accès et les démarches pertinentes.
- Contribuer à un environnement de soins sûr, digne et confidentiel, qui respecte les droits des patient·es et facilite l’accès aux mécanismes de retours et de plaintes.

**Développer le travail social communautaire et les partenariats**

- Participer aux maraudes et aux activités d’« aller-vers » pour identifier les besoins sociaux, les vulnérabilités et les risques de protection au sein des communautés.
- Développer, avec les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de médiation, des interventions pluridisciplinaires visant à renforcer les facteurs de protection et de résilience.
- Construire et actualiser une cartographie des services sociaux, des associations, des partenaires institutionnels et des dispositifs communautaires présents sur la zone du projet.
- Développer des relations de coopération avec les partenaires et suivre l’accessibilité, la disponibilité et la qualité des services proposés.
- Renforcer la coordination et l’orientation des personnes vers les dispositifs adaptés, en portant une attention particulière aux situations de violence, notamment sexuelle, et aux possibilités de prise en charge.
- Contribuer à la surveillance communautaire et à l’analyse des problématiques de protection rencontrées sur le terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer l’équipe**

- Encadrer les travailleur·ses sociaux·les et organiser les plannings en fonction des différentes activités : maraudes, entretiens individuels et activités collectives.
- Développer les compétences de l’équipe par la formation, le coaching, la supervision et le partage de pratiques.
- Identifier les besoins de développement professionnel et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences, en lien avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Former et sensibiliser les équipes aux questions de protection, de gestion de cas, de conduite d’entretien et d’orientation.
- Contribuer aux processus de recrutement, de formation et d’évaluation des équipes concernées, en collaboration avec les RH.
- Assurer la continuité des activités en apportant un soutien opérationnel et, si nécessaire, en remplaçant les membres de l’équipe absents.
- Veiller au bien-être de l’équipe et favoriser une coopération étroite avec les autres pôles du projet.

**Assurer Suivre les activités, analyser les données et garantir la qualité**

- Superviser la collecte, l’enregistrement et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de travail social et de protection.
- Suivre les indicateurs de résultats et produire un reporting régulier permettant d’identifier les tendances, les besoins émergents et les difficultés d’accès aux services.
- Documenter les situations et les tendances en matière de protection afin d’alimenter l’analyse opérationnelle et les actions de plaidoyer de MSF.
- Développer et adapter les outils et processus de travail social aux besoins du projet.
- Garantir le respect du cadre de travail social de MSF, des règles de confidentialité, de la protection des données et des exigences légales et éthiques.
- Planifier et coordonner les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires aux activités, en lien avec les départements support.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme français ou étranger de travailleur·se social·e, avec au moins trois années de formation théorique et pratique.
- Au moins trois ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes de travail social ou de domaines similaires : protection, accompagnement psychosocial, violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre, etc.
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe.
- Une expérience dans un contexte sanitaire, humanitaire, de protection ou de migration est fortement souhaitée.
- Une expérience avérée en gestion de cas ou en protection dans un contexte d’urgence constitue un atout.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Capacités d’analyse et aptitude à transformer les constats du terrain en réponses adaptées.
- Sens de l’organisation, orientation vers les résultats et exigence de qualité.
- Aptitude à manager, accompagner et développer une équipe.
- Esprit d’équipe, coopération et capacité à travailler en pluridisciplinarité.
- Sens du service et approche centrée sur la personne.
- Capacité à développer des partenariats et à construire des relations de confiance.
- Gestion du stress, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation à des environnements changeants et difficiles.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise courante du français indispensable.
- Bonne maîtrise de l’anglais à l’oral.
- La connaissance d’autres langues est fortement souhaitée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 425,87 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an· Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo.

**Poste à pourvoir :** 4 janvier 2027.

*En raison de contraintes administratives liées à la durée du contrat, les candidats doivent déjà disposer d'une autorisation de travail en France (citoyen de l'Union européenne) ou d’un titre de séjour leur permettant de travailler sur le sol français.*

jobs.title: Program Officer (Al Jazeera State, Sudan)
jobs.description:
**About CIVIC**

Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) is an international non-governmental organization (INGO) with offices around the world working to improve protection for civilians caught in conflict zones. CIVIC envisions a world in which no civilian is harmed in conflict. Our mission is to support communities affected by conflict in their quest for protection and strengthen the resolve and capacity of armed actors to prevent and respond to civilian harm. We are advocates who believe that no civilian caught in conflict should be ignored, and advisors who provide practical solutions to preventing and responding to civilian harm. Learn more at [civiliansinconflict.org.](https://www.civiliansinconflict.org/)

**About the Position**

CIVIC is seeking highly qualified applicants for the position of Program Officer – PROCIV Program, who will support the implementation of a new initiative on Humanitarian Dialogue and Humanitarian Diplomacy (PROCIV). The Program Officer will be part of the Sudan country team, working closely with local civil society, armed actor interlocutors, and regional/international policy stakeholders under the guidance of the Country Director and Senior Program Manager. This is a full-time position with a one-year contract.

***Job Purpose:*** Coordinate, implement, and support all activities under the PROCIV project focused on humanitarian dialogue, civilian protection, and evidence-based humanitarian diplomacy.

LOCATION: Al Jazeera State, Sudan

TRAVEL: As needed throughout Sudan

REPORTING TO: Senior Program Officer.

STAFF REPORTING: N/A

**Key Responsibilities**

- Support implementation of the PROCIV humanitarian dialogue and diplomacy activities, ensuring alignment with project outcomes and CIVIC methodologies.
- Coordinate protection risk analyses, civilian self-protection assessments, and mapping of local partners and community structures.
- Facilitate relationships with local CSOs, ERRs, community leaders, native administration, and other key stakeholders engaged in humanitarian dialogue.
- Support delivery of mentorship sessions for civil society leaders and community actors on humanitarian dialogue, negotiation, and protection priorities.
- Assist in convening confidential consultations with armed actors and authorities to create openings for constructive engagement on PoC and humanitarian access.
- Coordinate planning, logistics, and documentation for dialogue sessions, workshops, training, and joint analysis meetings, working closely with Operations.
- Support evidence generation for policy briefs, protection analysis, and outcome documentation, contributing to national, regional, and international advocacy.
- Ensure gender-sensitive and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout all activities, including representation of women, youth, and marginalized groups.
- Facilitate sharing of best practices between PROCIV partners, community representatives, and colleagues across the three target geographies (Sudan, DRC, Yemen).
- Coordinate data collection and serve as MEAL focal point for the PROCIV project, ensuring timely reporting on outputs, outcomes, and lessons learned.
- Maintain strong relationships with local partners, humanitarian actors, and coordination structures, ensuring complementarity with ICRC, OCHA, and protection clusters.
- Prepare timely reports, support documents, and updates to the Senior Program Manager, Country Director, and donor when requested.
- Represent CIVIC at relevant NGO, community, and stakeholder meetings to promote collaboration and humanitarian dialogue efforts.
- Perform any other duties as required to further the organization’s mission and the successful delivery of PROCIV activities in Sudan.

**Requirements**

- A Bachelor's Degree in international affairs, political science, conflict studies, development studies, or a related field.
- Minimum 5 years of relevant full-time experience in protection, humanitarian dialogue, civil society engagement, or program coordination in conflict-affected settings.
- Experience working in Sudan and deep knowledge of the national humanitarian landscape strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to CIVIC’s mission, humanitarian principles, and protection of civilians.
- Fluency in English and Arabic is mandatory.

**Qualities Sought**

- Strong understanding of civilian protection, humanitarian access, and conflict dynamics in Sudan.
- Experience engaging with local civil society, community structures, and humanitarian stakeholders, ideally in sensitive political and security environments.
- Demonstrated ability to work with community leaders, women’s groups, youth networks, and marginalized groups in participatory and inclusive ways.
- Ability to think analytically and strategically, including identifying opportunities for humanitarian dialogue and strengthening local protection arrangements.
- Poise, flexibility, discretion, and mature judgment in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
- Excellent organizational skills, self-motivation, and ability to deliver high-quality outputs with minimal supervision.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to produce clear analysis and documentation.
- Experience representing organizations in complex humanitarian or political settings is preferred.

**Additional Details**

**Application Deadline: November 6, 2026**

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. ***Shortlisted candidates will receive an email invitation from TestGorilla to submit their resume. Please complete this step promptly to ensure your candidacy is fully considered.***

CIVIC is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: CIVIC does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and does not pay placement fees for candidates submitted by agencies other than its approved partners.
