jobs.title: International Programme Director Tearfund Netherlands
jobs.description:
## Utrecht, 0.9-1.0FTE

## About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and impact-driven International Programme Director to provide strategic leadership for our humanitarian and development portfolio. The International Programme Director serves on the Executive Team and is responsible for strategy, programme quality & oversight, financial & risk management, external representation & partnerships, Institutional Funding and Business Development, impact and MEAL. The IP director reports to the CEO.

The International Programme Team oversees implementation of programmes across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East. The International Programme Team currently consists of 10+ employees with their own country-specific expertise and responsibilities. As International Programme Director, you are the primary point of contact for team leaders on programme and HR matters, fostering collaboration and ensuring the achievement of organisational objectives.

## We are looking for a leader who:

- Has substantial senior leadership experience in international development, humanitarian response, including at least five years of work experience in the majority world.
- Has a proven track record of leading and developing managers and multidisciplinary teams.
- Demonstrates a strong track record in developing, overseeing and strengthening complex international programmes, partnerships and organisational strategies.
- Has experience managing institutional donor relationships and donor-funded programme portfolios, including strategic engagement with governments, multilateral institutions, foundations and humanitarian donors.
- Brings significant experience in fragile, conflict-affected and humanitarian contexts and is able to navigate complex and rapidly changing environments.
- Holds a master's degree or an equivalent combination of education, knowledge and relevant professional experience.
- Demonstrates strong strategic and analytical thinking and is able to translate organisational vision into priorities, partnerships, programmes and measurable impact.
- Has experience in financial oversight, organisational governance, risk management, safeguarding, accountability and quality management within an international context.
- Is committed to strengthening locally led development and humanitarian action and values equitable partnerships with local organisations, churches and communities.
- Is an inspiring and empowering people leader who develops talent, builds trust, fosters collaboration and creates conditions for teams and individuals to thrive.
- Is able to represent Tearfund credibly and confidently in national and international networks, consortia, donor relationships and strategic partnerships.
- Possesses strong communication and influencing skills in fluent English and Dutch. Candidates who are not yet fluent in Dutch should be willing to develop working proficiency after appointment.
- Is willing to assume responsibility during emergencies, critical incidents and organisational crises, including occasional availability outside regular working hours when required.

## What we offer

As International Programme Director, you can expect:

- A challenging and varied position where you can make a meaningful contribution, with plenty of scope for personal initiative and professional growth.
- An international, inspiring, and dynamic workplace, offering a professional, collaborative, and value-driven working environment.
- Regular travel to our programme countries.
- A modern and flexible office environment in Utrecht.
- An annual contract, with the intention of extending.
- The position is graded at Staff Officer VIII, Salary Scale 10 (max € 6645,21) based on a full-time contract of 40 hours per week.

## Who we are

Tearfund Netherlands is a Christian developmental and humanitarian response organisation. We alleviate poverty around the world by ‘Doing Justice Together’ with supporters, churches, Christian non-governmental organisations, and local communities.

We believe poverty is rooted in broken relationships: with God, with ourselves, with others, and with creation. These broken relationships often lead to injustice and prevent people from reaching their full potential. We collaborate with and strengthen local organisations equipping them where needed to help restore relationships and bring about lasting, holistic change. Tearfund Netherlands delivers a distinctive community asset based approach to sustainable development, resilience building and peacebuilding. Through our extensive network of local and international partners, we are also well positioned to provide rapid and effective humanitarian assistance. This enables us to respond to both natural and human-made crises across the majority world through locally led action, complemented by international NGO support where needed. Our work is funded through partnerships with the Dutch government, the European Union, foundations, companies, churches, and a loyal and growing community of private supporters.

Tearfund Netherlands is headquartered in Utrecht and has around 50 employees. The annual budget in 2027 will be ca. €23 million, the majority of which will be spent on humanitarian aid, development and peacebuilding around the world.

*People's safety is very important to Tearfund and we therefore do not accept any form of abuse. Requesting references will therefore be part of the selection process. Because Tearfund is a signatory of the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, we do a reference check regarding integrity and a 'Statement of Conduct' (related to misconduct such as sexual abuse) and it is mandatory to sign a Personal Declaration of Integrity. Applying for a recent Certificate of Conduct (Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag, VOG) and signing a Code of Conduct are mandatory when entering employment at Tearfund.*

*You wholeheartedly agree with Tearfund's vision and mission and you are motivated to demonstrate and commit to it. In applying so, you endorse the international minimum operating standards ‘Protection from sexual exploitation and abuse’ (PSEA). Available upon request via HR@tearfund.nl.*

Visit our website [www.tearfund.nl](http://www.tearfund.nl/) for more information about Tearfund. Acquisition regarding this vacancy is not appreciated.

jobs.title: Consultant to Produce Explainer Video on the Civic Space in Nigeria
jobs.description:
**Scope:** Consultant to Produce Explainer Video on the Civic Space in Nigeria

**Location:** Abuja, Nigeria/Remote
**Application Close**: October 28, 2026

Global Rights is an international human rights and governance capacity-building non-governmental organization. We work with local activists in Africa to promote and protect the rights of marginalized populations. For more than 30 years, we have worked to build the capacity of underserved communities in Nigeria and build platforms for participatory governance, working on a wide range of cross cutting issues including: women’s rights, access to justice, natural resource governance, climate change and human rights; civic space strengthening; and security and human rights.
Global Rights works at the intersection of the protection, promotion and fulfilment of human rights through good governance. Mandatorily, women’s rights, access to remedies, and disabilities issues, are focal threads woven through the fabric of all our programs.

**Background**

Nigeria’s civic space is facing growing pressure from legal, regulatory and administrative measures that risk restricting the ability of civil society organizations (CSOs), human rights defenders, journalists and citizens to operate freely, organize collectively, and hold public institutions accountable. While regulation is necessary to promote transparency and accountability, the use or expansion of regulatory powers in ways that undermine freedom of association, expression and peaceful assembly raises serious concerns about the protection of fundamental rights and the sustainability of democratic participation.

These concerns are heightened by existing legal frameworks and proposed legislation that could expand government oversight of civil society, impose additional obligations on organizations, or create opportunities for arbitrary restrictions on their activities. The Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020, particularly provisions relating to the regulatory powers of the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) over incorporated trustees, has been the subject of legal contestation over the limits of regulatory authority and the autonomy of civil society organizations. More recently, proposed legislation, including the Foreign Aid Bill, has generated concerns about the potential implications of increased state oversight of foreign funding, organizational independence, and the ability of CSOs to carry out legitimate human rights and governance work.

Beyond the provisions of individual laws and bills, the cumulative effect of restrictive legal and regulatory measures can create an environment in which civil society organizations face uncertainty, increased compliance burdens, and potential interference in their operations. Such an environment may discourage civic participation, weaken independent advocacy, constrain access to resources, and limit the ability of marginalized communities to organize and seek redress. These risks have particular implications for organizations working on accountability, human rights, gender equality, natural resource governance, and the protection of vulnerable and underserved populations.

As part of Global Rights' broader efforts to strengthen civic space and promote informed public engagement, Global Rights is producing a new edition of its [**We No Go Gree**](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZXvVYMe6oOY) video series, using ongoing legal and policy developments as an entry point to examine the broader challenges facing civic space in Nigeria. The episode, **We No Go Gree 104**, will explore how existing laws and proposed legislation may affect the operating environment for civil society, the constitutional rights of citizens, and the ability of organizations to contribute to democratic governance and public accountability. The CAMA litigation, undertaken by Global Rights in partnership with the Network of University Legal Aid Institutions (NULAI) Nigeria, will serve as one illustrative example of the legal and constitutional questions arising from the regulation of civil society.

The video will translate complex legal and policy issues into accessible, engaging content for a wider public audience. It will be published on Global Rights’ YouTube channel and repurposed into shorter clips for dissemination across its social media platforms, with the aim of raising awareness, encouraging informed public discussion, and strengthening public understanding of the importance of protecting civic space in Nigeria.

**Goal**
To increase public awareness and understanding of the CAMA litigation and its implications for civic space, civil society organizations, and the regulatory environment in Nigeria through accessible and engaging digital media content.

**Objectives**

- To explain the CAMA litigation and the specific legal and regulatory issues under consideration in accessible language.
- To increase public understanding of how the regulation of incorporated trustees and CSOs affects civic space and civil society operations.
- Promote informed public discussion on the constitutional limits of regulatory powers and the protection of civic space.

**Scope of Work**

- Develop a concept, narrative and script for the episode in consultation with Global Rights.
- Explain the CAMA regulatory framework and the broader questions it raises about the powers of regulatory authorities and the autonomy of civil society organizations.
- Explore wider civic-space issues, including the implications of proposed legislation such as the Foreign Aid Bill.
- Produce a video (We No Go Gree 104) using a presenter-led format supported by infographics, text overlays and other visual elements, as well as shorter clips for social media distribution.
- Identify and engage a suitable influencer or content creator with a relevant audience to present the video.

**Key Issues to Be Addressed**
The video should address the following questions:

1. The regulatory framework established by CAMA 2020 for NGOs in Nigeria.
2. The powers of regulatory authorities under CAMA and the implications for the independence and autonomy of civil society organizations.
3. The implications of existing and proposed legislation, including the Foreign Aid Bill, for civil society.
4. The broader implications of restrictions on civic space for citizens’ participation, freedom of association and the ability to hold public institutions accountable.

**Expected Deliverables**

- An approved script for the video
- Identification and engagement of a suitable influencer or content creator to present the episode
- One completed We No Go Gree 104 video not exceeding 10 minutes
- Short clips adapted from the video for social media distribution

**Timeline**

3 weeks

**Reporting Line**

The consultant will report directly to the Executive Director or the designates.

**Intellectual Property Rights**

All intellectual property rights arising from the consultancy will be the property of Global Rights. The consultant will not disclose or use any confidential information obtained during the consultancy for any other purpose without the written consent of Global Rights.

**Confidentiality and Ethical Considerations**

The consultant will ensure that all data collected during the consultancy is treated with the utmost confidentiality and in accordance with ethical principles. In particular, the consultant will obtain informed consent from all participants before collecting any data and will ensure that data is stored securely and only accessible to authorized personnel. The consultant will also comply with any relevant legal and ethical standards and will report any ethical concerns or violations to Global Rights immediately.

**Expected Qualifications:**

- Proven experience in narrative video and documentary production.
- Proficiency in video production, camera operation, sound recording, and video editing
- A creative vision for translating reports into a visually engaging and emotionally resonant explainer video

**Proposal Submission:**

Interested qualified consultants are invited to submit a proposal that includes the following:

- An understanding of the requirements
- Methodology and work plan for performing the assignment
- Project delivery plans
- Relevant services undertaken in the past with detailed reference list indicating the scope of similar assignments
- Budget
- At least one sample of similar work

jobs.title: USDA Food for Peace Chief of Party II
jobs.description:
**NOTE: This recruitment is intended to establish a pool of qualified Chief of Party candidates for anticipated opportunities across multiple countries. Final project locations are pending donor confirmation, and positions will be contingent upon donor funding. Chief of Party positions will be based in the applicable country of assignment and are not remote positions.**

**Job Summary**

CRS seeks Chief of Party II candidates for the anticipated USDA Non-Emergency Food for Peace projects. These multi‑year, development-focused projects seek to combat chronic and acute malnutrition especially in children and mothers, strengthen early recovery and resilience, and support communities.

The Chief of Party II will provide vision, leadership and overall management of these large and complex projects to serve the poor and vulnerable. The incumbent’s strategic leadership, management and technical knowledge will ensure the delivery of high-quality programming and advance the position of CRS as a leading agency in the respective field. As a senior leader, the Chief of Party II will proactively manage security and mitigate security risks.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Lead all aspects of the development, implementation and consolidation of the assigned project, including sharing how the project contributes to the thought leadership of the industry. Serve as the primary point of contact with the donor as well as public, private and non-government stakeholders.
- Ensure the project is designed and implemented to meet donor expectations in terms of timely and quality results and budget, including strategies for phase out and sustainability. Lead coordination efforts between program and operations leads to ensure CRS program quality standards are adhered to.
- Effectively lead senior programming and operations talent. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching and mentoring. Strategically tailor individual development plans and complete performance assessments for direct reports. Oversee the development of staffing plans and the recruitment process of senior staff.
- Proactively manage and mitigate risk by monitoring national and regional issues that may impact staff and programming. Ensure all CRS staff safety and security policies and plans are regularly updated and all staff understand and adhere to these policies.
- Promote, uphold and model a commitment to the efficient use of agency and donor resources.
- Ensure compliance with donor grants, including financial tracking and oversight of partner budgets, finance, administration and donor reporting. Approve program expenditures, budget adjustments, and cost modification requests to donors.
- Represent CRS programming in international circles, highlighting innovative work. Publish program results and deliver presentations. Oversee the development of communication strategies and materials, complying with donor and CRS’ branding and marketing requirements and procedures.
- Manage relationships with consortium partner organizations, including organization of review/planning workshops. Coordinate the roles and activities of staff from other consortium member organizations to ensure implementation is in line with CRS partnership principles.
- Create and maintain proper conditions for learning. Establish a safe environment to share ideas, solutions, and difficulties. Build the internal capacity to detect, analyze and respond quickly to deficiencies.
- Identify performance gaps and training opportunities for CRS and partner staff and ensure the design and delivery of high-quality training and technical assistance.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, International Relations or a relevant technical area.
- Minimum of 8 years’ of relevant management and technical experience.
- Minimum of 7 years’ experience managing donor funds, including multi country grants. Excellent knowledge and experience in budget management.
- Minimum of 5 years’ of staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Experience coaching and mentoring senior program staff.
- Demonstrated experience of successful program management, including management of complex, high-value, multi-activity projects, with complicated logistics.
- Established leader in sector as demonstrated by peer reviewed publications, conference presentations etc.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in a related field.
- Experience engaging partners and strengthening partnerships. Knowledge of CRS partnership strategy.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Ability to represent and present at high levels.
- Excellent knowledge of MS Office package (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio), Web Conferencing Applications, and information and budget management systems.
- Excellent strategic, analytical, systems thinking, and problem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment and decisions.
- Excellent relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Ability to strategically approach each relationship.
- Team leadership abilities with diverse and multi-disciplinary teams. Coaching/mentoring skills.
- Strong communication and presentation skills. Ability to develop tailored and persuasive messaging for varied audiences.
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented mindset.

**Required Languages:** Fluency in English is required. Fluency in a local language depends on final geographic locations as determined by the donor.

**Travel:** Must be willing and able to travel up to 35%and will vary by award, country, and security context.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** Yes

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

CRS offers U.S. based staff a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, life insurance, vision, and a generous retirement savings plan. Salary and benefits packages for successful candidates employed outside the U.S. are based on the country of employment/in-country office where the candidate will perform the role. CRS´ work culture is a collaborative, mission-driven culture committed to improving the lives of the poor throughout the world.

jobs.title: Regional Internal Auditor - Sahel & Francophone
jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

The role reports directly and functionally to the MSI Head of Operational & Financial Audit, with an administrative dotted-line relationship to the Hostl Country Director. This arrangement will facilitate local coordination and integration while ensuring that responsibility for audit planning, scope, conclusions, performance management and professional oversight remains with Global Internal Audit, thereby preserving the independence of the audit function.

The role provides independent assurance across Mali, Senegal, Burkina Faso and Niger, with support to other Francophone Africa programmes where required. The post holder will complement Group Internal Audit cyclical audits through risk-based audits, targeted and routine monitoring, follow-up of audit actions and fraud investigations. The role will cover key financial, operational, donor compliance and programme risks, and will require regular regional travel.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- **Fluent in French and English;**
- Ability to plan and scope risk-based audits and translate key risks into proportionate audit procedures
- Ability to perform and document walkthroughs, control design assessments and tests of controls
- Strong data analysis skills, including use of CAATs to identify trends, anomalies and control exceptions
- Strong investigative skills, including root cause analysis, evidence evaluation and identification of fraud indicators
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce clear, concise audit and investigation reports
- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including confidence engaging and constructively challenging senior management.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Strong internal audit experience (at least 5 years), obtained through practice (Big 4/Mid-tier) or industry, with a working knowledge of the IIA Standards (essential)
- Experience conducting or supporting fraud and misconduct investigations (essential)
- Experience working in Francophone West Africa, the Sahel, or comparable fragile and conflict-affected environments, with a strong understanding of local operating contexts (desirable)
- Experience of working in an international, donor-funded service delivery organisation (desirable)

**Formal education/qualification**

- Holds a recognised professional accountancy/audit qualification (e.g., CA/ACA, ACCA, CPA, CIA etc.)

Please email Joshua.Wright@msichoices.org for the full job description.

**Location:** Dakar, Senegal.

**Full-time hours.**

**Contract type: 2 year fixed term contract.**

**Salary**: Gross Monthly Salary of 1,600,000 FCFA - 2,000,000 FCFA, plus benefits - dependent on experience.

**Salary band: Niveau 8**

**Closing date: 5th November 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be positioned within the existing salary structure of the country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

jobs.title: Assistant, Community Based Protection (Baidoa)
jobs.description:
**Duty station**: Baidoa

**Field travel:** Baidoa — Bay, Bakool and Lower Shabelle including high-risk frontline locations, subject to CIVIC security procedures.

**Expected start date**: 1 December 2026, to be confirmed and subject to project funding.

**Contract duration**: 12 months, to be confirmed and subject to project funding.

**Project and funding status**: Anticipated project. Funding has not yet been secured; recruitment and appointment are contingent on confirmed funding and approval to proceed.

1\. **Background**

Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) is an international non-governmental humanitarian protection organization that works to protect civilians affected by armed conflict. CIVIC works with communities, governments, security actors, civil society, and other partners to prevent, mitigate, and respond to civilian harm. In Somalia, CIVIC supports community-based protection, civilian harm mitigation, community-security and civil-military dialogue, engagement with security institutions, evidence and research, and policy and institutional efforts to strengthen civilian protection. A central part of CIVIC’s approach is supporting conflict-affected communities to identify and prioritize protection concerns, develop locally led responses, engage relevant authorities and security actors, and follow up on actions intended to improve civilian protection.

CIVIC supports Community Protection Groups (CPGs) and Community Protection Champions as locally rooted mechanisms for community engagement, protection analysis, advocacy and dialogue. CIVIC works with these structures to strengthen their capacity to identify and document protection concerns, conduct Protection of Civilians (PoC) awareness and engagement activities, engage authorities and security actors, participate in community-security dialogues, follow up on protection concerns and agreed actions, and monitor changes affecting civilian safety. To strengthen the capacity, leadership and sustainability of community-based protection structures, and to sustain CIVIC’s field presence and accompaniment alongside them, the Somalia Programme anticipates recruiting an Assistant Community-Based Protection based in Baidoa. These positions are planned for an anticipated project for which funding has not yet been secured. Recruitment and appointment are contingent on confirmation of project funding and approval to proceed.

2\. **Position Summary**

The Assistant, Community-Based Protection will support implementation and day-to-day follow-up of CIVIC’s community-based protection and civilian harm mitigation activities within an assigned geographic area. Through sustained support to Community Protection Groups (CPGs) and Community Protection Champions and direct engagement with local authorities, security and armed forces and conflict-affected communities, including in high-risk frontline areas, the Assistant will strengthen community leadership, facilitate safe, inclusive dialogue and follow up on commitments to reduce civilian harm. The Assistant will support community consultations and protection analysis, PoC workshops and community-led activities; prepare communities and security actors for structured dialogue; and follow up on protection concerns and agreed actions.

Central to the role is strengthening CPGs’ and Champions’ ability to independently convene discussions, conduct PoC awareness and workshops, engage authorities and security actors, raise protection concerns, facilitate or participate in dialogue, and follow up agreed actions. The Assistant will maintain regular community and stakeholder relationships, monitor community protection mechanisms and document changes resulting from community-led action and CIVIC-supported engagement.

The role requires sustained field presence and regular travel, including to high-risk frontline and conflict-affected areas under CIVIC security procedures. This position is based in Baidoa, covering Bay, Bakool and Lower Shabelle. All travel and activities depend on programme priorities, access assessments, security clearance and CIVIC duty-of-care requirements.

3\. **Key Responsibilities**

Across all responsibilities, strengthen the capacity, ownership and sustainability of CPGs and Community Protection Champions to increasingly lead protection activities independently of CIVIC.

**A. Community Engagement and Protection Analysis**

• Maintain continuous, inclusive community engagement beyond workshops and dialogues, involving women, youth, elders, persons with disabilities, displaced communities, minority groups and others facing heightened protection risks.

• Support consultations and joint analysis with communities and CPGs to identify and prioritize protection concerns, determine community-led responses, and distinguish issues requiring authorities, security, humanitarian or other actors.

• Identify emerging protection concerns and promptly communicate significant developments through CIVIC programme and management channels.

**B. CPG and Community Protection Champion Capacity Strengthening**

• Provide structured accompaniment, mentoring, training, refresher sessions, coaching and peer learning to build CPGs’ and Champions’ capacity, confidence and independence in PoC, civilian harm, community-based protection, conflict sensitivity, early warning and locally led approaches, including developing and updating protection action plans.

• Support CPGs and Champions to prioritize issues, prepare objectives and increasingly plan, organize and lead PoC workshops, consultations, awareness and protection engagements. Accompany activities, progressively transfer facilitation and leadership, coach engagement with decision-makers, and support documentation of issues, decisions and agreed actions.

• Follow up and document agreed actions and examples of independent activities, authority or security engagement, and resolution or escalation of protection concerns.Promote meaningful participation of women, youth and groups facing heightened risks, and exchange learning across programme locations where appropriate.

**C. Engagement with Security and Armed Forces and Frontline Dialogue**

• Prepare communities, CPGs, authorities and security and armed forces for structured civil-military and community-security dialogue, including in frontline areas. Conduct separate consultations to prioritize concerns, agree discussion points and assess participation, confidentiality and retaliation risks.

• With CIVIC staff and CPGs, organize and facilitate safe, inclusive dialogue with security and armed forces, including commanders and liaison officers, supporting community representatives to raise concerns and agree practical civilian harm prevention and mitigation measures.

• Record commitments, focal points and timelines in an action tracker; follow up implementation with communities, authorities and forces, and provide community feedback. Maintain district, state and field-level security relationships under CIVIC protocols; support recurring dialogue, safe communication and PoC awareness with colleagues, raise emerging harm concerns and encourage improvements. Engagement must exclude operational intelligence gathering or sharing.

**D. Protection Concerns, Referrals and Follow-Up**

• Support safe identification, confidential documentation and records of protection concerns under CIVIC policies and programme approaches, avoiding unnecessary risks to community members.

• Help CPGs and Champions identify safe pathways to raise concerns with authorities, security and armed forces or other stakeholders. Support specialized referrals through established protection service providers, with informed consent and confidentiality, within CIVIC’s mandate and procedures.

• Follow up concerns, document actor responses and monitor unresolved issues requiring programme, advocacy or management attention.Immediately escalate sensitive, serious or urgent concerns through appropriate CIVIC channels.

**E. Monitoring Community Protection Systems**

• Monitor CPG and Champion functionality, effectiveness and progress toward independent leadership, including regular meetings, identification of concerns, action plans, decision-maker engagement and follow-up. Assess participation and representation of women, youth and other relevant groups, and identify additional mentoring, training or support needs.

• Maintain updated membership, Champion activity, community-led initiative and follow-up records; contribute to periodic reviews of functionality, sustainability and readiness for greater ownership or transition.

**F. Monitoring Outcomes, Evidence and Learning**

• Document changes from community engagement, CPG advocacy, workshops, dialogue and other interventions; track whether commitments change security-force practices, authority responses, community behaviour or other protection outcomes.

• Conduct or support focus groups, key informant interviews, perception surveys and other monitoring and learning activities. Collect feedback on intervention relevance and perceived changes in safety, access and relationships with authorities and security actors.

• Identify successful community-led approaches, recurring barriers and lessons for adaptation. With programme and monitoring colleagues, ensure accurate, documented evidence for decision-making, programme and donor reports, learning products and advocacy.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

• Maintain constructive relationships and updated stakeholder mapping with community leaders, district and state government institutions, relevant security structures, civil society, women’s and youth groups, humanitarian and protection actors and other stakeholders.

• Safely connect CPGs and communities with appropriate stakeholders to address protection concerns; attend local coordination meetings when requested, provide timely programme feedback and support CIVIC and partner field missions.

**H. Programme Implementation and Reporting**

• Support activity planning and implementation with CPGs, Champions, communities and stakeholders, including logistical and administrative arrangements.

• Prepare timely activity reports, field updates and meeting notes; maintain accurate participant records, required sex- and age-disaggregated data, and a tracker of CPG activities, concerns, dialogue commitments, community-led actions and outstanding follow-up.

• Update the Community Engagement Officer on progress, emerging issues, stakeholder dynamics, risks and opportunities; contribute field evidence, outcomes, challenges and lessons to monthly, quarterly and donor reporting.

**I. Frontline Travel, Conflict Sensitivity, Safeguarding and Duty of Care**

• Apply conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches; maintain strict confidentiality and avoid exposing participants, CPG members or Champions to retaliation or other risks through engagement, documentation or advocacy.

• Avoid expectations or commitments outside CIVIC’s mandate or authority.Immediately report safeguarding, security and serious protection concerns through established procedures and comply with CIVIC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding requirements and organizational policies.

• Coordinate travel with programme and security focal points, obtain clearance, follow approved movement, communication and check-in arrangements, and promptly report access or security changes. Postpone, relocate or suspend travel or dialogue when CIVIC procedures require it or participant safety cannot be adequately addressed.

4\. **Geographic Responsibilities**

Duty station: Baidoa. Geographic coverage: CIVIC programme locations across Bay, Bakool and Lower Shabelle, including Baidoa and Hudur, as prioritized by the Somalia programme. The Assistant will travel regularly from Baidoa to support community-based protection, engagement with relevant security and armed forces, and dialogue in conflict-affected and high-risk frontline locations.

Provide sustained accompaniment to CPGs and Champions across assigned locations; strengthen their ability to identify protection concerns, implement community protection action plans, lead PoC awareness activities, engage authorities and armed forces, and follow up on dialogue commitments. In Hudur and other locations, tailor mentoring to the capacity and needs of each community protection structure and promote progressive community ownership. Field visits and frontline activities require CIVIC authorization, security and access assessments, movement planning and compliance with duty-of-care procedures.

5\. **Qualifications and Experience**

• Bachelor's degree in social sciences, human rights, international relations, development studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in community engagement, protection, humanitarian, human rights or peacebuilding programming, preferably in Somalia or a comparable context.

• Demonstrated experience working with community-based structures or similar participatory community protection mechanisms.

• Familiarity with Protection of Civilians (PoC), civilian harm prevention and mitigation, community-based protection, and civil-military and community-security dialogue approaches. Experience working in frontline or other high-risk conflict environments is an asset.

• Demonstrated skills in community-based protection, inclusive facilitation, conflict-sensitive communication and community liaison, including experience engaging security and armed forces and facilitating dialogue with conflict-affected communities.

• Fluency in Somali required; working proficiency in English is essential.

• Willingness and ability to undertake regular field travel from the assigned duty station, including to high-risk frontline and conflict-affected locations, subject to CIVIC access conditions including travelling on road where necessary.

• Strong written and spoken communication skills, including experience preparing activity reports, meeting notes and field updates.

• Commitment to CIVIC's mandate and values, and to conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches.

7\. **Safeguarding and Code of Conduct**

CIVIC is committed to safeguarding the people it works with and maintains a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, and to any other conduct that undermines its mission. All offers of employment are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. The successful candidate will be required to sign and adhere to CIVIC's Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy.

**Additional Details**

**Application Deadline: October 29, 2026**

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. ***Shortlisted candidates will receive an email invitation from TestGorilla to submit their resume. Please complete this step promptly to ensure your candidacy is fully considered.***

CIVIC is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: CIVIC does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and does not pay placement fees for candidates submitted by agencies other than its approved partners.

• Identify successful community-led approaches, recurring barriers and lessons for adaptation. With programme and monitoring colleagues, ensure accurate, documented evidence for decision-making, programme and donor reports, learning products and advocacy.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

• Maintain constructive relationships and updated stakeholder mapping with community leaders, district and state government institutions, relevant security structures, civil society, women’s and youth groups, humanitarian and protection actors and other stakeholders.

• Safely connect CPGs and communities with appropriate stakeholders to address protection concerns; attend local coordination meetings when requested, provide timely programme feedback and support CIVIC and partner field missions.

**H. Programme Implementation and Reporting**

• Support activity planning and implementation with CPGs, Champions, communities and stakeholders, including logistical and administrative arrangements.

• Prepare timely activity reports, field updates and meeting notes; maintain accurate participant records, required sex- and age-disaggregated data, and a tracker of CPG activities, concerns, dialogue commitments, community-led actions and outstanding follow-up.

• Update the Community Engagement Officer on progress, emerging issues, stakeholder dynamics, risks and opportunities; contribute field evidence, outcomes, challenges and lessons to monthly, quarterly and donor reporting.

**I. Frontline Travel, Conflict Sensitivity, Safeguarding and Duty of Care**

• Apply conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches; maintain strict confidentiality and avoid exposing participants, CPG members or Champions to retaliation or other risks through engagement, documentation or advocacy.

• Avoid expectations or commitments outside CIVIC’s mandate or authority.Immediately report safeguarding, security and serious protection concerns through established procedures and comply with CIVIC’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding requirements and organizational policies.

• Coordinate travel with programme and security focal points, obtain clearance, follow approved movement, communication and check-in arrangements, and promptly report access or security changes. Postpone, relocate or suspend travel or dialogue when CIVIC procedures require it or participant safety cannot be adequately addressed.

4\. **Geographic Responsibilities**

Duty station: Beledweyne. Geographic coverage: CIVIC programme locations across Hirshabelle and Galmudug, including Beledweyne, Adale and Haradhere, as prioritized by the Somalia programme. The Assistant will travel regularly from Beledweyne, including to conflict-affected and high-risk frontline locations, to accompany CPGs and Champions, support community-led protection activities, engage relevant security and armed forces, and facilitate community–armed forces dialogue. Strengthen community ownership of consultations, PoC workshops, protection action plans and follow-up on agreed commitments. Field visits and frontline activities require CIVIC authorization, security and access assessments, movement planning and compliance with duty-of-care procedures.

5\. **Qualifications and Experience**

• Bachelor's degree in social sciences, human rights, international relations, development studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in community engagement, protection, humanitarian, human rights or peacebuilding programming, preferably in Somalia or a comparable context.

• Demonstrated experience working with community-based structures or similar participatory community protection mechanisms.

• Familiarity with Protection of Civilians (PoC), civilian harm prevention and mitigation, community-based protection, and civil-military and community-security dialogue approaches. Experience working in frontline or other high-risk conflict environments is an asset.

• Demonstrated skills in community-based protection, inclusive facilitation, conflict-sensitive communication and community liaison, including experience engaging security and armed forces and facilitating dialogue with conflict-affected communities.

• Fluency in Somali required; working proficiency in English is essential.

• Willingness and ability to undertake regular field travel from the assigned duty station, including to high-risk frontline and conflict-affected locations, subject to CIVIC access conditions including travelling on road where necessary.

• Strong written and spoken communication skills, including experience preparing activity reports, meeting notes and field updates.

• Commitment to CIVIC's mandate and values, and to conflict-sensitive, inclusive and do-no-harm approaches.

7\. **Safeguarding and Code of Conduct**

CIVIC is committed to safeguarding the people it works with and maintains a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, and to any other conduct that undermines its mission. All offers of employment are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. The successful candidate will be required to sign and adhere to CIVIC's Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy.

**Additional Details**

**Application Deadline: October 29, 2026**

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. ***Shortlisted candidates will receive an email invitation from TestGorilla to submit their resume. Please complete this step promptly to ensure your candidacy is fully considered.***

CIVIC is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: CIVIC does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and does not pay placement fees for candidates submitted by agencies other than its approved partners.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker- CHW (Syria - Lattakia)
jobs.description:
**Job Title: Community Health Worker**

**Job location: Syria - Lattakia – Qastal Maaf, Ras Al-Bassit, Ein Al-Baida, Al-Samiyeh, Kansaba & Qasatel Halab, Al-Aedeen**

**Reports to: Project Coordinator**

**Number of positions: 6**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Community Health Worker works within the nutrition program at the assigned health facility and its catchment community. The role is responsible for distributing nutrition supplies, monitoring the stock of supplementary feeding products for Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) cases, dispensing Ready-to-Use Supplementary Food (RUSF) to admitted beneficiaries, and carrying out community activities, with a particular focus on tracing defaulters and following up non-responding cases to ensure continuity of treatment.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

1\. Distribute nutrition supplies and materials (supplements, micronutrients and awareness materials) to beneficiaries according to the program distribution plan and eligibility criteria.

2\. Dispense RUSF to children aged 6–59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) admitted with MAM, according to the prescribed ration and visit schedule, and record each distribution in the program registers and ration cards.

3\. Monitor the stock of MAM supplements at the health facility: receive deliveries, record stock movements on stock cards, conduct regular physical counts, check expiry dates and storage conditions, and report shortages or discrepancies promptly to the supervisor.

4\. Prepare weekly and monthly stock and distribution reports, and reconcile quantities dispensed against the number of beneficiaries served.

5\. Trace defaulters (cases who missed their follow-up visits) through home visits and phone calls, identify the reasons for defaulting, and encourage caregivers to return to the program.

6\. Follow up non-responding cases through home visits to check correct use of RUSF, sharing of the ration within the household, feeding and hygiene practices, and refer them to the nutritionist or physician for medical review.

7\. Conduct community activities, including active case finding through MUAC screening and awareness sessions on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF), malnutrition prevention and correct use of supplements.

8\. Refer identified malnutrition cases, and cases showing danger signs or medical complications, to the health facility or stabilization centers.

9\. Keep accurate records of home visits, follow-ups and community activities, and submit them to the supervisor on time.

10\. Coordinate with the nutrition team, community health workers and local community leaders to facilitate community activities and beneficiaries' access to services.

11\. Perform any other related tasks assigned by the direct supervisor.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

1\. Secondary school certificate as a minimum; an institute or university degree in nutrition, nursing, health sciences or a related field is an advantage.

2\. At least one year of experience in community outreach, nutrition programs or health awareness with non-governmental organizations.

3\. Knowledge of CMAM / MAM programs and basic stock management is an advantage.

4\. Good communication skills and the ability to deal respectfully with the local community.

5\. Basic computer skills (Word, Excel) and the ability to keep accurate records.

6\. Ability to work in the field, conduct home visits and work under pressure.

7\. Residence in the governorate and good knowledge of the area are preferred.

**ABOUT UITYD**

UITYD is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals of diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

UITYD Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to UITYD employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

1\. Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

2\. Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside UITYD.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY**

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to UITYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. UITYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY**

UITYD provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. UITYD employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

**Safeguarding & Code of Conduct**

All **UITYD** employees must adhere to PSEA's protection policies

Principles and rules of conduct. Strict compliance with safety and ethical standards is required.

jobs.title: ICO Communications, Online Visibility and Public Recognition Volunteer
jobs.description:
***ICO Communications, Online Visibility and Public***
***Recognition Volunteer***

Organisation: International Communities Organisation (ICO)
Location: Remote/Hybrid (as agreed)
Commitment: 10–15 hours per week (flexible)
Reporting to: Charlie Grant

**About ICO**
International Communities Organisation (ICO) is an independent, neutral and international NGO
dedicated to the protection of human rights. ICO advocates for economic, social, political and cultural
rights, through providing a platform for underrepresented minority voices and constructing environments
of cross-community cooperation predicated upon mutual respect.

**Role Purpose**
The Communications, Online Visibility and Public Recognition Volunteer will support the ICO team in
strengthening the organisation's communications, online presence and public profile. The volunteer will
assist with organising communications materials, promoting ICO's work across digital platforms, and
helping showcase the organisation's impact to partners, supporters and wider audiences.
Working alongside the ICO team, the volunteer will contribute to the development of communications
resources, support digital engagement, and assist with raising awareness of ICO's projects, partnerships
and achievements. A significant area of support will be assisting the team with developing and organising
materials for ICO's "10 Years of ICO" project, which celebrates a decade of the organisation's work and
impact.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to gain practical experience in communications,
public relations, digital engagement and charity communications while contributing to an organisation
making a positive difference internationally.

**Key Responsibilities**
Working under the guidance of the ICO team, the volunteer will support activities such as:
● Assisting with the organisation and development of communications materials relating to ICO's
projects, achievements and partnerships.

● Supporting the compilation and organisation of information, photographs, publications, reports
and media coverage for the "10 Years of ICO" project.
● Helping organise ICO's achievements, advocacy work and institutional milestones into accessible
communications resources.
● Assisting with the preparation and scheduling of content for LinkedIn and other digital platforms.
● Supporting the development and distribution of newsletters and Mailchimp campaigns.
● Assisting with drafting and editing press releases, news stories and organisational updates.
● Helping identify opportunities to increase ICO's online visibility and public recognition.
● Supporting the maintenance of a consistent communications style and organisational voice across
digital platforms.
● Conducting online research to identify media, communications and partnership opportunities.
● Providing general communications and administrative support to the ICO team as required.
What You'll Gain
As a volunteer, you will have the opportunity to:
● Gain practical experience in communications, public relations and digital engagement within an
international charity.
● Develop skills in content creation, communications planning and stakeholder engagement.
● Build experience using professional communications platforms such as LinkedIn and Mailchimp.
● Contribute to ICO's "10 Years of ICO" legacy project and help showcase the organisation's
impact.
● Work alongside experienced professionals in the charity, community development and
international sectors.
● Receive mentoring, support and a reference upon successful completion of the role.

**Skills and Experience**
**Essential**
● Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
● Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
● Good research and information management skills.
● Confidence using Microsoft Office or Google Workspace.
● An interest in communications, media, marketing, public relations or the charity sector.
● The ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team.

**Desirable**
● Experience creating content for social media platforms.

● Familiarity with LinkedIn, Mailchimp or similar communications tools.
● Experience writing articles, blogs, newsletters or press releases.
● An interest in international development, community engagement or advocacy.
● Previous experience in communications, journalism, marketing or a related field.

**Working Arrangements**
This is a flexible volunteer role requiring approximately 10–15 hours per week, with working hours
agreed in advance with the ICO team. The volunteer will work closely with Tallulah Pollock and Charlie
Grant, supporting ongoing communications, online visibility and public recognition activities. Guidance,
mentoring and regular feedback will be provided throughout the placement.
The role offers an excellent opportunity to develop practical communications experience while helping
strengthen ICO's public profile and promote the impact of its work across the UK and internationally.

jobs.title: Programme Development and Quality Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Overview and Purpose:** The Programme Development and Quality Co-ordinator (PDQC) provides strategic leadership on country strategy, programme development, quality, MEL, accountability, learning, communication & advocacy, partnerships and localisation. He or she ensures that programmes are relevant, needs- and evidence-based, technically sound, compliant with Concern’s standards and aligned with the National Strategic Plan. The PDQC sets the strategic direction for funding positioning and development, whilst the Grants Manager oversees the operational processes of grant management, proposal development, reporting, partnerships, communication and visibility. The PDQC reports to the Programme Director and provides line management oversight of the MEL and accountability functions, as well as of the Grants Manager. The Communications and Advocacy Officer and the Partnerships Manager are supervised by the Grants Manager.

**Line manager:** Director of Programmes

**Terms and conditions:** *Fixed-term contract (12 months), full-time, unsupervised, office-based role with frequent travel to the field*

**Salary:** GB6 €46,822 - 52,024

[GB4-6 Unaccompanied International Staff T&Cs](https://concern.icims.com/icims2/servlet/icims2?module=AppInert&action=download&id=299&hashed=-877963960)

**Responsibilities**

**1. Country Strategy and Strategic Programme Development**

- Support the Programme Director in developing, reviewing and monitoring the National Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with Concern’s organisational priorities and country team ownership.
- Analyse context, needs, vulnerabilities, sectoral trends and humanitarian developments to inform programme priorities and strategic decisions.
- Contribute to defining priorities for funding, positioning, growth and portfolio diversification.
- Provide strategic and conceptual leadership for new programmes and proposals, including theories of change, intervention logic, technical approaches and cross-cutting priorities.
- Ensure HCUEP, equality, protection, conflict sensitivity, disaster risk management and other Concern principles are integrated across programmes.
- Guide the Grants Manager in translating country priorities into funding opportunities, proposals and donor engagement.

**2. Programme Quality and Technical Support**

- Define and oversee the country programme quality framework and its application throughout the programme cycle.
- Ensure technical and methodological coherence across programmes, working with programme managers, area coordinators, technical advisers and HQ teams.
- Promote relevant humanitarian standards, Concern policies and programme cycle management systems.
- Identify technical support needs, coordinate quality reviews and ensure follow-up of recommendations from evaluations, audits, technical visits and learning exercises.
- Ensure adequate resources for programme quality, MEAL, accountability and cross-cutting priorities are included in programme designs and budgets.

**3. MEL, Accountability and Learning**

- Provide strategic leadership of the country MEL function, including the MEL strategy, results frameworks, indicators, data systems and dashboards.
- Ensure programme data is reliable, protected, analysed and used for decision-making, programme adaptation and demonstration of results.
- Oversee evaluations, studies, surveys, research and learning reviews, ensuring findings are disseminated and used.
- Promote learning, adaptive management and knowledge-sharing across programme sites, country, regional and technical teams.
- Oversee accountability to communities, including feedback and complaints mechanisms, community participation and closing the feedback loop.
- Ensure evidence, results and lessons learned inform proposals, donor reports and communications.

**4. Leadership, Coordination and Staff Management**

- Line manage and support the professional development of MEL and accountability managers and the Grants Manager.
- Ensure clear roles and effective coordination between PDQC, MEL, accountability, partnerships, grants and communications functions.
- Work closely with the Programme Director, Area Coordinators, Programme Managers, support functions and Dublin teams.
- Represent Concern in relevant strategic and technical forums.
- Ensure compliance with Concern’s policies, procedures, quality standards and commitments.

**5. Other Responsibilities**

- Play an active role in emergency preparedness and response and adapt programming to evolving country needs.
- Promote and comply with Concern policies and procedures, including safeguarding, Code of Conduct, equality, finance, logistics, HR and security.
- Undertake other related duties reasonably assigned by the Programme Director.

**Role Holder Requirements**

Essential

- At least five years’ relevant field and/or headquarters experience in the humanitarian or international development sector.
- Fluency in written and spoken English and French.
- Relevant university degree in political science, economics, agriculture, development studies or a related field.
- Proven experience in developing proposals for international NGOs and working with institutional donors.
- Strong experience across all stages of Programme Cycle Management, including assessments, programme design, logical frameworks, implementation, monitoring and learning.
- Experience in programme quality, results-based management and the integration of cross-cutting approaches.
- Proven experience working with national/local partners and rural communities.
- Knowledge and practical understanding of equality, particularly gender and disability inclusion, protection and participatory approaches.
- Demonstrated experience in staff management, capacity strengthening and team development.
- Ability to work independently, take initiative, prioritise effectively and deliver high-quality work under pressure and tight deadlines.
- Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, presentation, networking and influencing skills.
- Strong intercultural sensitivity, adaptability and ability to work effectively in diverse teams and contexts.
- Commitment to Concern’s mission, values and approaches, including participation, accountability, protection and capacity strengthening.
- Good IT skills.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to programme areas, including rural and remote locations, for up to 50% of working time.

jobs.title: Grants Manager
jobs.description:
**Overview and Purpose:** The Grants Manager is responsible for the operational management of Concern DRC’s grants portfolio and ensures compliance, quality and adherence to deadlines for proposals, contracts, reports and grant management processes. Under the supervision of the PDQC, they translate the strategic directions set out by the Programme Director and the PDQC into funding plans, proposal development processes and operational monitoring tools. The Grants Manager also leads communication, visibility and advocacy support functions, as well as the management and monitoring of partnerships, whilst providing line management for the Communications and Advocacy Officer and the Partnerships Manager. He/she works closely with the programme, finance, MEL and CRM teams, the area coordinators, the Desk and the Concern teams in Dublin, London and New York.

**Reports to:** Programme Development and Quality Coordinator

**Terms:** *6-month fixed-term contract (renewable), full-time, unaccompanied, office-based with fieldwork*

**Location:** Based in Beni, with frequent travel to other locations in Greater and Lesser North Kivu and Tanganyika, and occasional visits to our office in Kinshasa. The place of assignment may be subject to change depending on the evolving situation and needs, at the discretion of management.

**Salary:** GB5 €42,136 - €46,818

[GB4-6 Unaccompanied International Staff T&Cs](https://concern.icims.com/icims2/servlet/icims2?module=AppInert&action=download&id=299&hashed=-877963960)

**Responsibilities**

**1. Grant Management and Compliance**

- Lead grant management processes from inception to closure, including kick-off, monitoring, review and close-out meetings.
- Ensure compliance with donor contracts, rules and requirements, in coordination with Programme, Finance, MEAL, Partnerships and support teams.
- Maintain grant monitoring tools, calendars, compliance matrices, grant files and repositories, including GMS and the Working Site.
- Coordinate contractual amendments, budget revisions, extensions and official donor communications, subject to Programme Director and PDQC approval.
- Provide guidance and training on donor requirements, contractual obligations, filing and key deadlines.
- Ensure consistent, comprehensive and audit-ready grant documentation, archiving and version control.

**2. Proposals, Reporting and Deliverables**

- Coordinate the development of concept notes and proposals, based on strategic and technical direction from the Programme Director and PDQC.
- Develop proposal workplans, coordinate inputs from teams and partners, consolidate contributions and lead final drafting and review.
- Ensure proposals meet donor requirements, formats and deadlines.
- Coordinate narrative reporting, including collection of inputs, quality assurance, alignment with MEAL and financial data, approval and submission.
- Ensure consistency between narrative results, indicators, budgets, expenditure, forecasts and contractual deliverables.
- Track actions and recommendations arising from grant management meetings and programme reviews.

**3. Funding Strategy and Donor Relations**

- Operationalise the funding and positioning strategy defined by the Programme Director and PDQC.
- Maintain the funding pipeline, opportunity calendar, donor profiles and relevant analyses to support decision-making.
- Monitor donor priorities, policies, procedures and funding opportunities, and provide structured analysis to programme leadership.
- Coordinate with the Desk and fundraising teams in Dublin, London and New York on opportunities and deadlines.
- Prepare donor briefings, presentations and supporting documentation, and follow up on agreed actions.

**4. Communications, Visibility and Advocacy**

- Oversee implementation of Concern DRC’s communications, visibility and advocacy priorities, under the strategic direction of the Programme Director and PDQC.
- Line manage the Communications and Advocacy function, setting priorities, monitoring workplans and supporting professional development.
- Coordinate high-quality communication products, including case studies, testimonials, factsheets, photography, digital content and newsletters.
- Ensure compliance with donor visibility requirements, consent procedures, data protection and Concern standards.
- Support the development of advocacy messages and positioning materials, subject to relevant technical and strategic approval.
- Ensure programme results, learning and MEAL evidence are accurately reflected in reporting and communications.

**5. Partnerships and Capacity Strengthening**

- Lead the operational development of partnerships and localisation, with support from the Partnerships Manager.
- Oversee partner identification and selection, capacity assessments, due diligence, agreements and capacity-strengthening plans.
- Promote equitable partnership and localisation principles throughout programmes and organisational practices.
- Monitor partnership quality and promote appropriate sharing of responsibilities, resources, knowledge and decision-making.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Provide line management and professional development to the Communications and Advocacy and Partnerships functions, and additional team members as required.
- Promote meaningful community participation in proposal development, reporting and communications.
- Comply with and promote Concern policies and procedures, particularly safeguarding, Code of Conduct, equality, finance, logistics, HR and security.
- Contribute to emergency responses and programme visits as required.
- Undertake other relevant duties reasonably assigned by the PDQC or Programme Director.

**Role Holder Requirements**
Essential:

- Minimum two years’ international experience with an NGO, UN agency, donor or comparable organisation.
- Minimum two years’ experience in grant management, including donor compliance, reporting and proposal development.
- Proven experience developing successful funding applications for institutional donors.
- Excellent written and spoken English and French.
- Strong understanding of institutional donors, contractual requirements and compliance obligations.
- Experience working effectively in fast-paced, results-oriented environments and managing competing priorities under pressure.
- Strong organisational, planning and prioritisation skills, with excellent attention to detail.
- Good understanding of budget development, financial monitoring and financial reporting.
- Experience in facilitation, capacity strengthening and partnership development, including through formal and informal training.
- Good understanding of MEAL tools, logical frameworks, indicators and monitoring plans.
- Experience developing external communications materials, including factsheets, case studies, success stories, articles and digital content.
- Strong communication, interpersonal, networking and coordination skills.
- Ability to work collaboratively and effectively across multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
- Willingness and ability to travel frequently.

Desirable:

- Master’s degree in social sciences, human rights, humanitarian assistance, international development or another relevant field.
- Experience managing grants from major institutional donors, particularly Humanitarian Funds, US Government donors, UN agencies and EU/ECHO.
- Experience working within consortia and with national or international partners.
- Knowledge of relevant humanitarian quality and accountability standards, including Sphere and CHS.
- Experience delivering training on donor regulations, compliance requirements and humanitarian quality standards.
- Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected or insecure contexts.
- Strong cultural and political sensitivity and ability to operate effectively in complex environments.
- Demonstrated initiative, autonomy and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent analytical and writing skills.

jobs.title: Head of Programme - DRC (International)
jobs.description:
**Department:** Operations

**Duty Station:** **:** Goma

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Contract duration:** 1 year (renewable)

**Direct report:** Country Director

**Grade:** Head of (In country)

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this Role?**

The Head of Programme provides overall leadership, technical oversight, strategic direction, and management of Geneva Call’s programme portfolio in DRC. This includes ensuring high-quality programme design, effective implementation, sound financial management, and strong team leadership. The role requires working in complex and dynamic contexts, adapting programme strategies to meet changing needs, and ensuring alignment with Geneva Call’s mandate, values, and operational priorities.

## **Work Relations**

Under the supervision of the Country Director, the Head of Programme will provide overall leadership, technical oversight, management and strategic vision of the program of Geneva Call while managing staff and resources to ensure that the program meets its objectives and deliverable timely, qualitatively and within budget. The Head of Programme will work in a fluctuating and uncertain context and constantly adapt the answer of Geneva Call.

## **Duties and Responsibilities**

**Programme Leadership and Strategy**

- Lead the design, adaptation, and delivery of country programme strategies in alignment with Geneva Call’s global priorities and operational guidelines.
- Provide strategic oversight to ensure programmes are contextually relevant, conflict-sensitive, and responsive to humanitarian needs.
- Integrate conflict and humanitarian analysis into programme design, monitoring, and adaptation.
- Ensure programme implementation meets agreed objectives, quality standards, and donor requirements.

**Resource Mobilisation, Proposal Development, and Reporting**

- Foster innovation and identify new opportunities for engagement, partnerships, and growth.
- Lead proposal development and resource mobilisation with the Country Director and Donor Relations, aiming for diversified and multi-year funding, including consortium bids with international and national organisations, and ensuring viable programming consistent with access, security and absorption capacity.
- Ensure timely and high-quality donor reporting and internal programme reports.

**Programme Management and Coordination**

- Oversee the planning, delivery, and monitoring of all projects in line with project cycle management standards.
- Ensure effective coordination among programme teams and with other departments (finance, logistics, HR).
- Monitor programme expenditure against budgets and ensure compliance with Geneva Call policies, donor requirements, and accountability standards.
- Lead periodic grant reviews (activity progress, budget-versus-actual, burn rate) with Finance and the Programme Coordinators, and anticipate budget realignments or no-cost extension requests to avoid under- or overspending, and contribute to evaluations and audits.
- Maintain effective relationships with implementing partners, providing technical and operational support where required.
- Safeguard all programme data and ensure proper documentation and filing systems.

**Team Leadership and Human Resource Management**

- Line-manage senior programme staff and oversee recruitment, induction, and professional development.
- Promote a safe, collaborative, and high-performing team culture that aligns with Geneva Call’s values.
- Provide mentoring, coaching, and capacity-building to strengthen team skills and performance.
- Ensure compliance with HR policies, performance management processes, and safeguarding standards.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL)**

- Contribute to ensure robust MEAL systems are in place to track progress, assess impact, and inform programme adaptation.
- Support evidence-based decision-making and promote a learning culture within the team.
- Contribute to evaluations.

**External and internal Relations, Advocacy, and Representation**

- Represent Geneva Call with national authorities, donors, coordination bodies, and other key stakeholders.
