jobs.title: GPP Manager - Gates Programmes (Francophone)
jobs.location: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

MSI seeks a Global Programmes & Philanthropy Manager - Gates Programmes (project manager) to support implementation of a range of SRHR grant-funded projects by the Gates Foundation. Reporting to the head of the portfolio, the Manager will be responsible for supporting newly approved projects, with multicountry and bilateral investments, from the Gates Foundation (and other donors as assigned such as the Children’s Investment Fund Foundation and the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office) to advance sexual and reproductive health services and increase modern contraceptive prevalence in LMICs.

Working in the **Global Funding, Innovation and Impact** team and sub-teams, the Manager will actively support Country Programmes and partners’ implementation, ensuring delivery of agreed deliverables (including payment by results KPIs) for multiple grants. In addition, the Manager will work very closely with other relevant donor teams, operations, finance, and technical services departments to ensure MSI and donor priorities are reflected in project delivery and learning agenda. The Manager will play a critical role in donor relationship management including effective and timely reporting and serve as an important internal resource.

This role and programme team is part of the broader team supporting donor/grant-funded investments. The team oversees the technical design and execution of donor-funded investments and is responsible for stewarding and advancing MSI’s relationship with the Gates Foundation and other donors as a key contributor to achieving MSI’s mission. The team provides organizational leadership to ensure that MSI’s strategy, policy, systems, and capacities are responsive to donor priorities and investments, and that Gates-funded programming advances the MSI2030 strategy.

This is an exciting role that requires excellent financial and data analysis skills, strong communication and facilitation skills, analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent ability to work across teams (in both English and French) to deliver results, and great attention to detail.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- **Fluent English and French (essential) oral and written communication skills required.**
- Proven ability to liaise effectively with and collaborate with diverse stakeholders, including global, regional, national, local, public, and private partners.
- Excellent skills in communicating evidence, excellent facilitation skills with proven ability to synthesize complex technical component into easy-to-understand briefs or presentation.
- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective relationships across cross cultural settings to achieve mutual objectives and maximise opportunities.
- Exceptional problem-solving abilities and demonstrated confidence in handling difficult situations.
- Demonstrated ability to meet deadlines, perform under pressure and reputation for consistently delivering results to a high standard.
- Be data-literate with an attention for details. Able to analyse and interpret datasets, articulate trends, and generate charts and graphs.
- Advanced Excel and PowerPoint proficiency.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Experience of managing Gates donor-funded projects preferable, or large restricted foundations/government/institutional donor (multi-country desirable), including project monitoring and reporting against deliverables, proactive risk management and escalation (essential)
- Experience in writing and editing reports, or externally facing project information for donors or other external stakeholders (essential)
- Financial management experience including budgeting, budget tracking and financial performance analysis at the multi-million dollar level (essential)
- Program design and proposal experience (essential), with the Gates Foundation (preferred).
- Demonstrable experience managing complex relationships across organisations and across countries (essential)
- Experience in delivering capacity building support and skills development of others in either a technical area or project management skills, in order to meet project deliverables (essential)
- Understanding of the sexual and reproductive health and family planning fields (essential)

**Formal education/qualification**

- Master’s degree in public health or other social sciences desirable.

Please email Joshua.Wright@msichoices.org for the full job description.

**Location:** London, UK (minimum of 2 days per week in the office) or any country programme where MSI operates in.

**Full-time:** 35 hours a week, Monday to Friday.

**Contract type: 2 year fixed term contract.**

**Salary**: £48,900 - £56,300 per annum for London applicants. For country programme applicants, the salary will be strictly banded within the local national context.

**Salary band: BG 9**

**Closing date: 5th November 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be positioned within the existing salary structure of the country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

jobs.title: Regional Humanitarian Preparedness and Response Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Functional Area**: Humanitarian and Resilience

**Reports to**: Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience

**Location:** CO where Plan have a presence in Asia

**Travel required:** Both within and outside region, often in hardship locations

**Effective Date:** By January 2027

**Grade:** TBC

**Closing Date:** 22 November 2026

**Organisational Context**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood, and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge. For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries. We won’t stop until we are all equal

Plan International has been working in the Asia Pacific (APAC) Region since 1960. Currently there are 12 Country Offices (COs) that includes Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Thailand, Timor Leste, and Vietnam and 3 Fundraising Country/National Offices (FCNOs): (Indonesia, India, and Philippines); and 4 National Offices (NOs): HongKong, Australia, Japan, and Korea in the Asia Pacific Region.

In Asia Pacific region, through Humanitarian and Resilience programing, we build communities’ resilience and support children’s right to dignity and protection before, during and after disasters and conflicts. Aligned with the Global Strategy 2022 – 2027, Plan International will Scale up humanitarian impact as one of the program priorities where we aim to become a leading agency protection children’s right and promoting equality for girls in crisis. We will enhance humanitarian preparedness throughout the organisation, strengthen integration of humanitarian-development and peace work and finally improve ways of working to respond quickly and effective to emergencies. Plan International want to reach more children especially girls, in less time, save lives and leave lasting impact.

Under the supervision of the Regional Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience,
the Regional Humanitarian Preparedness and Response Coordinator will provide support to
strengthen the disaster preparedness, readiness and response to disaster caused by natural
hazard nor climate related hazards as well as conflict and protracted crisis in Asia Pacific
region.

The expected role is to support oversee the achievement of Country’s Ready to Respond (R2R), conduct regular analysis of disaster risk and conflict trends in the region, manage the emergency response data base and its documentation, promote the importance of Accountability to Affected People and support coordinate the APAC’ Children in Crisis Fund (CiCF) and representing Plan International in specific emergency technical working groups in particular the Accountability to Affected People (AAP) Working Group, CVA Working Group and the Regional Gender in Humanitarian Action (GiHA) network. Lastly this post holder is expected to be deployed in the initial phase of response and or during recovery phase to support COs in his/her capacity as technical advisor and or Deputy Emergency Response Manager as well as potential seconded to Country Offices to provide technical support in any humanitarian preparedness and readiness work in normal situation and support with delivering humanitarian related training i.e. Emergency Response Team (ERT) Training.

**DIMENSIONS OF THE ROLE**

The post holder serves as the principal regional coordinator on humanitarian preparedness and response related deliverables in Asia Pacific region and work in close coordination and collaboration with the Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience and the Regional Anticipatory Action and Climate Specialist.

This post covers 15 countries in the region with supervision of Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience and is expected to be part of Plan International Global Roster and deployed to support other COs in other region especially during Red alert emergencies.

The role works with Country Offices and regional teams to support ensuring a quality of humanitarian preparedness, readiness and response in an accountable and timely manner and contribute to strengthening Plan International’s visibility as Humanitarian actor in the region.

The Specific Dimension of the roles comprises of:

**Support programmatic and data management of humanitarian action in APAC:**

- A primary support function to the 15 Country Offices on issues relating to Emergency Preparedness, Readiness and Response, i.e. quarterly hotspot analysis, manage humanitarian preparedness and database and collecting CO contribution for monthly humanitarian round up.
- Provide support to ensure the timely update of CO’s Ready to Respond (R2R) Minimum Preparedness Action (MPA) implementation and it progress.
- Support manages the humanitarian dashboard of APAC
- Coordinating the APAC Children in Crisis Fund (CiCF) together with the assigned CiCF task-team; including responsible for drafting reports to respective donor.
- This post holder is expected to be deployed in the initial phase of response or during recovery phase to support COs in his/her capacity as technical advisor and or Deputy Emergency Response Manager as well as potential seconded to Country Offices to provide technical support in any humanitarian preparedness and readiness work in normal situation.

**Support strengthening COs capacity to be ready to respond**

- Provide support in facilitating CO’s humanitarian related training i.e. Emergency Response Team (ERT) training and CVA training; and other training linking with thematic sector lead in the organization.
- Provide support in roll out the R2R approach to the remaining CO in FY 27/28 together with the Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness, Response and Resilience.

**Support regional coordination and networking**

- The post holder will have to maintain excellent working relationships with colleagues in COs, Nos, the Global Humanitarian Team (APAC) and Regional Hub colleagues.
- This post will also act as thematic leads for different humanitarian networks in APAC in particular the regional Accountability to Affected People (AAP) Working Group, Regional Cash Voucher Assistance (CVA) Working Group, Regional GiHA Working Group and should have a strong Gender in Emergencies understanding and knowledge.

**Accountabilities**

**In non-emergencies: strengthen disaster preparedness, readiness and response capacity**

- Facilitate and support the roll out of various training and capacity building initiatives related to the implementation of the humanitarian scale up priorities.
- Prepare, and periodically update, a disaster/hazard calendar ( the ‘Hotspots analysis’) for the Asia Pacific and undertake an analysis and recommend use of existing early warning systems for Plan’s programming.
- Facilitate and support all countries in the region to go through an intensive Ready to Respond (R2R) Approach and ensure all agreed Minimum Preparedness Action (MPAs) are implemented according to its timeframe.
- Continue promoting the utilization of the Emergency Response manual for Operation and Programme in country offices in the region.
- Manage the emergency response’s database for Asia Pacific and present it in infographic in semester basis including contributing the GHT humanitarian footprint data.
- Facilitate learning and sharing of humanitarian relate resources/tools/experiences between countries in the region.
- Identify and produce a high-quality documentation of evidence in APAC region to justify the contribution for humanitarian scale up priorities in collaboration with MERL Specialists in APAC.
- Support the supervisor and Humanitarian and Resilience Team to review a new Country Strategy document and ensure the inclusion of risks/hazards related to disasters, conflict and environment in their child rights analysis and designed programs accordingly
- Support strengthens external engagement and coordination with other humanitarian actors (UN, NGOs, donors, etc) in the different technical sector through regular attendance in relevant networks and coordination forums, clusters especially on AAP, CPiE, EiE and CVA Network.
- Provide technical support at COs level to increase representation in the humanitarian network i.e. Humanitarian Country Team and other relevant national clusters. Conduct mentoring to COs representative in the leading/coordinating role in the in-county network as required.
- Working in collaboration with APAC technical specialists in development to promote the utilization if the Emergency Response Manual for Programme and promote nexus approach.
- Potential to be seconded to Country Office to provide technical support for humanitarian preparedness and readiness work in normal situation
- Coordinating the APAC Children in Crisis Fund (CiCF) in collaboration with its task force including drafting the donor reports in semester basis.

**In emergencies context**

- In all significant disasters, ready to deploy to assist the assigned ERM/Deputy ERM/Managers/Focal points at country level to design rapid assessment, compile reports, and drafting response plan, in consultations with Country Director and the Emergency Response Management Team (ERMT). The duration of deployment could be vary from 4 – 12 weeks at the initial phase of response.
- In all responses in APAC (regardless the scale), support COs in identifying the surge capacity needs internal COs, within the Region or require support from the Global Roster in close coordination with the supervisor.
- During deployment and or remote support for all emergencies, support strengthen the accountability of the response and the incorporation of Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI), Safeguarding, PSHEA and promoting CVA and MPCA as modality whenever appropriate.
- In the later stage of the response (early recovery and recovery phase) ready to be deployed to support CO in her/his capacity to provide technical support advice both at programmatic and operation as agreed with the Country Management Team and the supervisor. The duration of deployment in this stage could be varied from 4 – 8 weeks-time.
- Support COs in preparing the Real Time Review (RTR) for all orange 2 emergencies and facilitate coordination with the Supervisor.
- Support countries in documentation of lessons from all significant disasters and ensure it circulation to the internal and external organization as needed.

**Key relationships**

**Internal:**

- APAC Humanitarian and Resilience team
- APAC’s Program and Influencing Team
- APAC’s communication Team
- APAC Grants, Admin, Supply Chain and P&C team
- Country Humanitarian Manager/Advisors/ERMs and H&R teams at CO level
- Global Humanitarian Team
- CPiE Network
- EiE Network
- Cash Network
- SRHRiE Network
- GiE Network
- Accountability to Affected People (AAP) Network
- National Organisation’s Humanitarian team especially who in charge for humanitarian work

**External:**

- IASC Network
- Relevant Humanitarian actors to coordinate Plan’s work with other international/regional/national institutions, clusters and donors in line with Plan’s global strategy
- Academics, research institute and thought leaders in humanitarian work in Asia Pacific region

**Technical expertise, skills and knowledge**

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Documented experience from disaster risk management work, including disaster preparedness, readiness and managing response programmes.
- Documented experience from at least 2 major disaster events, working in “disaster /high risk” environments.
- Documented experience as a trainer/facilitator on humanitarian issues especially on international Humanitarian standard and one of the technical sectors CPiE, EiE, CVA, SRHRiE or WASHiE and Gender in Emergencies.
- Ability to priorities and manage complex and varied workload, often to tight deadlines
- Experience of strategy, i.e. analysing relevant factors from both the internal and external environments, identifying crucial issues that have to be addressed, setting objectives and developing plans of actions.
- Excellent communication skills, written and verbal in order to present arguments clearly and powerfully to a variety of audiences.
- Direct experience of working with children and young people and in understanding and responding to their needs and rights.
- Experience of working with institutional donors/fundraisers.
- Experience in utilisation of humanitarian standards i.e. Sphere, CHS, INEE MS on EiE, CPMS and other standards included in the Humanitarian Standard Partnership (HSP).
- Experience of promoting coordination and cooperation with other agencies through networking and alliance building.

**Skills**

- Energetic and motivated individual, with a proven track record of undertaking similar assignments successfully
- Expert in one of the technical sectors such as CPiE or EiE or SRHRiE, WASHiE and familiar with cash voucher assistance (CVA) as modality in emergency situations**.**
- Familiar with the concept of gender in emergencies
- Good interpersonal skills and able to work in a dynamic environment with multiple stakeholders at different level.
- Ability to think strategically, but also result oriented and get things done.
- Commitment to continuous learning and willingness to keep abreast of new developments in the field of humanitarian and resilience and it adherence to the humanitarian principles and standards.
- Able to work independently, but to function within a virtual team.
- Good interpersonal skills and ability to establish and sustain good working relations with colleagues
- Strong negotiation, facilitating, representation and influencing skills including familiar with Artificial Intelligence (AI) for humanitarian work
- Culturally and socially sensitive, and able to work successfully with partners and sector professionals

**Leadership Behaviours**

- Leads the theoretical discussion and strategy development.
- Coaches and builds capacity of both program and support staff in APAC and COs
- Promotes innovation and learning
- Communicates clearly and effectively
- Strong team building and motivational skills
- Critical and creative thinking
- Ability to influence
- Result oriented
- Flexible
- Good interpersonal skills

**Physical Environment and Demands:**

This position entails 50-60 % travel both within and outside region, often in hardship locations.

**Level of Contact with Children:**

Mid contact: Occasional interaction with children

**Plan International’s Values in Practice**

**We are open and accountable**

- Promotes a culture of openness and transparency, including with sponsors and donors.
- Holds self and others accountable to achieve the highest standards of integrity.
- Consistent and fair in the treatment of people.
- Open about mistakes and keen to learn from them.
- Accountable for ensuring we are a safe organisation for all children, girls & young people

**We strive for lasting impact**

- Articulates a clear purpose for staff and sets high expectations.
- Creates a climate of continuous improvement, open to challenge and new ideas.
- Focuses resources to drive change and maximise long-term impact, responsive to changed priorities or crises.
- Evidence-based and evaluates effectiveness.

**We work well together**

- Seeks constructive outcomes, listens to others, willing to compromise when appropriate.
- Builds constructive relationships across Plan International to support our shared goals.
- Develops trusting and ‘win-win’ relationships with funders, partners and communities.
- Engages and works well with others outside the organization to build a better world for girls and all children.

**We are inclusive and empowering**

- We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential
- We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge equality in our programs and our workplace
- We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives

**Physical Environment**

Position is based at Plan International Thailand’s Country Office in Thailand with occasional work in local partner offices as needed for delivering project activities and outcomes.

jobs.title: Action Against Hunger Sudan is looking to recrute a Consultant in Supply Chain
jobs.description:
ACF Sudan is therefore seeking a Supply Chain consultant specialized in procurement and framework agreements for a three-month assignment, with the specific responsibility of managing and implementing prioritized FWA procedures from their initial preparation through to contract signature.

The overall objective of the consultancy is to accelerate the implementation of the mission's Framework Agreement pipeline, ensuring that prioritized agreements are properly prepared, tendered, evaluated, negotiated, and finalized in compliance with ACF procurement procedures and applicable donor requirements.

Required qualifications and experience:
• University degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Procurement, Business Administration, or a related field.
• Significant professional experience in humanitarian supply chain management, with a strong focus on procurement and supplier contracting.
• Strong knowledge of procurement compliance requirements, competitive tendering principles, and procurement documentation standards.
• Previous experience with Action Against Hunger procurement procedures and tools would be a strong asset.
• Previous experience with LINK would be a strong asset.
• Experience coordinating procurement processes involving multiple operational bases, technical departments, and stakeholders.
• Previous experience in Sudan or other complex humanitarian operational contexts would be an asset.
• Excellent organizational, analytical, negotiation, and communication skills.
• Ability to work independently, manage multiple procurement procedures simultaneously, and deliver results within tight deadlines.
• Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Arabic would be an asset.
• Availability to work both remotely and in Sudan, including potential field visits subject to security and access conditions.

For further information and how to apply, please download the [Terms of Reference](https://accioncontraelhambre.org/sites/default/files/2026-10/2026_SD_ToRs_Supply%20chain%20consultant-FV.pdf).

jobs.title: Regional Safety & Security Director
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Context**

The East Africa region supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges – conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation – through integrated, impactful approaches.

The region prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration.

The region responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. EA focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs.

The EA region operates country programs in Uganda, Kenya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, and Ethiopia.

**Position Summary**

The Regional Safety and Security Director (RSSD) is one of the most senior leadership roles in the East Africa region and provides strategic leadership for safety, security, and humanitarian access across the region. They set and drive the implementation of a comprehensive strategy to anticipate, analyze, and mitigate risks, safeguard staff and assets, enable principled humanitarian access, and ensure the continuity of IRC’s operations and programs in complex and high-risk environments.

As the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the Regional Vice President (RVP), the RSSD works alongside the RVP on the decisions that shape IRC’s presence, access, and continuity across the region. They are a full member of the Regional Management Team and of IRC’s global safety and security (S&S) team. Within the Regional Management Team, the RSSD contributes as a senior leader to regional strategy, priorities, and decision-making, not only as the safety and security function, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices. They integrate Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) informed security risk analysis into strategic, operational, programmatic, and partnership decisions so that security considerations are embedded across IRC’s work.

Reporting jointly to the RVP and the Senior Director for Safety and Security (SDSS), the RSSD operates with significant autonomy and influence. Working in close partnership with Country Directors, they ensure that each country program has robust, context-appropriate protocols, systems, and capacities in place to address unique threats and challenges, while remaining agile to adapt to shifting environments.

The RSSD maintains in-depth knowledge of security dynamics across all EA countries, monitors early warning indicators, and deploys regularly, including at short notice, to support local teams. They play a central role in mentoring and building the capabilities of IRC staff and leaders to operate safely and effectively, thereby strengthening IRC’s ability to reach and serve the most affected and underserved populations.

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership and Regional Management**

- As a member of the Regional Management Team, contribute as a senior leader to regional strategy, priority-setting, and decision-making, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices across the region rather than representing the safety and security function alone.
- Serve as the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the RVP, enabling timely, risk-informed decisions on humanitarian access, operational continuity, and duty of care, and jointly activating and leading crisis management when required.
- Partner with Country Directors to align safety, security, and humanitarian access with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs) and operational priorities, supporting their decision-making and accountability for risk.

**Security Risk Management**

- Lead and supervise the identification, analysis, and mitigation of S&S risks across the region, ensuring alignment with IRC’s global standards.
- Guide and support Country Directors and field leaders to adapt and implement context-specific security risk management strategies ensuring proactive risk identification, mitigation, and emergency preparedness.
- Review, monitor, and encourage compliance with the Security Minimum Standards (SMS) in all country programs providing follow-up and technical guidance where gaps are identified.
- Drive and champion the development, adaptation, and roll-out of global and regional initiatives on duty of care and safeguarding, embedding these into operational culture and practice.
- Shape and strengthen safety and security policies, procedures, and practices that fully integrate Gender Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (GEDI) principles as well as Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) commitments.
- Extend IRC’s security capacity to partners, ensuring they receive tailored risk management support, access to systems, and benefit from IRC’s standards relevant to their operational contexts.
- Build and maintain an active network of IRC security focal points across country programs and cultivate strong external relationships with professional contacts, peer agencies, and security counterparts to enhance collective risk management.

**Humanitarian Access Management**

- Enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access across country programs, ensuring communities can be reached and served in line with IRC’s country Strategy Action Plans (SAP).
- Strengthen and expand humanitarian access teams and capabilities across the region, building skills, systems, and approaches that enhance operational reach and acceptance.
- Develop, adapt, and implement context-specific guidelines for humanitarian access and engagement with state and non-state actors, ensuring alignment with IRC policy, international humanitarian law, and standards.
- Advise and guide country programs in the design of operational and programmatic contingency plans ensuring preparedness for sudden shifts in political, security, or conflict dynamics.
- Collaborate with relevant IRC units to ensure prompt and appropriate follow-up to violations of IRC’s Code of Conduct and breaches of humanitarian principles, reinforcing accountability and ethical operations.

**Performance Management and Development**

- Lead and actively contribute to the recruitment and selection of key positions with S&S responsibilities, ensuring high-caliber talent and diverse representation.
- Co-manage and mentor direct-report staff (under the Management in Partnership (MiP) model with Country Directors), setting clear expectations, defining performance objectives, providing regular, timely feedback, and conducting documented performance reviews that drive accountability and growth.
- Promote and safeguard staff well-being, monitoring staff care across the region and supporting appropriate interventions to address the needs of both national and international staff.
- Directly supervise and develop the Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Coordinator, ensuring progressive and forward-looking S&S plans that align with regional priorities and organizational strategy.

**Learning & Development**

- Design, support, and supervise the implementation of regional capacity-building plans, ensuring effective delivery of IRC’s global S&S training programs across EA country programs.
- Embed gender-sensitive approaches into all capacity development and learning initiatives, addressing gender-specific risks and ensuring inclusivity in staff preparedness.
- Lead and facilitate critical incident management trainings and simulations, in close coordination with the global S&S unit to strengthen preparedness and response capacities across the region.

**Incident Management**

- Support country programs to ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality incident notification, reporting, analysis, and dissemination of lessons learned.
- Serve as a member of the Regional Incident Management Team actively supporting the RVP in the management and resolution of Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents.
- Facilitate After-Action Reviews ensuring that corrective measures are clearly defined, documented, and systematically implemented in line with established incident protocols.
- Oversee and monitor the SHIELD incident database producing quarterly trend analyses to inform strategic decision-making and strengthen regional risk mitigation.

**Key Working Relationships**

- Reports to: Regional Vice President, East Africa, and Senior Director, Global Safety & Security (matrixed reporting)
- Member of: Regional Management Team and IRC’s global Safety & Security team
- Partners closely with: the Regional Vice President, as principal safety and security advisor, and Country Directors on country risk, humanitarian access, and duty of care
- Manages: Regional Humanitarian Access & Security Coordinator; and, through Management in Partnership with the respective Country Directors, country Security Leads
- Collaborates with: fellow Regional Safety & Security Directors, the Director of Security Learning & Operations, the Global Duty of Care Director, People & Culture, and other members of the Regional Management Team; and, externally, with peer agencies, security networks, and relevant counterparts

**Qualifications & Requirements**

- At least 10 years’ experience in international humanitarian assistance, with proven ability to plan, organize, and lead security management operations.
- Prior experience in EA with strong knowledge of regional and country dynamics is essential.
- Fluency in English required; proficiency in a relevant regional language (e.g. Arabic, Amharic, Somali, or Swahili) is an asset.
- Demonstrated grounding in humanitarian principles, codes of conduct, NGO culture, and proven success in gender-sensitive security management and gender equality.
- Skilled at influencing without authority and building effective relationships across multinational teams, partners, and stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge through mentoring, coaching, and non-formal methods.
- Strong capacity to analyze and present complex security dynamics and incidents clearly and on short notice, highlighting implications for operations.
- Willingness and ability to travel up to 40% of the time.

**Work Environment**

This position is open to both national and international applicants, in the locations indicated as well as potentially other IRC locations open to hosting. We will, however, prioritize consideration of national candidates from the region and for which our highly competitive national salary scale and benefits will apply.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based, are currently located outside your home country, and possess over 4 years of international work experience, the IRC has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing, and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion:** at IRC, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply for this role, and are committed to supporting them through flexible working arrangements, safety and duty of care planning tailored to the East African countries’ context, and a workplace culture that values the leadership women bring to humanitarian response.

In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: National Consultant - Telephony systems for UXO
jobs.description:
1. ## BACKGROUND & PROJECT DESCRIPTION

Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) remains one of the countries most heavily affected by unexploded ordnance (UXO) contamination. Despite significant progress in survey, clearance, risk education, and victim assistance, UXO continues to pose humanitarian, social, and economic challenges, particularly in rural and remote communities. UXO accidents continue to result in death and injury, while the presence of contamination restricts access to land, livelihoods, infrastructure development, and essential services.

The Government of Lao PDR has demonstrated its commitment to addressing the impact of UXO through the implementation of the National Strategic Plan for the UXO Sector in the Lao PDR 2021–2030, “Safe Path Forward III” (SPF III), Sustainable Development Goal 18 (SDG 18): Lives Safe from UXO, and its obligations under the Convention on Cluster Munitions (CCM). The National Regulatory Authority for the UXO/Mine Action Sector (NRA) serves as the national coordinating body responsible for policy oversight, sector coordination, information management, quality management, victim assistance coordination, and risk education.

An effective reporting and coordination mechanism is essential to support the achievement of these national objectives. Timely reporting of suspected UXO, rapid coordination of emergency response following accidents, effective referral of survivors to appropriate services, and mechanisms for public feedback and complaints are all critical components of a responsive and accountable UXO sector.

Hotline 1603 was established to serve as a national point of contact for UXO-related reporting and coordination. The hotline is intended to provide communities and stakeholders with an accessible mechanism to report suspected UXO items and instigate UXO removal report accidents and emergencies, seek information regarding UXO-related services, facilitate referral to victim assistance services, and communicate complaints or feedback regarding UXO sector activities.

As the sector looks towards the future, it is evident that increasingly, a robust telephony mechanism to support Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) will be needed as clearance operators increasingly will rely on community reporting of ordnance being found.

While Hotline 1603 has been operational for several years, its functionality remains limited. Current operations rely largely on manual processes and direct routing of calls to NRA personnel, resulting in inconsistent documentation, limited case tracking, and challenges in monitoring response actions. Standardized procedures, institutional arrangements, and technical systems remain underdeveloped, reducing the overall effectiveness and sustainability of the mechanism. The system is also affected by a high volume of non-genuine calls and lacks a structured approach for data management, service monitoring, and grievance handling.

Furthermore, the long-term operational model for Hotline 1603 has not yet been fully assessed. Questions remain regarding the most appropriate institutional arrangements, management structure, technical requirements, staffing needs, financing requirements, and sustainability options. Several implementation approaches may be considered, including direct management by the NRA, outsourcing to telecommunications providers or call center operators, or hybrid arrangements combining government oversight with external service delivery.

Recognizing the need for a strategic review of Hotline 1603, the NRA seeks to engage a qualified national or international individual consultant or consulting firm to assess the current system, identify operational and institutional needs, evaluate implementation options, and develop a practical roadmap for establishing Hotline 1603 as a sustainable national mechanism for UXO reporting, emergency response coordination, victim assistance referral, and grievance redress.

1. ## Objective

To develop a practical and evidence-based implementation roadmap for Hotline 1603 as a sustainable national mechanism for UXO reporting, emergency response coordination, referral to victim assistance services, and grievance redress in Lao PDR.

1. ## SCOPE OF WORK

The successful applicant will be expected to be responsible for the following:

***Task 1: Assessment of Existing Hotline System***

- Existing call management arrangements and workflows
- Current reporting, referral, and response processes
- Institutional roles and responsibilities
- Existing data collection and reporting practices
- Existing complaint and feedback handling mechanisms
- Strengths, weaknesses, risks, and operational challenges

***Task 2: Assessment of Needs and Requirements***

- Institutional and governance requirements
- Human resource and capacity needs
- Technical and infrastructure requirements
- Information management (IMSMA) requirements
- Victim assistance referral requirements
- Grievance redress requirements
- Resource and sustainability considerations

***Task 3: Analysis of System/Implementation Options***

***Option A – NRA-managed (In-house) Model***

- Operational requirements
- Resource implications
- Advantages and limitations

**Option B – Outsourced Model**

- Telecommunications provider-managed solutions
- Call center service provider arrangements
- Cost and operational implications

**Option C – Other Models**

- Alternative institutional and operational arrangements identified through the assessment process
- Operational and technical requirements
- Resource implications
- Advantages, limitations, and risks
- Sustainability considerations

***Task 4: Development of Implementation Roadmap***

- Institutional and governance arrangements
- Operational framework
- Roles and responsibilities
- Technology and infrastructure requirements
- Human resource and capacity development requirements
- Estimated implementation costs and resource requirements
- Risk assessment and mitigation measures
- Implementation timeline and milestones
- Sustainability considerations

**Proposed methodology**

**Defining Scope of Work, methodology**

- Drafting of an inception report detailing the proposed methodology, workplan, stakeholder engagement approach, and assessment framework

**Desk review**

- Review relevant national policies, strategies, and frameworks related to UXO reporting, emergency response coordination, victim assistance, and grievance redress, including Safe Path Forward III (SPF III), SDG 18, and relevant NRA policies and procedures
- Review existing Hotline 1603 documentation, reports, operational arrangements, and available data
- Review existing information management systems, reporting mechanisms, and referral pathways relevant to UXO reporting, victim assistance, and grievance management
- Review hotline management, call centre, and grievance redress models implemented in Lao PDR and comparable contexts to identify good practices and lessons learned
- Identify key institutional, operational, technical, and sustainability considerations relevant to the future development of Hotline 1603

**Primary data collection**

- Based on information gaps identified in the desk review, prepare interview guides for facilitating key informant interviews and/or multi-stakeholder consultation(s) to gather in-depth feedback from partners.
- Assess current workflows, institutional arrangements, reporting processes, referral pathways, and operational challenges.
- Identify stakeholder expectations, system requirements, and opportunities for improvement
- Present a debrief of the emerging findings and recommendations from the desk review and primary data collection

**Options Assessment and Roadmap Development**

- Assess feasible implementation options, including NRA-managed (in-house), outsourced, and other models
- Analyze the advantages, limitations, risks, resource requirements, and sustainability considerations of each option
- Recommend the most suitable implementation model for Hotline 1603
- Develop a phased implementation roadmap, including governance arrangements, operational requirements, resource needs, implementation timeline, and sustainability measures

***Present findings***

- Consolidate findings from the desk review, stakeholder consultations, and options assessment into a draft implementation roadmap
- Present key findings, recommendations, and the proposed implementation roadmap to NRA and relevant stakeholders for review and validation
- Facilitate discussion and collect stakeholder feedback on the proposed implementation model and roadmap
- Incorporate stakeholder feedback and revise the draft implementation roadmap
- Submit the draft implementation roadmap for review
- Make any amendments or adjustments as necessary
- Submit final Implementation Roadmap

1. ## Deliverables & Implementation Timeline

The inception report should clearly describe the proposed methodology, workplan, stakeholder engagement approach, and assessment framework to be applied throughout the assignment. The report should demonstrate how the consultant will assess the existing Hotline 1603 system, identify institutional and operational needs, evaluate implementation options, and develop a practical implementation roadmap. The inception report shall be presented to the NRA and relevant stakeholders for review and may be revised based on feedback.

The consultant shall undertake a comprehensive desk review of relevant national policies, strategies, procedures, and operational documents related to UXO reporting, emergency response coordination, victim assistance, and grievance redress. The consultant shall also conduct stakeholder consultations and system assessments to identify current strengths, gaps, challenges, and opportunities for strengthening Hotline 1603.

Based on the findings, the consultant shall assess feasible implementation options, including in-house, outsourced, and other models, and recommend the most appropriate approach for the Lao context.

The final implementation roadmap should provide clear recommendations on institutional arrangements, governance structures, operational requirements, human resource needs, technical requirements, implementation timelines, resource requirements, and sustainability considerations for the future development of Hotline 1603. The roadmap should be practical, achievable, and aligned with national priorities and the objectives of the UXO sector.

**Deliverables (expected days work/target due)**

Inception Report, including methodology, workplan, stakeholder mapping, and assessment framework (3 - 20/11/2026)

Draft report including assessment, recommendations and roadmap (15 - 21/12/2026)

Final report incorporating feedback from stakeholders (2 - 30/12/2026)

1. ## Duration of Assignment, Duty Station & Expected Places of Travel

**Estimated number of working days: 20 working days over a period of 1.5 months tentatively from 11/16/2026 to 12/30/2026, subject to contract award.**

**Duty station**: Home-based

**Expected places of travel**: None

1. ## PROVISION OF MONITORING & PROGRESS CONTROL

In the inception report, a timeline of activities and deliverables will be drafted and agreed upon between the consultant and the client. As above, a brief weekly meeting will be submitted to the client to update the client on progress against the timeline. Any delays or anticipated problems should be highlighted so that the client might unblock any issues where possible.

1. ## ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT & REFERENCE DOCUMENTS

### Administrative Support

The National Regulatory Authority for the UXO/Mine Action Sector (NRA), with support from the UNDP UXO Unit, will facilitate introductions to relevant stakeholders and provide access to available documents, reports, and information necessary for the assignment.

### Reference Documents

Safe Path Forward III

1. ## DEGREE OF EXPERTISE & QUALIFICATIONS

***Guidance:***

- *Please only add criteria **which can be assessed via CV desk review**. To assess writing skill, report samples must be submitted.*
- *Skills which can only be assessed via interview (e.g. speaking or presentation skills) should **not** be included here unless an interview is specifically required for assessment.*

**Qualifications**

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or higher) in Public Administration, Public Policy, Information Management, Information Systems, Development Studies, Telecommunications, Social Sciences, Business Administration, or other relevant fields

**Relevant Professional Experience**

- Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in public service delivery systems, information management systems, hotline/call centre systems, grievance redress mechanisms, or related areas.
- *Demonstrated experience in conducting assessments, stakeholder consultations, and developing strategic plans, roadmaps, or operational frameworks.*
- Familiarity with UXO or Mine Action programming would be a distinct advantage.

**Other Competencies**

- *Strong analytical and report-writing skills*
- *Demonstrated experience in qualitative research, stakeholder consultation, and systems assessment*
- *Knowledge of hotline operations, grievance redress mechanisms, referral systems, or customer service platforms would be an advantage*
- *Familiarity with institutional governance arrangements, operational planning, and implementation roadmaps.*

**Language Requirements**

- Fluency in English

1. ## PAYMENT TERMS

***Guidance**:*

- *Depending on the assignment’s duration, there should be a limited number of payment milestones in order to reduce the paperwork and workload for project assistant(s).*
- *Specify payment milestones (e.g. 10% upon receipt and acceptance of detailed workplan, 30% upon acceptance of Output 1, etc.).*
- *Since time is required to review/approve outputs prior to authorizing payments, clarify that the submission of deliverables does not equate to immediate payment.*
- *Please note that **NO advance payment should be made**.*

jobs.title: Expression of Interest – Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer, Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program
jobs.description:
**About DT Global**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**Program Context**

The Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program is a DFAT funded program that is part of the Pacific Australia Skills work in Solomon Islands. Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across Timor-Leste and the Pacific. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of prior Australian Government support for skills and training in Timor-Leste. The SIRIS program will focus on support for rural training centres (RTCs) and other training providers to strengthen their institutional capability, improve the quality and relevance of skills delivery, and respond effectively to labour-market needs. Effective delivery of the activity will require coordinated planning across program, operational and technical functions, with resources aligned to agreed activities and results.

**About the Role**

We are seeking **Expressions of Interest** for **SIRIS program Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer** position for an upcoming Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program. The SIRIS MEL Officer is responsible for supporting the implementation of Pacific Australia Skills’ MEL Plan and System in the Solomon Islands country office. The role will focus on aligning the Pacific Australia Skills’ overarching program logic and MEL Plan to the Solomon Islands country context. The position will work closely with the Solomon Islands Country MEL Coordinator and other Country MEL Coordinators in data collection and writing reports for their country. The SIRIS program MEL Officer together with the Solomon Islands MEL Country Coordinator will report to the Solomon Islands Country Director. They will receive significant guidance and support from the regional MEL team (based in Suva) to ensure they have relevant tools and skills to fulfil their roles.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

- **MEL Plan and System**: Assist the Country Director to implement and strengthen a country-specific program logic and MEL Plan which flows from the overarching Pacific Australia Skills program logic and MEL Plan.
- **Data collection and monitoring:** Collect, analyse and maintain relevant MEL data to monitor progress against the Solomon Islands Country Strategy, Country Workplan and MEL Plan. This may include implementing student and employer surveys, conduct organisational capacity assessments, and develop case studies. Data will be entered into the Pacific Australia Skills Management Information System (MIS).
- **Reporting:** Support the Country Director and MEL Coordinator to prepare MEL reports for the Solomon Islands Country Office reporting, including the country annex of the program annual report and inputs to monthly reports and any other reports required by DFAT and partners.
- **Adaptive Management & Learning:** Assist the MEL Coordinator with facilitation of regular reflection sessions, learning events, and knowledge-sharing activities to integrate MEL insights into program improvement. Contribute to an ongoing process of testing, refining and further developing the program logic and its key assumptions.
- **Communication**: Support the development of evidence-based communication products that demonstrate the progress, results and contributions to Solomon Islands’ priorities by the SIRIS project and the broader Solomon Islands program. This may include identifying success stories, case studies, photographs and other relevant evidence for use in use in Pacific Australia Skills communications, reporting and public diplomacy activities. Ensure appropriate consent and safeguarding requirements are followed when collecting and using participant information and stories
- **Capacity Building:** Support MEL capacity building for Pacific Australia Skills’ in-country partners, especially the Rural Training Centres, with a focus on assisting them to develop appropriate systems and tools for monitoring, reporting and learning.
- **Evaluation & Research:** Support the implementation of evaluations, reviews and research activities related to the SIRIS project and other Solomon Islands MEL priorities, as required.
- Other duties: Undertake other MEL-related duties as required.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position: [https://tinyurl.com/7xjhb9yp](https://tinyurl.com/7xjhb9yp)

**Selection Criteria**

Essential Experience and Knowledge

- Qualifications in research, MEL, social sciences, international development, or related field.
- Minimum 5 years of experience in MEL, including developing program logics and MEL Plans.
- Experience implementing data collection and analysis.
- Ability to translate complex data into actionable insights and facilitate learning.
- Strong organisational and communication skills, with the ability to train and mentor others.
- Experience working in cross-cultural settings with a strong understanding of participatory approaches.
- Experience working with international development projects, NGOs, or donor-funded initiatives is an advantage.
- Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental protection, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.
- DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities.
- People with lived experience of the regions in which Pacific Australia Skills operate are strongly encouraged to apply.

***Please note:***

**About the Role**

We are seeking **Expressions of Interest** for **SIRIS program Activity Lead** position for an upcoming Solomon Islands RTC Institutional Strengthening (SIRIS) Program. The SIRIS programActivity Lead is accountable for coordinating all program activities implemented to support RTCs and training providers. The role will translate approved plans into coordinated delivery; ensure that budgets, staffing and technical inputs match planned activities; oversee the Activity Support Team; monitor progress, risks and results; and provide timely advice and reporting to the Country Director. The SIRIS program Activity Lead will work across operations, skills delivery, skills development reform, communications, MEL and partnerships management to maintain an integrated approach to implementation.

The role is responsible for converting the approved rationale and delivery approach for each activity into sequenced implementation plans, ensuring value for money, managing dependencies and supporting achievement of the agreed outputs and impacts within the work-plan period.

1\. Strengthening Trainer Capability at RTCs and SINU TAFE: Upskill trainers to meet national quality standards, particularly Quality Standard 8 on trainer competence, and strengthen learner-centered, workplace-relevant and inclusive delivery.

2\. Strengthening RTC and SINU TAFE Institutional Capacity: Strengthen selected RTCs and SINU TAFE to deliver quality-assured, inclusive and demand-driven skills development through sustained technical assistance, accompaniment, equipment and improvements to training spaces.

3\. Transitioning RTCs to Technical Colleges: Provide targeted top-up technical assistance and facility upgrades to enable two RTCs to transition to Technical College status and generate practical guidance for future transitions.

**Cross-cutting**

Across all three activities, the SIRIS program Activity Lead will ensure locally led development, gender equity, disability inclusion, youth inclusion and access for rural and remote communities are integrated into planning and delivery. The role will embed safeguarding, accessibility, climate-change and disaster-resilience considerations where relevant; coordinate communications and public-diplomacy opportunities; maintain alignment with SITESA and national TVET reforms; manage synergies with other DFAT investments; and document evidence, lessons and value-for-money decisions.

## **Activity Planning and Coordination**

- Lead integrated work planning, scheduling and coordination of all institutional strengthening support to RTCs and training providers.
- Maintain a consolidated activity plan that identifies outputs, milestones, responsibilities, dependencies, resource requirements and delivery timeframes.
- Coordinate inputs from technical and enabling teams and resolve gaps, overlaps, or sequencing issues affecting delivery.
- Ensure activities respond to provider priorities and are consistent with approved program strategies, plans and commitments.
- Convene regular implementation meetings and maintain clear records of decisions, actions and accountabilities.

## **Resource and Operational Management**

- Translate activity plans into realistic budget, staffing, procurement and logistical requirements.
- Work with the Operations team to align forecasts, procurement plans, compliance requirements, resource availability, contracting, travel and payments with implementation schedules.
- Monitor expenditure and staff allocations against approved plans, investigate variances and recommend timely corrective action.
- Confirm that funds, people and other inputs are available when required and are used efficiently, transparently and for their intended purpose.
- Prepare and maintain activity-level costings, cash-flow forecasts and resource plans that support funding decisions and demonstrate value for money.
- Support accurate financial and operational reporting while maintaining appropriate records and compliance with applicable policies and procedures.

## **Team Leadership**

- Provide day-to-day leadership, direction and workload coordination for the Activity Support Team.
- Set clear expectations, delegate responsibilities, monitor performance and provide regular coaching and feedback.
- Promote collaboration, accountability, safeguarding, inclusion and respectful workplace practices.
- Identify capability needs and support staff development and continuous improvement.

## **Training Provider and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Maintain productive working relationships with RTCs, training providers, relevant government counterparts, communities, industry and program partners.
- Coordinate consultation, assessment, planning and follow-up with providers so that support is practical, demand-led and locally appropriate.
- Communicate plans, roles, expectations, progress and changes clearly to internal and external stakeholders.
- Coordinate transparent provider and cohort selection, partnership agreements and MOUs in line with approved criteria, SITESA processes and program commitments.
- Escalate sensitive, strategic or unresolved issues to the Country Director with options for action.

## **Monitoring, Learning, Risk and Reporting**

- Work with the MEL team to establish activity-level indicators, evidence requirements, and practical data collection arrangements.
- Track delivery against milestones, budgets and intended results, and use evidence and feedback to improve implementation.
- Maintain current activity risks, issues and dependencies, assign mitigation actions and escalate matters that may affect scope, cost, quality, timing, or reputation.
- Provide concise, accurate and timely progress, financial and management reports to the Country Director and contribute to broader program reporting.
- Capture lessons, good practice and examples of change, working with Communications and Partnerships Management to share approved information appropriately.

## **Cross-functional Coordination**

- Coordinate closely with Skills Delivery and Skills Development Reform teams to align institutional strengthening with technical assistance, training delivery and reform priorities.
- Work with Communications to plan appropriate visibility, knowledge products and stakeholder communications.
- Partner with Operations, MEL and Partnerships Management to ensure coherent delivery, compliance, evidence use and relationship management.
- Maintain an integrated portfolio view, actively managing sequencing, shared resources, provider readiness and dependencies between institutional strengthening and Technical College transition.
- Undertake other reasonable duties aligned with the role and program objectives, as directed by the Country Director.

**Selection Criteria**

### **Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- Tertiary qualification in skills development, education, combined with qualifications in project management, business development, international development or a related field; or substantial equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, multi-stakeholder activities, preferably in skills development and in school systems strengthening.
- Strong project management capability, including work planning, scheduling, budget monitoring, resource allocation, risk management, and reporting.
- Experience coordinating finance, procurement, logistics and technical inputs to meet delivery milestones.
- Proven ability to lead and supervise staff, manage workloads, and support individual and team performance.
- Strong relationship-management skills and experience working with training providers, government, communities, development partners or similar stakeholders.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation and interpersonal skills, including the ability to present clear advice to senior management.
- Strong analytical, organisational, problem-solving and time-management skills, with attention to detail and follow-through.
- Ability to work effectively across diverse, cross-cultural and geographically dispersed teams and to travel within Solomon Islands as required.
- Experience working on international development programs in Solomon Islands, Melanesia or the wider Pacific.
- Knowledge of the Solomon Islands technical and vocational education and training environment, including RTC operating contexts.
- Experience engaging with donors and managing partner agreements or grants.

### **Desirable**

- Demonstrated high level of customer service skills with experience in solving problems associated with highly complex systems.
- Demonstrated high level of interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills including the ability to relate effectively, collaboratively and ethically to staff, learners and other stakeholders (including the ability to liaise with industry and partner institutions).

- Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental protection, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.

- Contributes to design and implementation of effective M & E system for country work using both qualitative and quantitative indicators.
- Contributes to Pacific Partnership EVAWG project donor reports.
- Applies learnings to improve programme performance.
- Identifies and documents performance stories, case studies and outcomes of SPC Pacific Partnership EVAWG project work in country.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Technical expertise**

- Good knowledge of Vanuatu and an understanding of education and broader development challenges in the country and region.

- Proven experience in report writing, analysis, financial and narrative project reporting.

**Contract Duration** – This position is budgeted until 31 December 2027.
