jobs.title: Project Associate
jobs.description:
Background

The Philippines' recent transition to upper-middle-income status has increased the importance of aligning economic growth with sustainability, digital transformation, and human rights accountability. As sectors such as mining, renewable energy, agribusiness, tourism, infrastructure, and digital platforms expand, governance challenges related to community grievances, land and resource disputes, labor rights, environmental impacts, and stakeholder participation persist, often disproportionately affecting women and marginalized groups.

To address these challenges, the Philippines initiated work on a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights (NAP-BHR), led by the Presidential Human Rights Committee Secretariat (PHRCS). While several ASEAN countries have already institutionalized their NAPs, the Philippines remains in the development stage. Recent efforts have accelerated under the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan 2024-2028, including the establishment of a multi-agency technical working group to develop a NAP-BHR focused on responsible business conduct, Indigenous Peoples' rights, and ancestral domains.

The FAIR BHR Project seeks to strengthen Business and Human Rights (BHR) governance by promoting more integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approaches that connect sustainability, human rights, accountability, conflict sensitivity, and stakeholder engagement. The project will support the Philippine government in building evidence, raising awareness, strengthening coordination, and fostering inclusive dialogue to inform BHR reforms.

The initiative will also promote stronger collaboration among UN agencies, leveraging complementary expertise and positioning UNDP as a strategic convener. As an initial pilot, the project will generate evidence and lessons to inform longer-term programming and the development of a comprehensive Project Document supporting the institutionalization of BHR in the Philippines.

UNDP Philippines is seeking a Project Associate to support the Institutions and Partnerships (I&P) Programme Team. As part of the Project Management Unit (PMU), the incumbent will primarily support the implementation of the FAIR BHR Project and contribute to the effective coordination, implementation, and monitoring of the team's programme and project portfolio to ensure the timely delivery of activities and achievement of results.

Scope of work

Provides support to overall effective and efficient management and monitoring of project:

- Contribute to the development of project’s annual and quarterly work plans, procurement plan, human resources recruitment plan, travel plan and financial and physical progress reports;

- Keep track of the delivery of the project and contracted parties, and frequently report to the Project Coordinator on the delivery situation;

- Maintenance of the internal expenditures control system including budget checks and timely corrective actions on unposted vouchers, including the vouchers with budget check errors, match exceptions, unapproved vouchers;

- Work closely with the Programme Team, Results and Quality Team, Procurement Team and Finance Team to ensure efficient and transparent use of project resources in line with approved budgets and within UNDP rules and regulations;

- Support to the conduct of project reviews, audits, monitoring missions, evaluations;

- Support timely operational and financial closure of a project, determination of unutilized funds and processing operational/financial closure of projects;

- Support in drafting terms of reference and support the recruitment and management of national and international consultants, subject matter experts, consulting firms, and other such resources.

Ensures implementation of operational strategies, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance of operational activities with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and strategies.

- Provision of inputs to the CO administrative business processes and implementation of the internal standard operating procedures (SOPs)

- Undertake administrative, finance and procurement procedures, such as travel processing, liquidations of cash advances, processing of payments to suppliers, canvassing/collection of price quotations and payment of utilities;

- Support to small-value procurement and coordinating with the suppliers for the delivery of goods;

- Raise requisitions as required and register as general user role in Quantum.

- Provision of inputs to the project team results-oriented workplan

Support to ensure the efficient administrative support, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support to the coordination of travel arrangements such as preparation of travel requests, coordination with travel unit for travel authorizations, booking and reservation of hotel rooms, ticket bookings, and visa.

- Support to the organization of workshops and meetings including transportation services, booking of conference room, compiling of documents, arranging of equipment, among other similar administrative activities.

- Support to maintain an accurate and reliable filing system;

Provides support to proper supply and assets management, focusing on achievement of the following result:

- Support to the coordination of assets management in the unit, timely preparation and submission of periodic inventory reports.

- Support to the coordination of the provision of reliable and quality office supplies.

Supports knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support to organization of trainings and events

- Provision of inputs to lessons learnt and best practices in programme including meeting documentation, drafting of communication letters, and logging of minutes from project and partner meetings.

- Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Support in preparation of Corporate Requirements including but not limited to annual work plan, quarterly report, and annual report.

- In collaboration with the I&P Team, support the implementation of the common activities of the programme team and the Country Office in general.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the Team Leader, Institutions and Partnerships (I&P) Programme Team, and the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, with technical oversight from the I&P Programme Analyst for Governance and Rule of Law, the Project Associate will support the effective implementation and coordination of programme and project initiatives, primarily for the FAIR BHR Project.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Achieve Results

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, deliver quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL & TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES

Business Management: Operations Management

Ability to effectively plan, organize and oversee the operation's business processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner, Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

Procurement: Procurement Management

The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source

Procurement: Contract Management

Knowledge of contract management concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/ or practical situations

Finance: Accounting (General)

Knowledge of accounting concepts, principles, frameworks, standards, regulations, policies and trends, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations

Finance: Budget management

Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets

Finance: Financial planning and budgeting

Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analysing and reporting.

Finance: Financial reporting and analysis

Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector. Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring. Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including non-financial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Academic Education

- Completion of secondary education is required.

- First level university degree (bachelor's degree) in Business Administration, Management, Entrepreneurship, Accounting, Economics, Finance or other related fields will be given due consideration but is not a requirement.

Minimum years of relevant Work experience

- Minimum of six (6) years (with secondary education) or three (3) years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in administrative, financial, procurement, and/or logistics support at the national or international level is required

Required skills and competencies

- Demonstrated proficiency in ICT applications and Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, for data management, reporting, and administrative support is required.

- At least three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in project and/or financial management is required, including planning and monitoring budgets, developing annual workplans, tracking project implementation, and preparing progress, performance, and financial reports.

Desired additional skills and competencies

- A minimum of three (3) years of experience providing administrative, financial, and/or procurement support to donor-funded, development, humanitarian, or government projects is desirable.

- A minimum of three (3) years of experience using enterprise resource planning (ERP), enterprise risk management (ERM), or other integrated corporate management systems is desirable.

- A minimum of three (3) years of experience working with United Nations agencies, international organizations, NGOs/INGOs, development partners, or government institutions is considered an asset.

Required Language(s) (at working level)

- Fluency in spoken and written English and Filipino is required

Professional Certificates

- Professional certification in procurement, finance, administration, or other relevant disciplines (e.g., CIPS, CPM, ACCA, CPA, or equivalent) is desirable

Travel:

Travels may be required for this position. The incumbent may be required to undertake travel within the Philippines to support project implementation, stakeholder consultations, coordination meetings, capacity-building activities, monitoring missions, and other project-related activities.

The following documents shall be required from the applicants:

- Personal CV or P11 , indicating all past positions held and their main underlying functions, their durations (month/year), the qualifications, as well as the contact details (email and telephone number) of the Candidate, and at least three (3) the most recent professional references of previous supervisors. References may also include peers.

- A cover letter (maximum length: 1 page) indicating why the candidate considers him-/herself to be suitable for the position.

- Transcript of Records and Diploma

- Copies of relevant training certificates (if applicable)

Disclaimer

Applicant information about UNDP rosters:

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

Background

The UNDP Global Centre for Technology, Innovation and Sustainable Development (GC-TISD) is part of UNDP’s Digital, AI and Innovation (DAI) Hub, which leverages digital, data, and systems innovation to help governments and partners address complex development challenges through more agile, adaptive, and inclusive approaches.

Based in Singapore, the Global Centre draws on the country’s strengths in technology, policy, and innovation, engaging a broad ecosystem of government agencies, private sector actors, academia, and thought leaders. Through this collaboration, the Centre connects policymakers, practitioners, and experts globally to exchange insights and co-create practical solutions that advance sustainable development.

UNDP is the development arm of the United Nations. Present in 170 countries with over 17,000 people, UNDP works on the world’s biggest challenges, from rising poverty and inequality to a rapidly changing climate, the emergence of crises and the continued degradation and destruction of our natural world. Our UNDP Digital Strategy 2022 – 2025 aims to support our partner countries to unlock the power of digital to tackle these pressing issues. The strategy lays out UNDP’s ambition to use a rights-based approach to digital technologies to improve our development results and help build inclusive digital ecosystems globally that leave no one behind. These aims are supported by the transformation of our internal, operational systems and building an agile, digitally capable workforce

Duties and Responsibilities

UNDP is looking for a Senior Programme Advisor to provide programme coordination, technical analysis, and stakeholder engagement support for the UNDP Global Centre for Technology, Innovation and Sustainable Development (the UNDP Global Centre). The Centre has a particular thematic focus on digital foundations and cyber resilience, trustworthy and inclusive AI, digital and systems thinking, and innovation for climate, sustainability and sustainable finance. The Senior Programme Advisor will report and provide direct support to the Chief Digital Officer and the Head of Global Partnerships and Engagement to scale impact and enable opportunities for collective action, especially through multi-disciplinary and multi-stakeholder coalitions across UNDP’s global network. This is a coordination and technical support role, with a unique opportunity to contribute to how UNDP leverages Singapore’s digital ecosystem to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Under the supervision of the Chief Digital Officer/Director of the DAI Hub, provide operational and analytical support for the annual workplan of the UNDP Global Centre, tracking implementation milestones and delivery of results. This includes:

Programme Planning and Implementation Support:

- Coordinating the design and implementation of the Centre’s programme activities in collaboration with the DAI Hub team and relevant partners;

- Supporting the Head of Global Partnerships on resource mobilization activities, including preparing concept notes and documentation to identify opportunities from development partners, private sector, and key stakeholders;

- Coordinating with the Head of Strategic Resourcing of the DAI Hub on budget tracking and financial management matters, ensuring alignment with UNDP policies, funding arrangements, and corporate requirements;

- Monitoring and providing regular progress updates on Centre activities, flagging implementation risks and proposing adjustments for the consideration of the Chief Digital Officer;

- Collaborating with DAI Hub colleagues to support the development of cohesive offers, proposals, programmes, and projects aligned to the Centre’s thematic focus areas;

- Supporting the Centre’s contribution to UNDP’s broader digital transformation agenda, ensuring the coherence of activities with the DAI Hub’s strategic objectives.

Technical Analysis and Knowledge Support:

- Continuously monitor emerging developments in digital policy, AI, innovation and technology with relevance to sustainable development, preparing research summaries and horizon-scanning briefs for the Chief Digital Officer and DAI Hub leadership;

- Prepare and contribute to knowledge products, policy briefs, reports and presentations that support the Centre’s role as a hub for digital and AI knowledge in development;

- Support the design and delivery of Centre activities, including events, workshops, and convenings, ensuring they are substantively grounded and relevant to policymakers, private sector, academia, and civil society stakeholders;

- Engage with relevant UNDP colleagues in regional bureaux and thematic teams to support alignment of the Centre’s programme with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, providing analytical inputs and briefings as requested.

Stakeholder Coordination and Engagement Support:

- Provide coordination, analytical, and operational support for partnership engagement activities with external and internal stakeholders, under the strategic direction of the Chief Digital Officer and the Head of Partnerships and Engagement of the DAI Hub;

- Under the guidance of the Head of Partnerships and Engagement, support the identification and analysis of partnership opportunities, particularly with private sector actors, digital and technology companies, and innovation institutions in Singapore and the Asia-Pacific region;

- Liaise and coordinate with UNDP regional and central bureaux, including the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific, the Malaysia Country Office, and relevant Global Policy Network (GPN) teams, to ensure effective information-sharing and collaboration;

- Facilitate connections between external stakeholders and UNDP teams, supporting the brokering of knowledge exchanges, expert convenings, and collaborative initiatives under the direction of DAI Hub leadership.

Knowledge Management and UNDP Integration

- Support information flows within and between the UNDP Global Centre, the DAI Hub and its broader digital network, BPPS, and the wider UNDP Global Policy Network, continually identifying opportunities to contribute to UNDP’s impact;

- Keep abreast of major institutional initiatives and relevant events, identifying opportunities for DAI Hub and UNDP engagement, and preparing briefings and inputs as requested;

- Facilitate regular information-sharing and planning with different parts of the DAI Hub and UNDP, identifying opportunities, gaps, and areas for collaboration to ensure the value-added of the Centre’s activities;

- Coordinate the management of donor and partner reporting for the Centre, collecting key results, lessons, and ensuring sound reporting in collaboration with the DAI Hub Partnerships Team, Operations, and Finance;

- Contribute to institutional learning by documenting good practices, lessons learned, and Centre results in accessible knowledge products for the benefit of the DAI Hub and UNDP more broadly;

- Develop benchmarks and methods for monitoring the Centre’s programme performance and reporting against agreed results frameworks.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

- The position will report into Chief Digital Officer/Director of DAI hub.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

Achieve Results:LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy: Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Digital: Digital Ecosystems: Knowledge of how they work, understanding of the opportunities and challenges for governments and Society.

Digital : Artificial intelligence thought leadership: Deep understanding of current and emerging trends in AI, along with their social, ethical, and economic implications, including data privacy and human rights.

Ability to engage with industry experts, government representatives, and academics to stay updated on latest trends and to form partnerships. Strong skills in conducting and interpreting research to support thought leadership initiatives, including white papers, policy briefs, or case studies. Understanding of global trends and cultural nuances, as they relate to the field of AI. Familiarity with international laws and standards regarding technology, particularly in a multi-stakeholder environment like the UN.

Data: Data Analysis: Ability to extract, analyse and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision making

Business Direction & Strategy: Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management: Results-based Management : Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Business Management : Partnerships Management : Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in Public Policy, International Development, Digital Policy, Computer Science, or related discipline is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of a master’s degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 10 years of relevant work experience (with master’s degree) or 12 years of relevant work experience (with bachelor’s degree) in international development, digital policy, or technology for development (international organizations, government, private sector, or civil society.

Required Skills:

- Demonstrated experience in programme coordination and knowledge management within international or multilateral organizations;

- Proven track record of substantive experience in engagement with the Singaporean digital, AI and innovation ecosystem;

- Strong experience building partnerships and facilitating multi-stakeholder collaboration, particularly with private sector, government, and academia;

- Strong professional experience and understanding of the role of digital, technology, and innovation in sustainable development, including work on digital strategies or technology solutions;

- Proven experience developing impactful, outcomes-focused partnerships, particularly with the private sector and digital and AI innovation actors.

Desired Skills:

- Experience in resource mobilization support and donor/partner coordination for global or strategic programmes;

- Experience in working with the Singaporean ecosystem on areas of focus for the Centre;

- Experience working within UNDP or UN system.

Required Languages:

- Fluency in English is required.

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. The Fiji multi-country office covers ten countries including Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Republic of Naoero, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu as well as provides support to regional initiatives.

UNDP in the Pacific has developed its Multi-Country Programme Document (MCPD, 2023-2027) to guide its interventions in the next five years in full alignment and directly to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023–2027). The Office covers 10 countries in the Pacific with an extensive portfolio which has grown over time. The UNSDCF and UNDP MCPD are designed in full alignment with the 2030 agenda, Samoa Pathway, and 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent, which is endorsed by the Pacific Island Countries (PICs) among others. The UNDP Pacific Office next five-year plan strategic priorities are encapsulated under three outcome areas: (i) Planet, (ii) Prosperity, and (iii) Peace. Following a strategic review process which was completed in June 2022, UNDP Pacific office structure is aligned to the emerging priorities of the office. In this regard, the programme portfolio will include mutually reinforcing work streams crafted around two clusters (i) Resilience and Climate Change; and (ii) Inclusive Growth and Effective Governance, supported by a policy and innovations team, operations team, management programme and oversight team, which provides strategic guidance on results management and compliance entrusted with the corporate alignment, programme finance management and quality assurance, and a strategic communications team, which provides knowledge management and communication support to all programme interventions.

Fiji is among the most disaster-prone countries in the Pacific and is exposed to tropical cyclones, floods, storm surges, landslides, droughts, earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic hazards, disease outbreaks and the increasing impacts of climate change. These hazards continue to affect lives, livelihoods, infrastructure, ecosystems and national development.

The National Disaster Management Act 2024 establishes the National Disaster Risk Management Office (NDRMO) as the lead agency responsible for coordinating disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, response, and recovery and resilience-building across Fiji. The Act further provides for the establishment of Divisional Disaster Risk Management Offices to strengthen sub-national coordination and implementation of disaster risk management.

To support implementation of the National Disaster Management Act 2024, the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018–2030, the National Disaster Risk Management Plan, the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Initiative and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) Roadmap, the Government of Fiji, through the UNDP Green Climate Fund Programme, will recruit an IT Assistant to manage and optimize its ICT infrastructure, enterprise platforms, and disaster information systems, while accelerating digital transformation initiatives across Fiji's emergency management system.

Working under the technical direction of the National Coordinator and the Project Manager - EW4All, the Project IT Assistant will ensure the continuous operation (24/7 operational readiness), security, interoperability, real-time disaster monitoring, multi-agency coordination, rapid public warning dissemination and enhancement of NDRMO's critical disaster information systems, including: the National Disaster Information System (NDRIS), the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy (NDRRP) Online M&E Tracker, the Asset Management Tracker, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) information and display systems, and the digital platforms driving the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) and Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).

Duties and Responsibilities

The incumbent will serve as the primary focal point for:

- Enterprise ICT Infrastructure & System Administration.

- Multi-Hazard Early Warning & CAP Platform Integration.

- Disaster Information Systems & Analytics.

- 24/7 NEOC and Emergency Operations Support.

- Stakeholder Coordination, Policy & Innovation

1. Maintain enterprise ICT Infrastructure and system administration:

- Infrastructure Management: maintain, optimize, and secure NDRMO’s core servers, enterprise networks, databases, cloud platforms, and storage environments to guarantee high operational availability.

- Security & Continuity: implement robust cybersecurity protocols, role-based user access controls, automated data backup solutions, and disaster recovery plan (DRP) arrangements to ensure continuous service during crisis events.

- Asset Lifecycle & Standards: manage the ICT hardware asset register, software licensing, system upgrades, and hardware refresh planning in full compliance with Government and UNDP standards.

2.Support multi-hazard early warning & CAP platform integration:

- CAP Administration: administer the central National Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) platform, facilitating technical integrations with authorized warning authorities (e.g., FMS, MRD, MSAF, MoHMS).

- Interoperability & Connectivity: maintain digital gateways and API connections between NDRMO systems, the Ministry of Communications, telecommunications providers (mobile network operators), broadcasters, and digital channels for rapid warning fan-out.

- System Testing & Drills: conduct routine technical tests, simulation exercises, and operational readiness checks of all automated public warning dissemination systems.

3.Monitor disaster information systems & analytics:

- NDRIS Administration: maintain and scale the National Disaster Risk Information System (NDRIS) to secure data integrity across historical incident records, loss databases, and situational updates.

- NDRRP Online Tracker: oversee user administration, data quality control, and functional support for the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy (NDRRP) M&E Tracker across participating Government bodies.

- GIS & Business Intelligence: develop dynamic operational dashboards, geospatial visualizations, and reporting tools to support real-time decision-making for leadership.

4. Ensure 24/7 NEOC and emergency operations support:

5.Support stakeholder coordination, policy & innovation:

- Government ICT Alignment: work closely with the Ministry of Communications and national technology partners to align NDRMO systems with broader e-Government and national cybersecurity frameworks.

- Emerging Technologies: evaluate and advise leadership on integrating emerging technologies (e.g., geospatial analysis, automated alerts, AI analytics, mobile applications) into national disaster management.

- Capacity Building: develop technical documentation, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and user training programs for NDRMO personnel and inter-agency partners.

6.Support knowledge building and knowledge sharing relevant to the project:

- Participate in training on IT or related matters for the staff and provide support to the organization of training and other capacity building activities as needed.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. The Fiji multi-country office covers ten countries including Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Republic of Naoero, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu as well as provides support to regional initiatives.

UNDP in the Pacific has developed its Multi-Country Programme Document (MCPD, 2023-2027) to guide its interventions in the next five years in full alignment and directly to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023–2027). The Office covers 10 countries in the Pacific with an extensive portfolio which has grown over time. The UNSDCF and UNDP MCPD are designed in full alignment with the 2030 agenda, Samoa Pathway, and 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent, which is endorsed by the Pacific Island Countries (PICs) among others. The UNDP Pacific Office next five-year plan strategic priorities are encapsulated under three outcome areas: (i) Planet, (ii) Prosperity, and (iii) Peace. Following a strategic review process which was completed in June 2022, UNDP Pacific office structure is aligned to the emerging priorities of the office. In this regard, the programme portfolio will include mutually reinforcing work streams crafted around two clusters (i) Resilience and Climate Change; and (ii) Inclusive Growth and Effective Governance, supported by a policy and innovations team, operations team, management programme and oversight team, which provides strategic guidance on results management and compliance entrusted with the corporate alignment, programme finance management and quality assurance, and a strategic communications team, which provides knowledge management and communication support to all programme interventions.

Fiji is among the most disaster-prone countries in the Pacific and is exposed to tropical cyclones, floods, storm surges, landslides, droughts, earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic hazards, disease outbreaks and the increasing impacts of climate change. These hazards continue to affect lives, livelihoods, infrastructure, ecosystems and national development.

The National Disaster Management Act 2024 establishes the National Disaster Risk Management Office (NDRMO) as the lead agency responsible for coordinating disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, response, and recovery and resilience-building across Fiji. The Act further provides for the establishment of Divisional Disaster Risk Management Offices to strengthen sub-national coordination and implementation of disaster risk management.

To support implementation of the National Disaster Management Act 2024, the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018–2030, the National Disaster Risk Management Plan, the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Initiative and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) Roadmap, the Government of Fiji, through the UNDP Green Climate Fund Programme, will recruit a Communications & Public Relations Assistant to lead strategic communications, public information, media engagement and awareness activities that promote disaster risk reduction, climate resilience and the objectives of the GCF EW4All Project and the NDRMO.

Working under the technical direction of the Manager Emergency Planning Coordination (NDRMO) and the Project Manager - EW4All, the Project Communications & Public Relations Assistant will ensure timely, accurate, and accessible disaster information, strengthen public confidence, and support the implementation of Fiji’s Multi Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) and Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of Key Functions:

The incumbent will serve as the primary focal point for:

- Strategic Communications: develop and implement communication strategies, annual plans, and public education campaigns.

- Disaster Risk Communication: lead awareness initiatives, risk communication strategies, and behaviour change campaigns.

- Media & Partnerships: build strong partnerships with broadcasters, telecoms, and digital platforms to ensure rapid dissemination of alerts.

- Emergency Public Information: coordinate official messaging during National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) activations, ensuring consistency and accuracy.

- Digital Engagement: manage NDRMO’s website, social media, and digital channels with inclusive, multilingual content.

- Trust & Feedback: establish mechanisms to counter misinformation, strengthen transparency, and capture community feedback for continuous improvement.

1.Provide strategic and risk communications:

- Strategy & Planning: develop and implement NDRMO’s Communication Strategy, Annual Communication Plan, and national public awareness campaigns supporting disaster risk reduction (DRR), preparedness, response, and recovery.

- Risk & Emergency Communication: lead proactive risk communication to promote accurate and consistent public information before, during, and after disasters.

- Programme Integration: coordinate communication strategies for key NDRMO initiatives, including the Green Climate Fund (GCF) Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Project, Fiji’s Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS), and the National Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).

2.Disseminate emergency operations & public information:

- NEOC Coordination: serve as the focal point for public information during National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) activations, ensuring real-time, accurate, and consistent official warnings and situation reports.

- Direct Dissemination: leverage the National CAP Platform to coordinate multi-channel public warnings across broadcasters, mobile networks, social media, websites, and community channels.

3.Facilitate media engagement & stakeholder partnerships:

- Partner Collaboration: build and maintain strong working relationships with the Ministry of Information, Ministry of Communications, broadcasters, telecommunications providers, and digital platforms.

- Misinformation & Public Trust: monitor media channels to detect misinformation/disinformation, issuing rapid clarifications and official myth-busting updates to preserve public confidence.

- Media Management: lead media relations, issue press releases, organize briefings, and prepare speeches, advisories, and official statements.

4.Lead in digital engagement, content creation & inclusion:

- Digital Platforms: manage NDRMO’s official website, social media, and digital channels with accurate, timely, and engaging content.

- Accessible Content Development: produce diverse content (infographics, short videos, podcasts, newsletters) ensuring products are culturally appropriate, multilingual, and fully accessible to persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups.

5.Gauge community feedback, and support M&E & knowledge management:

- Feedback Loops: establish and manage community feedback mechanisms (including post-event evaluations) to measure public trust, warning comprehension, and information reach.

- Analytics & Performance Reporting: monitor media analytics, track campaign effectiveness, and prepare periodic performance reports with actionable recommendations for continuous improvement.

- Documentation & Donor Visibility: oversee photography, videography, and documentation for key events, ensuring full compliance with donor visibility and reporting requirements (including GCF).

6.Manage flagship campaigns and initiatives:

The incumbent will directly drive and manage the following core campaigns:

- “Know Your Risk Fiji” Campaign: a year-round, multi-media national awareness initiative promoting disaster risk reduction across traditional and digital platforms.

- Monthly Hazard Awareness Calendar: targeted seasonal campaigns aligned with Fiji's primary hazards (cyclones, flooding, drought, tsunamis, and fire).

- Disaster Ready Fiji Schools Initiative: tailored communication packages, educational toolkits, and interactive preparedness activities for primary and secondary schools.

- Community Champions Programme: training and equipping community leaders, faith-based organizations, women's clubs, and youth ambassadors to amplify life-saving preparedness messages.

- Rapid Myth-Busting & Rumour Management Unit: an active monitoring mechanism to identify public confusion during disasters and publish instant, verified clarifications.

- Multi-Platform Public Warning Framework: operational coordination with telecoms, media houses, and local networks to guarantee automated, seamless alert delivery through the CAP platform.

7.The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Demonstrate focus on achieving quality results and impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Look beyond conventional approaches and established methods

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Actively pursue opportunities for learning and self-development professionally and personally

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Be flexible in handling change, and adopt new ideas, approaches and ways of working

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Pursue everything with motivation and drive

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Act in a way that demonstrates empathy and emotional intelligence, showing consideration for the needs and feelings of others

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Treat all individuals with respect, consider ethical implications and respond sensitively to all differences among people

Cross-Functional & Technical Compentencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Strategic Thinking : Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Business Management

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Digital

- Social Media : Knowledge of social media and ability to advise the use of social media for development outcomes.

External Relations & Advocacy - General (across the functions)

- Public Relations : Ability to build and maintain an overall positive public image for the organisation, its mandate and its brand, while ensuring that individual campaigns and other communications and advocacy initiatives are supported in reaching the public.

- Digital Literacy: Ability to apply terms and concepts from digital communications in daily work.

- Multimedia writing/editing: Ability to create and/or edit written content for multimedia.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education is required, OR

- A University Degree (Bachelor’s degree) in communications, journalism, public relations, or another related discipline would be given due consideration but not a requirement

Experience:

Minimum of 5 years (with high school diploma) or 2 years (with bachelor’s degree) of demonstrated experience in strategic communications, media relations, and public awareness campaigns is required.

Required Skills

Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Skills

- Demonstrated experience in strategic communications, public awareness campaigns, and public relations within disaster risk management, climate change, or development programs.

- Proven excellence in professional writing, editing, and content creation for diverse platforms, including articles, social media campaigns, newsletters, blogs, press releases, and public multimedia materials.

- Hands-on experience in supporting public safety messaging, emergency communications, or multi-hazard early warning dissemination channels.

- Proven Familiarity with Fiji’s Disaster Risk Management Framework, the National Disaster Management Act 2024, the Fiji National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018–2030, and the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative.

- Demonstrated ability in translating complex technical information (such as Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems and Common Alerting Protocols) into accessible, clear public outreach materials.

Language

- Fluency in English is a requirement.

- Working knowledge of the local languages Fiji Hindi or iTaukei is desirable.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

OFFICE/UNIT/PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with Governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

The 2030 Agenda for SDGs and the pledge to leave no one behind reflect the interconnectedness of health and sustainable development, including widening economic and social inequalities, the climate crisis, rapid urbanization, the continuing burden of HIV and other infectious diseases (e.g., malaria, tuberculosis), the growing burden of non-communicable diseases and the emergence of health threats. The scope and scale of delivering health and well-being for all demands innovative partnerships and financing. As affirmed in the Political Declaration of the 2019 High-Level Meeting on Universal Health Coverage (UHC), the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (Global Fund), the Vaccine Alliance (Gavi) and others are critical partners for delivering on the health-related goals of the 2030 Agenda. Stronger Collaboration, Better Health: Global Action Plan for Healthy Lives and Well-being for All outlines how a dozen multilateral health, development and humanitarian agencies, including UNDP, the Global Fund, Gavi and others will collaborate to be more efficient and effective in supporting countries to deliver UHC and achieve the health-related SDG targets.

UNDP’s partnership with the Global Fund makes a vital contribution to UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the SDGs and the pledge to leave no one behind.

As a long-standing partner of the Global Fund, UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance to Global Fund grants in 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of the integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach in supporting countries with significant national capacity constraints to manage large-scale health programmes. By providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including financial management, health information systems, procurement and supply chain management, UNDP is able to deliver results whilst sustainably transitioning to national entities. UNDP’s track record as interim PR over the last 20 years and capacity to deliver in challenging operating environments has been critical for strengthening its positioning as a health implementation support partner.

As a trusted, long-term partner of the Global Fund, UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including financial management, health information systems, procurement and supply chain management. Within the Prosperity & Well-being Hub, the Health Funds and Systems team (HFST) is a dedicated team providing support to UNDP Country Offices implementing health and development programmes.

UNDP has been appointed as the non-governmental Principal Recipient (PR) by the CCM (Country Coordination Mechanism) to implement the Global Fund GC8 Malaria grant, with the main objective of eliminating malaria and strengthening health systems in Guinea-Bissau.

To provide strategic planning, programmatic and operational management and oversight to the Global Fund portfolio to achieve the defined programme goals, targets and effective delivery, a dedicated Health Team has been established within UNDP country office in Bissau.

Within this context, the Finance Analyst leads the finance unit within the health team and is responsible for leading high-quality financial management, grant budgeting, expenditure monitoring, financial reporting, cash management, Sub-Recipient financial oversight, audit preparedness and fiduciary risk control. The role ensures that the finance function provides timely, accurate and strategic support to programme delivery while maintaining robust segregation of duties, compliance with UNDP and Global Fund requirements, sound internal controls and strong fiduciary safeguards across all levels of implementation in Guinea-Bissau.

SCOPE OF WORK

Lead strategic financial management, planning and budget control for the Global Fund Grant managed by UNDP.

- Lead preparation, review and monitoring of annual and quarterly budgets, workplans, cash forecasts and financial plans for UNDP, Sub-Recipients and programme delivery partners.

- Provide strategic financial analysis to programme management, including budget variances, absorption rates, commitments, burn rates, pipeline analysis and funding gaps affecting malaria activities in Guinea-Bissau.

- Ensure that all financial planning and budget revisions are aligned with approved Global Fund budgets, grant conditions, UNDP regulations and programme priorities for malaria prevention, diagnosis, treatment and supply chain support.

- Comply with all UNDP and donor financial reporting requirements, including Progress Updates to the Global Fund.

Ensure robust financial operations, accounting, reporting and cash management.

- Oversee accounting, payment processing, financial records, reconciliations and transaction quality assurance for the Global Fund grant, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timeliness.

- Lead preparation and quality review of financial reports, expenditure statements, supporting schedules and donor reporting inputs required by UNDP management and the Global Fund.

- Monitor cash flow, advances, liquidations, bank balances and payment schedules to ensure timely programme implementation and adequate liquidity for approved malaria activities.

- Ensure proper use of UNDP corporate systems, financial coding, document retention and audit trails for all grant-funded transactions.

Provide finance management and programme finance support for the Global Fund Grant.

- Perform and quality assure typical UNDP Quantum finance transactions, including review of requisitions, purchase orders, receipts, supplier invoices, payment requests, journal vouchers, budget checks, project chart of accounts, cost-recovery entries and supporting documentation for grant-funded activities.

- Monitor Quantum project budgets, expenditures, commitments, pre-encumbrances, budget availability, donor fund utilization and financial dashboards to support timely decision-making, accurate reporting and resolution of exceptions affecting the Global Fund grant.

- Coordinate closely with the Country Office finance team on Quantum workflows, payment processing, bank reconciliations, cash management, vendor management, month-end and year-end closure, financial controls, audit trails and compliance with UNDP financial rules and delegation of authority.

- Provide programme finance support to the Global Fund Programme by linking financial analysis with programme delivery, including activity-level budget monitoring, expenditure forecasting, variance analysis, liquidation follow-up, Sub-Recipient financial tracking and alignment of financial information with programmatic results, grant performance indicators and implementation priorities.

Ensure fiduciary risk management, internal controls and Sub-Recipient financial oversight.

- Ensure implementation of fiduciary controls, financial risk assessments, spot checks, financial verifications and follow-up actions for Sub-Recipients involved in Global Fund grant programme delivery.

- Develop and monitor finance-related risk mitigation measures that reflect Guinea-Bissau’s operating context, including risks related to cash handling, advances, procurement payments, supply chain expenditures and partner financial capacity.

- Provide technical guidance to Sub-Recipients to strengthen budgeting, expenditure documentation, liquidation of advances, segregation of duties, asset controls and compliance with UNDP and Global Fund requirements.

- Develop and di

Coordinate audits, assurance activities, compliance follow-up and management action plans.

- Coordinate preparation for internal and external audits, Local Fund Agent reviews, assurance visits and financial monitoring missions related to the Global Fund grant.

- Ensure timely follow-up of audit findings, management letters, spot check recommendations and assurance observations, ensuring implementation of corrective actions by UNDP teams and Sub-Recipients.

- Maintain a strong compliance culture by advising programme and operations colleagues on financial rules, donor conditions, eligible expenditures and documentation standards.

Manage the finance team, strengthen partner capacity and support knowledge transfer.

- Supervise, guide and quality assure the work of finance personnel supporting the Global Fund grant, promoting clear roles, effective workload management and adherence to internal control standards.

- Build the capacity of finance staff, programme colleagues and Sub-Recipient teams through coaching, training, practical guidance and dissemination of tools, templates and good practices.

- Engage with UNDP management, programme teams, operations units, national counterparts, Global Fund stakeholders, auditors, suppliers and service providers on finance-related matters requiring coordination and informed decision-making.

Perform other duties within the incumbent’s functional profile as assigned and deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Global Fund Grant, UNDP Guinea-Bissau and the Organization.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENT

The Finance Analyst reports to the Programme Manager of the Health team.

The incumbent leads the Finance Unit and supervises two Finance Associates.

S/he heads the project finance function and works in close collaboration with the Country Office finance team, programme, procurement, supply chain and operations colleagues, national counterparts, Sub-Recipients, Global Fund stakeholders, auditors and relevant service providers. The role ensures effective coordination between project-level programme finance requirements and Country Office financial management, Quantum workflows, corporate compliance, internal controls and financial reporting processes.

COMPETENCIES

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Finance - Accounting (General): Knowledge of accounting concepts, principles, frameworks, standards, regulations, policies and trends, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations.

Finance - Financial risk management: Ensures financial resilience through proactive assessment of risk, implementation of controls and taking mitigating action. Understands risk and reward in relation to collaborative and commercial projects. Ensures a culture of positive risk management.

Finance - Budget management: Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets.

Finance - Banking and cash management: Ability to collect, handle, and manage cash, which involves assessing market liquidity, cash flow, and Investments.

Business Management - Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Development - Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to Apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS OF THE SUCCESSFUL IPSA

Min. Education requirements

A professional accounting qualification from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy, and/or Advanced (Master’s) University Degree in Finance and/or Accounting is required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Candidates with professional accounting qualifications from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.

Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance must complete the Finance Training and Certification Programme (FTCP), if recruited.

Candidates satisfying the two above criteria are exempted from undertaking the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT).

Candidates with MBA or master's in finance with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

Min. years of relevant work experience

Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in providing financial management services, and/or managing staff and operational systems is required.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the UN’s global development network, an organization advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, working with national counterparts on solutions to global and national development challenges. In Bhutan, over the last 50 years, UNDP has been supporting the Royal Government to attain its national priorities. In 2024, UNDP started implementation of the Country Programme Document 2024-2028, aligning to the country’s 13th Five Year Plan (13th FYP).

In 2023, Bhutan graduated from the UN list of Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Over the past decades, the country has made remarkable progress in reducing income and multidimensional poverty, aligned with its commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Despite the impressive progress, the country is grappling with critical socio-economic challenges such as large-scale emigration of the productive and skilled labor force, youth unemployment, declining fertility rate, increasing trade deficit, and shrinking fiscal space. These challenges take place amidst a slow post-pandemic economic recovery and against the broader backdrop of structural challenges, such as limited economic diversification, a still-nascent private sector, absence of robust regulatory and institutional framework.

Bhutan’s 13th FYP (2024-2029) sets out the ambitious target of doubling the size of the country’s economy within the next five years and then doubling it again over the subsequent five years, reaching USD 10 billion by 2034, a target year that Bhutan plans to reach the high-income status. Recognizing the challenges and potential opportunities in Bhutan’s 21st-century economy, the Royal Government of Bhutan aims to accelerate and foster a robust economic recovery and growth. It is in this context that the Royal Government of Bhutan requested UNDP’s policy advisory assistance to support the Prime Minister’s Office in a high-level consultation and the subsequent development of a development roadmap for the realization for the government’s development vision as outlined above.

In June 2025, the Royal Government endorsed the Bhutan 21st Century Economic Roadmap, which sets the ambitious target of growing Bhutan’s economy tenfold (10X) by 2050 or earlier and transforming the country into a high-income, inclusive and sustainable economy. Recognising that achieving this 10X ambition requires a fundamentally different delivery architecture — one centred on performance, execution and accountability — the Royal Government established a dedicated Delivery Unit (DU) under the Prime Minister’s Office, anchored within the Office of the Cabinet Affairs and Strategic Coordination (OCASC), to drive the implementation of the 21st Century Economic Roadmap and the 13th Five Year Plan.

The Delivery Unit forms part of a wider 10X Implementation Governance Structure that comprises a National Steering Committee (NSC) chaired by the Hon’ble Prime Minister. The DU will serve as the secretariat to the NSC and report directly to the Hon’ble Prime Minister. It will be composed of a multidisciplinary team with expertise in planning, economic and financial analysis, project and performance management, data analytics, investment facilitation and public–private partnerships.

The Delivery Unit’s mandate spans the full delivery cycle: (i) designing and formulating detailed sectoral roadmaps with defined interventions, milestones, KPIs and implementation pathways in close coordination with lead agencies; (ii) developing investment frameworks and financing strategies, structuring bankable projects, and engaging investors and development partners in coordination with the Economic Development Board (EDB); (iii) facilitating and negotiating public–private partnerships and coordinating implementation across ministries and agencies; (iv) rigorously monitoring progress through dashboards, field reviews and structured delivery assessments, and providing regular updates to the NSC and the Hon’ble Prime Minister; and (v) conducting annual evaluations of agencies implementing projects under the 21st Century Economic Roadmap. In doing so, the DU will institutionalize the missing link between strategic ambition and on-the-ground delivery, embedding a culture of performance, foresight and accountability across government and accelerating Bhutan’s journey towards high-income status by 2034.

To support this initiative, UNDP seeks to recruit a Delivery and Performance Specialist to be embedded within the Delivery Unit. The Delivery and Performance Specialist will serve as the core engine of the Delivery Unit’s performance management and analytical functions, translating the 10X ambition into measurable KPIs, real-time dashboards and structured delivery routines that enable evidence-based decision-making by the National Steering Committee.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Director General, Office of the Cabinet Affairs and Strategic Coordination and Director, Office of the Prime Minister, and supervision of the Programme Analyst, Governance and Advocacy at UNDP CO, the Delivery and Performance Specialist will lead the design, operation and continuous improvement of the Delivery Unit’s performance management system, data analytics and dashboards for priority projects identified in the Bhutan 21st Century Economic Roadmap and other strategies and projects which are priority for the Delivery Unit. The Delivery and Performance Specialist will also support the Delivery Unit’s work in tracking implementation progress, surfacing bottlenecks, and equipping the National Steering Committee, Technical Steering Committees and lead agencies with the data, evidence and insights required to course-correct in real time.

Design and operationalize the Delivery Unit’s performance management framework

- Design and operationalize the Delivery Unit’s performance management framework, including KPIs, milestones, trajectories and delivery scorecards for priority projects under the 21st Century Economic Roadmap.

- Support the development of sectoral 10X project blueprints and contribute performance-management inputs to detailed sectoral roadmaps, KPIs and delivery plans.

- Work closely with the Bhutan Innovation Lab (BIL) to support the transition of Entry Point Project (EPP) blueprints into implementation, translating strategic recommendations, delivery pathways, milestones and KPIs developed by BIL into operational delivery plans, performance monitoring frameworks and implementation tracking mechanisms.

Develop and maintain dashboards, data pipelines and analytical tools

- Build and maintain live dashboards and visualization tools, including Power BI, Tableau or other relevant platforms, to track progress of 10X priority projects, with regular reporting to the National Steering Committee, Technical Steering Committees and the Hon’ble Prime Minister.

- Establish data pipelines and reporting protocols with line ministries, agencies and lead implementers to ensure timely, accurate and reliable data flow into the Delivery Unit.

- Conduct data analysis and diagnostics to identify implementation bottlenecks, delivery risks and early warning signals, and propose evidence-based course corrections.

Support structured delivery routines, reporting and evaluation

- Organise and facilitate structured delivery routines, including stock takes, problem-solving sessions and monthly performance reviews between the Delivery Unit, lead agencies and the Hon’ble Prime Minister, and document agreed actions and follow-ups.

- Support the annual evaluation of agencies implementing projects under the 21st Century Economic Roadmap, and contribute to the preparation of progress reports, briefing notes and presentations for the National Steering Committee and the Hon’ble Prime Minister.

- Contribute to the design and facilitation of 10X Labs and stakeholder clinics, providing data-analytics inputs to detailed sectoral roadmaps, KPIs and delivery plans.

Ensure gender-responsive analysis and programming

- Ensure the systematic integration of gender perspectives into policy analysis, recommendations, and programming, informed by sound gender analysis that incorporates sex-disaggregated data and addresses differentiated needs, priorities, and impacts across diverse groups.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic areas.

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities. Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

- Ensure project reports capture results, lessons learned and good practices for possible wider application.

Background

The Philippines' recent transition to upper-middle-income status has increased the importance of aligning economic growth with sustainability, digital transformation, and human rights accountability. As sectors such as mining, renewable energy, agribusiness, tourism, infrastructure, and digital platforms expand, governance challenges related to community grievances, land and resource disputes, labor rights, environmental impacts, and stakeholder participation persist, often disproportionately affecting women and marginalized groups.

To address these challenges, the Philippines initiated work on a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights (NAP-BHR), led by the Presidential Human Rights Committee Secretariat (PHRCS). While several ASEAN countries have already institutionalized their NAPs, the Philippines remains in the development stage. Recent efforts have accelerated under the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan 2024-2028, including the establishment of a multi-agency technical working group to develop a NAP-BHR focused on responsible business conduct, Indigenous Peoples' rights, and ancestral domains.

The FAIR BHR Project seeks to strengthen Business and Human Rights (BHR) governance by promoting more integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approaches that connect sustainability, human rights, accountability, conflict sensitivity, and stakeholder engagement. The project will support the Philippine government in building evidence, raising awareness, strengthening coordination, and fostering inclusive dialogue to inform BHR reforms.

The initiative will also promote stronger collaboration among UN agencies, leveraging complementary expertise and positioning UNDP as a strategic convener. As an initial pilot, the project will generate evidence and lessons to inform longer-term programming and the development of a comprehensive Project Document supporting the institutionalization of BHR in the Philippines.
